body.title: Fooled by a Generation
body.body:
>

> You can't save your way to wealth.

There are many reasons for this and I think it is pretty obvious to most readers why this is the case, so we needn't delve into it now. Instead, I will mention a conversation I was having over lunch with a friend, who heads up the ICT organisation for a very large manufacturing company. We were talking about various things, but AI agents came up and it is obviously an area he knows quite well. Yet, as we were talking he hadn't fully realised the implications of what they are being used for, because what everyone is trying to do with them, *is save.* 

> We are fooled by the term \

.

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23y8733p751VmHxtY9YLfLEVQpLTApqwL5spkjMLPRuHVjBmZUJmQ9fiXMWyJahYsSYkr.png)


---

Of course, the lowest hanging fruit in terms of increasing profits is to reduce costs, but ultimately, it is going to get to a point where two situations are met. One is that there is a floor on savings, which means that at some point, it is no longer possible to save any more, or the law of diminishing returns sets in and the cost of saving more is higher than the gain of the saving. But the other point is that while savings can be made, the potential to generate revenue can also be lost. For a very obvious example, a company can save a huge amount by firing all of their salespeople, but then their sales grind to a halt also. 

We were actually talking mostly about the Finnish government and how they keep making cuts in the budget. While most people see this as them trying to plug a sinking boat, I see it more as a way to make people accustomed to having more and more taken away from them, because there is no way that the government can ever save enough to make a significant difference and be able to return to growth, because *they aren't investing in anything that has growth potential.*

It is the same with the way that most companies are looking to use AI, as while it will create efficiency savings pretty easily, it doesn't mean that it is going to increase revenue. And that means that eventually, the company is salary-capped and without investment into new growth streams, is likely to lose any competitive advantage it might have anyway. 

Many people I have talked to who use AI in their work argue that it has made them better at their job, which from an outcome perspective can be true, but not necessarily from a skill perspective. What most deem as \

is when they can do what they were doing earlier more efficiently, where for instance what took them two hours now takes them one. The problem with this is that while their job efficiency increases, their own skill levels remain stagnant and the more efficiencies they find, the more stagnant the person becomes and eventually, they will be relegated to the jobless queue also. 

And as I explained to my friend, operational efficiency doesn't necessarily mean better outcomes. For instance, he uses Copilot to generate reports and also summarise the reports he needs to understand. But what he is summarising are the generated reports that other people have created, based on other AI summaries. Essentially, AIs are talking to each other. But more than that, they are deciding what information is relevant and making *business decisions* based on their evaluations. Some might be better, some might be worse than human suggestions, but to the inexperienced, it has to be taken as gospel. And while someone like my friend has a broad range and deep experience and knowledge to look at results with a discerning eye, most people and especially the young who have only dealt through AI filters, will have to take it at face value, and act on it. 

> What is really operating the business? 

The more we use an AI to shortcut our own skills, the *less experience* we have, and that means that even if we are in a role for some years, we can actually know very little, because we are reliant on the service provided by the AI. And when those AI LLMs are all pulling data from the same sources, it means that there is a reduction in the pool of \

and what they are suggesting across the board doesn't bring competitive advantage to any company, because all have the same information. Many people don't seem to yet understand the implications of this. For instance a lot of sales people I have worked with love how easy it is to get all the information on a prospect now and what kind of time saving it gives them and advantage with the customer. What they have apparently failed to recognise is that all of their competitors have likely run the same searches and have very similar information, so there is no advantage. And perhaps this is near where I will leave this seemingly ongoing conversation I am having with mostly myself. When there is no advantage in the information, the advantage comes down to what you do with it. If you aren't growing your methods and skills with how to use information to generate growth, there is actually a retraction. In the same way that someone can say they don't have the time to exercise, so they buy gadgets to vacuum the floor and do the dishes, and eat takeout so they don't have to spend time cooking, but with the free time they now have, *they do nothing.* AI efficiencies are freeing up people hours but instead of investing that time into growth generation activities and skill development, companies are instead getting rid of people. If they can save one hour a day in a role, it means they only need seven people where before they had eight. But, what companies should be doing is recognising that in order to have a competitive advantage, they need to grow, not just be efficient. That means they have to identify growth potential and *develop it* which generally takes time and new learning. Instead of getting rid of people to save money, they should be finding ways for at least some of those same people to develop new products and services. But the thing is, like governments have become, business is incredibly short-sighted, panicking and knee-jerking on quarterly sales figures, making cuts to increase profit margins, and forgetting that for a business to maintain success, *it has to build.* For now, savings might be enough for companies, but at some point, the information pool becomes so homogenous, and the savings potential so thin, that it isn't going to be enough to generate the profit returns that investors expect. And by that time, the operating model will be so lean, and the people knowledge and skill base so poor, that there will be nothing left to turn the ship around. And they will be swallowed up by a larger animal, until the economy collapses completely under the weight of capitalistic cannibalism. > But hey, you know what you are doing. Save a bit more valuable time and energy. body.title: Hotel Grand Aston La Habana/Grand Aston Havana Hotel (Esp-Eng)\n\n
body.body:
> Hola, mis amigos de worldmappin. Que placer saludarlos una vez más. Hoy sigo mostrándoles las maravillas de La Habana. Si de diseños futuristas hablamos, el sitio que les traigo hoy, está entre los primeros de Cuba. Con menos de cinco años de creado y situado frente al mundialmente conocido Malecón habanero, este majestuoso hotel tiene su entrada por la calle 1ra del Vedado. Cuenta con un diseño elegante que representa el nuevo estilo de vida urbano caribeño. El hotel Grand Aston La Habana es un flamante cinco estrellas que se ha convertido en uno de los alojamientos más modernos y comentados de la capital cubana. >Hello, my friends from worldmappin. What a pleasure to greet you once again. Today I continue showing you the wonders of Havana. > >When it comes to futuristic designs, the place I'm bringing you today ranks among the top in Cuba. Created less than five years ago and located right in front of the world-famous Malecón in Havana, this majestic hotel has its entrance on 1st Street in Vedado. It features an elegant design that represents the new Caribbean urban lifestyle. The Grand Aston Havana Hotel is a brand-new five-star hotel that has become one of the most modern and talked-about accommodations in the Cuban capital.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUMuNfqaUDMTCqwTPbNjefc48fv9KEcMBJELbQc2zrR24/1776805157364.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc9q2EuurcoFXffK7Aph1JSqgwHjBNagsmqg1gnbk5RvX/1776805412210.jpg)

> Ubicado en el exclusivo barrio del Vedado, el Grand Aston se levanta imponente con sus cristales y sus dos torres de 600 habitaciones. No solo es uno de los hoteles más nuevos de La Habana, sino que también es el único de la ciudad que posse una sucursal bancaria en su interior. Al entrar, te das cuenta de que su diseño es una fusión muy chula entre el glamour de La Habana de los años 30 y la elegancia asiática, lo que le da un aire fresco y sofisticado. Las habitaciones son amplias, luminosas y están equipadas con todas las comodidades modernas. >Located in the exclusive Vedado neighborhood, the Grand Aston stands imposingly with its glass windows and two towers housing 600 rooms. Not only is it one of the newest hotels in Havana, but it's also the only hotel in the city that has a bank branch inside. Upon entering, you realize its design is a very cool fusion between the glamour of 1930s Havana and Asian elegance, giving it a fresh and sophisticated feel. The rooms are spacious, bright, and equipped with all modern comforts.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTKk9sTUV8RA4diQnnjiNctuctfh4ZeSbzbz18jZM8UDe/1776805412346.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfCPa4sX78wG2DCFZzxHFJtBjPkPagFsKKGoUVssZY6LK/1776805412676.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeHkYopdZw6J95B58D27nu3Wz54b6owC5Qa9qiSNjPbhp/1776805461652.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTaqeYvKQ8Y2JG4HK3PmtnnbDXXBp2HB6YLRma4CDnk7h/1776805461838.jpg)

> Si algo hace especial a este hotel, son sus zonas comunes, el Spa, las cafeterías y restaurantes. Y la joya de la corona es, sin dudas, la piscina. Con sus 56 metros de largo, es una de las más grandes de la capital. Rodeada de cristales, está ubicada en una terraza que ofrece unas vistas de ensueño del mar Caribe. >What makes this hotel special are its common areas, the Spa, the coffee shops, and restaurants. And the crown jewel is, without a doubt, the swimming pool. At 56 meters long, it's one of the largest in the capital. Surrounded by glass, it sits on a terrace offering dreamlike views of the Caribbean Sea.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeW9NCzhHLRCZpXMqRw77yAg3AQ6jXcSJzLZhuvyR271V/1776805502202.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQqh9bJMSsV9dn4dYVVNarFqn8t1ggDJQynCuRQStZ549/1776805502375.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcyhrwqQKwsjE5zBZXW7vbMQoLji3gLqUWtPWga23nfJQ/1776805502533.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXdWT2pBno7xt59hz9amJxeWGj9DMVwT7dM7PTY2TC1HC/1776805502683.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbfnsdumSsZTzFHLogNxwjEsnp5AHcd2SKn15XAAozPbt/1776805502853.jpg)

> Como dato curioso, supe que es el único hotel en la ciudad con un gimnasio abierto las 24 horas, eso por si te da por hacer ejercicios de madrugada. Por lo que pude ver, el servicio, en general, es excelente. El personal es descrito como atento, servicial y siempre dispuesto a ayudar. La ubicación es ideal para recorrer la ciudad, y el ambiente en la piscina o en sus restaurantes es perfecto para relajarse y disfrutar de una buena comida o una copa viendo el atardecer. En plataformas como TripAdvisor tiene una puntuación altísima, rozando el 5 sobre 5 en categorías como ubicación y limpieza. >As a fun fact, I learned it's the only hotel in the city with a 24-hour gym, just in case you feel like working out in the early morning. From what I could see, the service overall is excellent. The staff is described as attentive, helpful, and always willing to assist. The location is ideal for exploring the city, and the atmosphere by the pool or in its restaurants is perfect for relaxing and enjoying a good meal or a drink while watching the sunset. On platforms like TripAdvisor, it has a very high rating, close to 5 out of 5 in categories like location and cleanliness.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUL3JSx2gRqba3yGaVX2YnchsHZWESte1jQYyAW9PT3EX/1776805572637.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaqExAeRQxMUF9XPRcvMLHmeArWCk3wNWMRH3tXunP1rG/1776805572677.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSzKZRgcEgJUKxcVGkUEMhXZt7CorHLS5G8BNjWt5U5NW/1776805572719.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfZQ8qfZ8vBSccAStRBEJNixPBNuTQqGRKQ41gk2mbgk5/1776805572904.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcRPyKw5nrP3NgPgbbk9qgsCaZggL8eSL2R2Fg5ovGrsZ/1776805573076.jpg)

> Eso sí, como todo sitio nuevo, hay opiniones para todos los gustos. También hay quien dice que está un poco alejado del centro histórico, aunque otris coinciden y yo también, en que la tranquilidad y las vistas del Malecón lo compensan con creces. Si buscas un hotel en La Habana que combine lujo moderno, comodidades de primer nivel y una ubicación privilegiada frente al mar, el Grand Aston La Habana es una opción segura. Es el sitio perfecto para alojarse si quieres disfrutar de lo nuevo que ofrece la ciudad sin renunciar al confort. Una muy buena opción para tus próximas vacaciones si es que la economía te alcanza, porque el lujo y el glamour tienen su precio. >Of course, as with any new place, opinions vary. Some say it's a bit far from the historic center, though others – and I agree – believe the tranquility and views of the Malecón more than make up for it. If you're looking for a hotel in Havana that combines modern luxury, top-notch amenities, and a privileged oceanfront location, the Grand Aston Havana is a safe bet. It's the perfect place to stay if you want to enjoy what's new in the city without giving up comfort. A very good option for your next vacation if your budget allows, because luxury and glamour come at a price.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU2LxvR3ghySknScj7xBQvLMzDg9A7a1XLsi2SZfbEqac/1776805608831.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdk8VfafAXG6VeZ6ngPuF58e4kUTePQEUjt7rJLcDxKdX/1776805609010.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQzeY62UqFoP8ThbVvtpNkPkqkT9fdfsbAc4aJSV3Y3v5/1776805609171.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmetEeftD6cand5Y6ezyC3Ao7W9pMjnCDjqwbkKaBo3tmo/1776805609315.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTqtP9s1YEgshcTir5FcnSdsFJDFNCdp6XuTCU1RD7LMW/1776805609496.jpg)

body.title: CONOCIENDO ESPAÑA: LA BELLA CÓRDOBA: La ciudad de las tres culturas // DISCOVERING SPAIN: BEAUTIFUL CÓRDOBA: The City of Three Cultures  (Spanish-English)
body.body:
![Conociendo España.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23z7NNu4dpoWP2a7NVmFt635np5et9WgC692DRvihrr39wXsG5k25exPxqimE6HjcK2di.png)
Banner diseñado por mí en canva.com Las fotos pertenecen a mi álbum de fotos personal fueron tomadas con la cámara de mi teléfono móvil
Banner designed by me on canva.com Pictures are from my personal photo album It were taked with my cell phone camera

#
CONOCIENDO ESPAÑA: LA BELLA CÓRDOBA: La ciudad de las tres culturas

*

>Saludos, amigos lectores, con este artículo voy a continuar mi recorrido por ciudades y lugares de España, país donde resido en la actualidad. Mi país de origen es Venezuela, país ubicado al norte de América del Sur. Con anterioridad he publicado varios artículos sobre ciudades españolas que he visitado. Dediqué varios artículos de mi blog a Barcelona, Nerja, Frigiliana, Granada, Málaga, Salobreña, Sevilla. Acompáñenme hoy a visitar La bella ciudad andaluza de CÓRDOBA, ubicada a orillas del río Guadalquivir y al pie de la Sierra Morena. Una de las ciudades más bonitas e impresionantes de España.*
![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
*

> La mayoría de las ciudades importantes de Europa y de España rivalizan por su historia, por su arquitectura, por los rincones singulares que poseen. Pero la ciudad que reseñaré, que pude visitar a comienzos de este año, realmente tiene una historia extraordinaria, por lo que me alegra haberla podido visitar. Cuando la recorres vas caminando en el tiempo, sientes una suerte de desdoblamiento, del presente, lo que ves, hacia el pasado, qué hechos históricos determinaron la construcción de la ciudad. Nosotros hicimos dos free tours y un tour específico dentro de la Mezquita-Catedral, sin duda su monumento histórico más importante. La bella Córdoba tiene muchos espacios llenos de encanto. *
![Yo en el jardín de entrada de la Mezquita de Córdoba.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/243qF9LwLa2tULmYaY9Eq6ajAJKE6GCk6EDAdh1jGA3MM25Yq3jddm5svBhYKSQe36AHv.jpg) Yo en el patio de los naranjos que precede la Mezquita-Catedral de Córdoba ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

> La historia de Córdoba se remonta al siglo II a.C. Fue fundada por los romanos en la época republicana. En aquel tiempo se convirtió en la capital de la Hispania Ulterior y fue una de las ciudades más prósperas y cultas del Imperio. Cuando la región fue invadida por los musulmanes en el siglo VIII de nuestra era, fue capital del Emirato de Córdoba, inicialmente, y en su época de mayor esplendor, se transformó en la capital del Califato de Córdoba. En el siglo X, fue una de las ciudades más importantes del mundo civilizado de la época. No sólo por su gran extensión y población, sino también porque en la ciudad se encontraron algunas de las mentes más brillantes del momento: matemáticos, científicos, médicos, artistas, filósofos. (Maimónides, Averroes, Fernando de Córdoba, Muhammad ibn Massarra, entre otros). En este primer artículo les hablaré sobre el Puente Romano, la Torre de la Calahorra y la Mezquita-Catedral. Acompáñame a visitarla.
##
El puente romano

>Es el puente más antiguo de la ciudad, une el barrio del Campo de la Verdad con el Barrio de la Catedral. Durante veinte siglos fue el único puente que unía las dos orillas de la ciudad, hasta que se construyó el puente San Rafael, a mediados del siglo XX. Es uno de los espacios de la ciudad que deben visitarse, por su importancia histórica. En la antigüedad este puente fue uno de los puntos importantes de entrada a la península ibérica desde el sur, porque permitió el cruce del río Guadalquivir sin tener que usar una embarcación. Aunque su nombre, por su antigüedad, es “Puente Romano”, en realidad ha sufrido diversos cambios y restauraciones a través del tiempo. En algún momento circularon por él vehículos, pero desde el 1 de mayo de 2004 se prohibió su paso y es sólo un puente peatonal, lo que permitirá su mejor conservación.

>Y allí estuvimos, pasamos el arco que da entrada al puente, caminamos sobre sus arcos de piedra y contemplamos un rato el Guadalquivir y la vegetación que cubre sus orillas. Entré a la Torre de la Calahorra, que cierra el puente (luego comentaré brevemente sobre ella). Volvimos al anochecer y pudimos disfrutar de una vista realmente hermosa. El puente está muy cerca de la Mezquita-Catedral, en la zona del centro histórico. Información sobre el Puente Romano en https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puente_romano_de_C%C3%B3rdoba

##
La Torre de la Calahorra

> La Torre de la Calahorra (en árabe: qala’at al-hurriya), que se encuentra al final del puente romano de Cordoba, fue construida como una fortaleza de origen islámico, cuya función era servir de entrada al puente y al mismo tiempo protegerlo. Cuando subes a la azotea, la parte más alta del edificio, tienes una vista muy amplia de kilómetros hacia todas las direcciones. Si algún enemigo se acercaba podían divisarlo desde la parte superior de la torre. A lo largo de los siglos ha tenido diversas funciones: fue prisión de nobles, centro educativo femenino (1863) y cuartel de la Guardia Civil. En 1952 el alcalde Antonio Cruz-Conde consiguió la cesión del edificio para el Ayuntamiento, y luego de ser restaurado abrió sus puertas al público en 1953 con una exposición conmemorativa por el V Centenario del nacimiento del Gran Capitán, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba (1453-1515), héroe legendario de la ciudad.

>En la actualidad, la Torre de la Calahorra es uno de los museos más importantes de Córdoba, y es único en el mundo en tanto es el más completo sobre la cultura al-Andalus. En las tres plantas que lo componen puedes ver expresiones de su arquitectura, música, ciencia. En aquel momento, entre los siglos IX Y XIII coexistieron en la ciudad las mentes más brillantes de las religiones cristiana, judía y musulmana. Puedes ver audiovisuales, ver maquetas de las grandes edificaciones de Granada (La Mezquita-Catedral de Córdoba, la Alhambra, la Medina Azahara).

>Así también, mientras visitas la Torre puedes escuchar a través de unos audífonos una explicación detallada de lo que encuentras en cada sala, la vida de grandes sabios del al-Andalus, puedes ver instrumentos musicales y escuchar audios de música. Es una visita extraordinaria. Las vistas al subir a lo alto de la Torre son espectaculares. Forma parte del centro histórico de Córdoba que fue declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la Unesco en 1994. Información sobre la Torre de la Calahorra en https://www.torrecalahorra.es/

La Mezquita-Catedral de Córdoba

### La Mezquita

> La gran joya arquitectónica de Córdoba es la Mezquita-Catedral. Un monumento único en España y en el mundo, por su monumentalidad y albergar dentro de sí, en un mismo edificio, una mezquita árabe y una catedral católica. Es el monumento histórico más impresionante que he visitado en España. Al entrar al edificio está el patio de los naranjos, un bonito jardín con árboles y fuentes y los pasillos laterales que conducen a la entrada del edificio. Cuando ya estás adentro te impresiona de una manera abrumadora una suerte de bosque de columnas que se pierden de vista, las cuales sostienen sus famosas dovelas (los arcos con franjas terracotas y blancas). Contando las diversas ampliaciones que ha tenido la Mezquita, son 924 columnas estructurales, y 467 decorativas. En total 1391 columnas. Al fondo de la nave principal está la “mihnab” (nicho que indica la alquibla, es decir, la dirección de la Kaaba en La Meca hacia donde debe dirigirse la oración musulmana). Ese nicho en tonos dorados es precioso. Te comparto algunas fotos.

### La Catedral cristiana

>Cuando la ciudad de Córdoba es reconquistada por el rey cristiano Fernando III de Castilla en 1236, no se destruyó el monumental edificio de la Mezquita construido durante el emirato y califato árabes, en los siglos en los cuales España fue ocupada por el Islam, pero se ordenó su consagración como edificio cristiano y fue convertida por el obispo Lope de Fitero en catedral de la diócesis de la ciudad. Pero no se hicieron cambios importantes en el edificio hasta tres siglos después, cuando se construyó la Capilla Mayor cristiana, que se hizo entre 1523 y 1607.

>Es entonces cuando se vuelve realmente un monumento único, al albergar dentro de sus espacios también los altares y naves cristianos. El ala cristiana del edificio también posee hermosos espacios y estatuas y es monumental, como toda catedral cristina lo es. Pero se encuentra dentro de la misma edificación. Desde que entras en la Mezquita puedes observar capillas laterales cristianas. Y al avanzar en el recorrido vi cristos crucificados, estatuas y los hermosos libros de Coro (cancioneros). Bellamente empastados en rojo. Al entrar en la catedral propiamente dicha encuentras tres espacios importantes: la Capilla Mayor, la impresionante sala del Coro tallada en madera de caoba y el Trascoro que precide una estatua de San Pedro. DISCOVERING SPAIN: BEAUTIFUL CÓRDOBA: The City of Three Cultures

*

> Greetings, dear readers. In this article, I’ll continue my tour of cities and places in Spain, the country where I currently live. I’m originally from Venezuela, a country located in northern South America. I’ve previously published several articles about Spanish cities I’ve visited. I’ve dedicated several blog posts to Barcelona, Nerja, Frigiliana, Granada, Málaga, Salobreña, and Seville. Join me today as we visit the beautiful Andalusian city of CÓRDOBA, located on the banks of the Guadalquivir River and at the foot of the Sierra Morena. It’s one of the most beautiful and impressive cities in Spain.*
![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
*

> Most major cities in Europe and Spain compete with one another in terms of their history, architecture, and unique spots. But the city I’m going to describe—which I had the chance to visit earlier this year—truly has an extraordinary history, which is why I’m so glad I was able to visit it. As you explore it, you feel as though you’re walking through time; you experience a sort of split between the present—what you see—and the past—the historical events that shaped the city’s development. We took two free tours and a special tour inside the Mosque-Cathedral, undoubtedly its most important historical monument. Beautiful Córdoba has many charming spots.*
![Yo en el jardín de entrada de la Mezquita de Córdoba.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/243qF9LwLa2tULmYaY9Eq6ajAJKE6GCk6EDAdh1jGA3MM25Yq3jddm5svBhYKSQe36AHv.jpg) It's me in the Courtyard of the Orange Trees in front of the Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

>The history of Córdoba dates back to the 2nd century B.C. It was founded by the Romans during the Republican era. At that time, it became the capital of Hispania Ulterior and was one of the most prosperous and cultured cities in the Empire. When the region was invaded by the Muslims in the 8th century CE, it was initially the capital of the Emirate of Córdoba, and during its period of greatest splendor, it became the capital of the Caliphate of Córdoba. In the 10th century, it was one of the most important cities in the civilized world of the time. Not only because of its vast size and population, but also because the city was home to some of the most brilliant minds of the era: mathematicians, scientists, doctors, artists, and philosophers (Maimonides, Averroes, Fernando de Córdoba, Muhammad ibn Massarra, among others). In this first article, I’ll tell you about the Roman Bridge, the Calahorra Tower, and the Mosque-Cathedral. Join me on a tour.
##
The Roman Bridge

> It is the oldest bridge in the city, connecting the Campo de la Verdad neighborhood with the Cathedral District. For twenty centuries, it was the only bridge linking the city’s two banks, until the San Rafael Bridge was built in the mid-20th century. It is one of the city’s must-see sites due to its historical significance. In ancient times, this bridge was one of the key entry points to the Iberian Peninsula from the south, as it allowed travelers to cross the Guadalquivir River without needing a boat. Although it is called the “Roman Bridge” because of its age, it has actually undergone various changes and restorations over time. At one time, vehicles used to cross it, but since May 1, 2004, vehicle traffic has been prohibited, and it is now exclusively a pedestrian bridge, which will allow for better preservation.

> And there we were: we passed through the archway leading to the bridge, walked across its stone arches, and spent a while admiring the Guadalquivir River and the vegetation lining its banks. I went inside the Calahorra Tower, which stands at the end of the bridge (I’ll say a few words about it later). We returned at dusk and were treated to a truly beautiful view. The bridge is very close to the Mosque-Cathedral, in the historic district. Information about the Roman Bridge at https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puente_romano_de_C%C3%B3rdoba
![Yo en puente romano con la Torrre de la Calahorra al fondo.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23r1o9SExXGUnweh1DsXgiseEmAaKGLsW9k49EpGukV3WmRqMgfcLFwiy639WsHjqd7p8.jpg) Me at the Roman Bridge in Córdoba, with the Calahorra Tower in the background ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
![puente romano desde la azotea de la Torre de la Calahorra.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23yd5eKsWzZjfRsnudnf8qJjHrpek26Qbe3bxJhQtYR24svr2GyGeajhNPEC62b3HGNWL.jpg) The Roman Bridge in Córdoba, as seen from the Calahorra Tower ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

![río Guadalquivir 2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/244A2kZ9mFgtdRcdeSMix98f5scQQKL6cZnzWhXsCRJu8pUb8MCnJ5RKxVSc1JrBNybiQ.jpg) The Guadalquivir River as seen from the Roman bridge ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
![Guadalquivir al atardecer.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23ycuYhEuqUh83aC19sBWhqW4cWL4ng1rdeivCTSsM2H6qchifPKAiuhbiK7myK7AyMpr.jpg) The Guadalquivir at dusk ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
##
Calahorra Tower

> The Calahorra Tower (in Arabic: qala’at al-hurriya), located at the end of the Roman Bridge in Córdoba, was built as an Islamic fortress designed to serve as the entrance to the bridge while also protecting it. When you climb to the rooftop, the highest point of the building, you are treated to a sweeping view stretching for miles in every direction. If any enemy approached, they could be spotted from the top of the tower. Over the centuries, it has served various purposes: it was a prison for nobles, a girls’ school (1863), and a Civil Guard barracks. In 1952, Mayor Antonio Cruz-Conde secured the transfer of the building to the City Council, and after being restored, it opened its doors to the public in 1953 with a commemorative exhibition marking the 500th anniversary of the birth of the Great Captain, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba (1453–1515), the city’s legendary hero.

> Today, the Calahorra Tower is one of the most important museums in Córdoba, and it is unique in the world as the most comprehensive museum dedicated to the culture of al-Andalus. Across its three floors, you can explore examples of its architecture, music, and science. At that time, between the 9th and 13th centuries, the city was home to the brightest minds of the Christian, Jewish, and Muslim faiths. You can watch audiovisual presentations and view models of the great buildings of Granada (the Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba, the Alhambra, and Medina Azahara).

> In addition, while visiting the tower, you can listen through headphones to a detailed explanation of what you’ll find in each room and learn about the lives of the great scholars of al-Andalus; you can also see musical instruments and listen to music recordings. It’s an extraordinary experience. The views from the top of the tower are spectacular. It is part of the historic center of Córdoba, which was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994. Information about the Calahorra Tower is available at https://www.torrecalahorra.es/
![torre de la Calahorra azotea.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/243zZtFHjen6rmGwawG3ePo5GLxuz1FfQTXYdgHNUL4KjXqbZemNvVFcEBHZX61J59HnX.jpg) Calahorra Tower: rooftop ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

body.title: Майбутнє в моєму тілі: Як бездротовий датчик тканин перевертає уявлення про хірургію
body.body: >Знаєте, іноді я дивлюся на свій смартфон і думаю: ми навчили цю коробочку впізнавати наше обличчя, платити за каву та навіть рахувати кроки, але коли справа доходить до найціннішого — нашого внутрішнього світу в буквальному сенсі — ми все ще покладаємося на старі методи. Нещодавно я натрапив на новину, яка змусила мене замислитися про те, наскільки близько ми підійшли до межі, де техніка та жива плоть стають одним цілим. Мова про новий бездротовий пристрій, який вміє розпізнавати стан тканин у реальному часі. І це не просто чергова іграшка для техно-гіків, це те, що завтра може врятувати життя комусь із нас.

>Коли я вперше прочитав про цей девайс, у мене перед очима постала картина з наукової фантастики. Уявіть собі крихітний сенсор, який не потребує батарейок чи довгих дротів, що стирчать із тіла. Він просто знаходиться там, де потрібен, і «спілкується» з лікарями через шкіру. Найбільше мене вразило те, як він розрізняє здорові тканини від пошкоджених. Це як мати внутрішнього охоронця, який подає сигнал тривоги ще до того, як проблема стане очевидною для ока хірурга.

Я часто думаю про те, як страшно проходити через складні операції. Найбільший ризик — це не сама маніпуляція, а те, що відбувається після. Чи приживеться тканина? Чи немає внутрішньої кровотечі, яку не помітили? Цей новий гаджет, працює за принципом «tissue-aware» — тобто він «усвідомлює» тканину навколо себе. Це звучить трохи моторошно, але водночас неймовірно заспокійливо. Це як різниця між тим, щоб йти в темній кімнаті навпомацки, і тим, щоб раптово увімкнути ліхтарик.

>Мене завжди дратувало, наскільки медицина іноді буває громіздкою. Всі ці апарати МРТ розміром з невелику кімнату, кілометри кабелів... А тут ми бачимо мініатюризацію в її найкращому прояві. Бездротова технологія дозволяє моніторити пацієнта без зайвого дискомфорту. Я намагаюся уявити, як це змінить відновлення після операцій. Людина може просто відпочивати, а лікарі на планшеті бачать повну картину того, що відбувається всередині шва чи органа. Це дає відчуття контролю, якого нам так бракує у критичні моменти життя.

>
Поглинуті передавачі та ретрансляційні станції співпрацюють для покращення чіткішого бездротового зв'язку з зовнішнім приймачем. Джерело: Осакський метрополітенський університет

>Що мене справді «зачепило» в цій історії, так це інтелект самого пристрою. Він не просто передає дані, він адаптується. Вчені пояснюють, що сенсор використовує особливі електромагнітні сигнали для аналізу щільності та вологості тканин. Для мене це виглядає як перехід від грубої механіки до тонкої психології тіла. Ми нарешті починаємо говорити з нашим організмом на одній мові — мові сигналів, які можна миттєво інтерпретувати.

>

_Системна модель імплантаційної комунікації з розподіленим променевим формуванням._ [Source](https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41598-026-36694-w/MediaObjects/41598_2026_36694_Fig2_HTML.png?as=webp)

>Звісно, як у скептика всередині мене виникають питання. А що, якщо сигнал перехоплять? Або якщо пристрій дасть збій? Але, дивлячись на темпи прогресу, я розумію, що ризик відсутності таких технологій набагато вищий, ніж ризик від їх використання. Я пам'ятаю часи, коли навіть пульсометр на руці здавався чимось неймовірним, а зараз ми обговорюємо імплантати, які стежать за загоєнням клітин. Це величезний крок у бік персоналізованої медицини, де лікують не «середньостатистичного пацієнта», а саме тебе, з твоїми унікальними біологічними показниками.

>Будемо відверті, ніхто не хоче опинитися на операційному столі. Але якщо вже так сталося, я б хотів, щоб за моїм станом стежив такий «розумний» помічник. Це дає надію на те, що помилок стане менше, а період реабілітації — коротшим. Ми стаємо свідками ери, де кордон між біологією та електронікою стирається заради однієї мети — людського виживання та комфорту.

На завершення хочу сказати, що подібні новини повертають мені віру в людський геній. Поки ми сперечаємося про дурні речі в соцмережах, десь у лабораторіях люди створюють майбутнє, яке буквально проникає під шкіру в кращому сенсі цього слова. Це нагадування про те, що ми — не просто набір органів, а складна система, яку ми нарешті вчимося розуміти по-справжньому.

>А як ви ставитеся до ідеї вживлення подібних датчиків? Чи вважаєте ви, що такий тотальний контроль над внутрішніми процесами — це порятунок, чи все ж таки ми занадто глибоко втручаємося в природу, створюючи з себе кіборгів? Мені було б цікаво почути ваші думки, бо межа між людиною і машиною стає все тоншою з кожним таким винаходом. Ви б довірили своє життя датчику розміром з зернятко?
>Детально ознайомитися із цією крутою розробкою можна за цим посиланням.
body.author: phdmed

body.body:

---

Original Song: I Remember What I AM
Singer-Songwriter-Producer: Shavon
A Sound Legion Production
#soundlegion #bonnielegion #shavon 

I went a little wild with this one, and honestly, I had a great time doing it 😄This one’s just meant to be a fun ride.
It fits the energy of the song, this kind of ancient awakening that rises up out of the lyrics, something I pulled from a really deep place inside myself. It’s definitely not historically accurate, and is a completely made up piece of my overspilling imagination. Timelines are all over the place… honestly, what time period is this even?
We start with ancient tribes and warriors… and somehow build into a full-on battle with giants, aliens, and Annunaki falling from the sky.
Come on… it’s fun.
I also did a live capture performance of this song if you want to check that out too.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CtCZKm_QejY

Lyrics

 “I Remember What I Am” 

I walked with a name I was given at birth
Carried it close like it measured my worth
Spoke in a voice that was shaped by the room
Echoed the world like a hollowed-out tune

There in the quiet beneath all the sound
Something was waiting, but not to be found
Not in the seeking, not reaching above
But in the breaking of what I once was

There is a pull I can’t deny
It moves through me, it doesn’t lie
No longer asking what is true
It’s rising up from somewhere new

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

I felt it stirring under my skin
Not from outside, but deep within
A widening space I could not contain
Not bound by loss, not shaped by pain

Every moment began to unfold
Not something new, but something old
A living current, silent and wide
Watching through me from the inside

There is no edge, there is no end
No place I stop, no place I bend
What I was taught begins to fall
It was never that small

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

At the first turning, I laid it down
All that I built to keep me bound
What I was holding slipped away
And still I stood, and still I stayed

At the second turning, time grew still
No past to chase, no future to fill
Only the breath, the space between
Where I end and all has been

At the final turning, nothing to hide
No shape to carry, no place to divide
What I was seeking was never apart
It was the rhythm inside of my heart

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

---

▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=soundlegion/2a55a0a5)

Spoke in a voice that was shaped by the room
Echoed the world like a hollowed-out tune

There in the quiet beneath all the sound
Something was waiting, but not to be found
Not in the seeking, not reaching above
But in the breaking of what I once was

There is a pull I can’t deny
It moves through me, it doesn’t lie
No longer asking what is true
It’s rising up from somewhere new

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

I felt it stirring under my skin
Not from outside, but deep within
A widening space I could not contain
Not bound by loss, not shaped by pain

Every moment began to unfold
Not something new, but something old
A living current, silent and wide
Watching through me from the inside

There is no edge, there is no end
No place I stop, no place I bend
What I was taught begins to fall
It was never that small

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

At the first turning, I laid it down
All that I built to keep me bound
What I was holding slipped away
And still I stood, and still I stayed

At the second turning, time grew still
No past to chase, no future to fill
Only the breath, the space between
Where I end and all has been

At the final turning, nothing to hide
No shape to carry, no place to divide
What I was seeking was never apart
It was the rhythm inside of my heart

I remember what I am
Not the body, not the plan
Not the story, not the name
Not the pieces I became

I remember what I am
I was never held by them
Now the veil is wearing thin
And I feel it moving in

body.title: Recipe: Delicious osso buco medallions in sauce - Receta: Deliciosos medallones de osobuco en salsa. 🍖🥦
body.body:
> Hello friends, how are you? It's a pleasure to greet you. Today I'm sharing a delicious recipe with you: osso buco medallions in sauce. >Hola amigos como estan? un gusto saludarles, hoy les comparto una rica receta, se trata de unos deliciosos medallones de osobuco en salsa.

![Picsart_26-04-21_18-09-05-986.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maricrochets/23uFVawXByjmGGbCgSxwMoYrDKMaif75eqrdZd6t4W6Ubnpr8i8R85yyg3rWUKfrXTHDm.jpg)

> 🍖 **Ingredients:** 2 oxtail medallions. 1 white onion. 2 sweet peppers. Scallions. 1/2 carrot. 2 garlic cloves. Salt and pepper. Red seasoning. Worcestershire sauce. Oil as needed. >🍖 **Ingredientes:** >2 medellones de osobuco. 1 cebolla blanca. 2 ajies dulces. Ramas de cebollin. 1/2 zanahoria. 2 dientes de ajo. Sal y pimienta. Aliño rojo. Salsa inglesa. Aceite el necesario.

![IMG_20260421_174917_632.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maricrochets/23xL9EK27HEZw86V2mDpnu19YPTWW3NsNE8oEEEHRvtn2BnaNuc8Kkkkc8rsMGLWoAQFg.jpg)

> 🍖 **Preparation:** I'll start by placing the medallions in a pan with water and simmering them in a covered pot until the meat is tender. I'll finely chop the vegetables and garlic and grate the carrot. Set aside. Once the meat is tender, add all the vegetables, salt, pepper, and Worcestershire sauce. Continue cooking over low heat until the liquid is absorbed and a thick sauce remains. I served these delicious medallions with white rice and fried plantains. Thanks for sharing, friends! Best regards. 🙏🏻🙏🏻🫂🫂 >🍖 **Preparacion:** >Comenzare colocamdo los medallones en un sarten con agua y poniendolos a cocer a fuego lento en una olla tapada hasta ablandar la carne. >Cortamos los vegetales y el ajo muy pequeños y rallamos la zanahoria, reservamos, al estar la carne suave agregamos todos los vegetales, sal y pimienta, salsa inglesa y seguimos cocinando a fuego lento hasta consumir el liquido y quede una salsa espesa, estos deliciosos medallones los acompañe con arroz blanco y tajadas de platano. Gracias amigos por compartir, saludos. 🙏🏻🙏🏻🫂🫂

We live in a world full of tribulations.  Tribulation can come to both the righteous and the wicked. It can come to anyone. There is no special people that tribulation can come to. It can come to the people of God, too.

 In ***John 16:33***, it says, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace in the world. Ye shall have tribulation, but be of good cheer, and overcome the world. 

 Jesus Christ is telling himself that we might overcome tribulations as children of Christ. The world is full of injustice, corruption, and so many good things, but we will not have to skip through. The world is a very good place, but it can be turned into a miserable place because of the disobedience of God. 

Sometimes in the past, the earth can be a very important place for us to live. So many people are dying of hunger. People have lost their jobs. People  have lost resources and everything. So only few are really enjoying life, which is not free tribulation. God has assured us that we are part of those that also enjoy life as children of God. 

 God has given us what we need here on earth, even though it might be free tribulation. God wants to tell you that civilization should be over.

body.title: Visiting A Productive and Agricultural Place in Parola Farm Valley In Manticao, Misamis Oriental
body.body: >\nIf we say valley, it is a kind of place where plain lands can be seen and found. This time, I decided to went at the Farm valley located here in Zone 23, Barangay Poblacion Manticao, Misamis Oriental Mindanao Philippines. A place where lots of valuable agricultural plants like coconuts and bananas planted. Parola farm valley is not only a place where small private resort and swimming pool built, it is also a kind of land where different kinds of plants locates. This farm holds 15 hectare and all of it are filled with agricultural plants like coconuts and banana. Yesterday, I decided to went there for a Nature trip because this place is also filled and surrounded with lots of big and tall trees grows. \n</div class=\

>

![Messenger_creation_D16A0723-409F-4C82-BEB8-8B381B26FE97.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdLyvvSH4jfACAdeH52dtv45PrPdkWEP8gzJX1d7YdTBX/Messenger_creation_D16A0723-409F-4C82-BEB8-8B381B26FE97.jpeg)
</center>
This dusty and bumpy road here served as a shortcut road going to the small sitio here in Barangay Poblacion. It is located at the middle of the farm and each side contains lots of tall coconut trees and wild plants grows. Accessible by any kinds of vehicles like trucks, cars, bicycles, motorcycles and many more. Aside of that bicycle trail activities is also good in here because of some obstacle course in this road just like bumpy and rocky parts of the road. Every time I went here, this is the only way we can passing by and because of the tall trees grows here, it is not really contains hot and intense heat because of the shady areas.

![Messenger_creation_AF2A0F82-6BB7-463B-B88A-A9D374C7B64E.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUsp9zXDR2Ve7icbDxPyovZJf77NQMv2Gw9DuwLWrFEuw/Messenger_creation_AF2A0F82-6BB7-463B-B88A-A9D374C7B64E.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_7AA32206-93A9-4768-AFDA-7FBDB7263005.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmStCMnMEqhDhGuqdKu1ihxyR6fKVtmmiV5pu9i9KTtjfM/Messenger_creation_7AA32206-93A9-4768-AFDA-7FBDB7263005.jpeg)
</center>
Not far from the Farm Valley is this wide long river. This is the Manticao River and it connects lots of streams passing by lots of Barangays also. Here in the Farm Valley, they get lots of water here using water Pump for the plants and animals. Aside of that, tourists who visited here at the Farm Valley don't want to miss to visit this river also taking pictures and enjoyed themselves walking and splashing of the crystal clear fresh and cold water at the river. It surrounded with lots of tall trees and wild plants on each side of the cliffs and few wild animals like birds also found here.

![Messenger_creation_10E1F867-0C39-4E58-9CC3-9ED516E55B8D.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUGfTaRrRtTTY5hv41dERt9rDHTwPGnwwP5jXMKz7VJx4/Messenger_creation_10E1F867-0C39-4E58-9CC3-9ED516E55B8D.jpeg)
</center>
This is the private and restricted areas here at the Valley, where fertilizers and any farm materials placed. Fences are made of sharp bobwires and metal sheets to keep ot secured. Only farm hired personels can enter inside of this place. It is also equipped with lots of solar lights at the fence and few Cameras working 24/7.

![Messenger_creation_FC4299EA-DD85-413B-BD6A-10C0C000A1C7.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmetT25MkY6LibAwVtSoH41QWFmgwYFkMQfuMpcMT7VCJT/Messenger_creation_FC4299EA-DD85-413B-BD6A-10C0C000A1C7.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_20926283-39F9-4D56-9518-F32F72E3B3D2.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSL63YADXXvrx5h5CoLwm74qVQ3uxzBrHtCYzJiTFS64x/Messenger_creation_20926283-39F9-4D56-9518-F32F72E3B3D2.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_15AA53A7-906B-421F-B8C6-6BFE4B41A388.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc5hRW3Tizpuwcs6ahjmXqXib8zarwzUcbeZpFkicQrqp/Messenger_creation_15AA53A7-906B-421F-B8C6-6BFE4B41A388.jpeg)
</center>
Hundreds of young coconut trees planted here and there are also lots of old tall trees can be seen and found here. Aside of that, banana plants also planted and it covers few hectares of land. Parola Farm valley is one of the good example of productive and very agricultural land. Land manage are well done and handled perfectly and truly inspired to other farmers who also owned a land. 

![Messenger_creation_FB40E644-7DE1-41DE-87B7-3B09991E2DF2.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPfWFifKdv5KpnvC1t4pmd2NFE28QkiHLRcUyB8h1a9Pr/Messenger_creation_FB40E644-7DE1-41DE-87B7-3B09991E2DF2.jpeg)
</center>
This very old foundation here was constructed late 90's and it is a kind of structure where an old hanging bridge was built here. For many years has past, the structure was completely abandoned leaving this piece of heavy and big concrete blocks and foundation. Owner says they will reconstructed it and make useful again. It built near at the bamboo trees so passers will feel comfortable and relaxing because of the cool and relaxing areas.

![Messenger_creation_8BD2B014-B21C-41C6-8775-E30FA97D1A52.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdJAk9umnMFhyjwimpGWyt2UKmxiTt1QKLBN4WDBuwp8Y/Messenger_creation_8BD2B014-B21C-41C6-8775-E30FA97D1A52.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_19D78D50-4D4A-4F18-8C39-FAA225572078.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP3zG37xHsbdfydx7JYteGhNm3aTNTy5tZ53f2iYFTntW/Messenger_creation_19D78D50-4D4A-4F18-8C39-FAA225572078.jpeg)
</center>
This is one of the stream connects to the river. As I observed during my visit, I noticed that the bodies of water is already dried up leaving this tons of big silica rocks at the surface. Every rainy season, lots of water flows here and sometimes residents went here just to washed their clothes and fetch water for their plants and animals. Cliffs are almost covered with big roots and tons of rocks and aside of that it also gives a relaxing and cool feelings brought by big trees and wild plants.

#### *This Valley hold lots of wonderful and inspiring things. This productive land will truly have and give a wonderful success not only to the owner but also for those who works in here*.


Until next post, have a nice and safe travel to everyone.

body.title: 🍋RECIPE FOR A FRUIT DRINK. 🍋(ENG-ESP)
body.body:
<center>**¡HELLO COMMUNITY🖐️**</center> 

* *Today I want to share a recipe that usually helps me on those days when I’m bloated due to indigestion, hormonal changes, or other situations that cause inflammation in our bodies. Ginger and turmeric tea is almost always the go-to drink for these situations, but I’m not a big fan of that kind of drink, so as an alternative, I usually make this recipe, which also helps reduce my inflammation.*

---------------------------


**ESP**

<center>**¡HOLA COMUNIDAD! 🖐️**</center>

* *El día de hoy quiero compartirles una receta que suele ayudarme en esos días cuando estoy inflamada debido a una mala digestión, cambios hormonales u otras situaciones que provocan alguna inflamación en nuestro cuerpo. Casi siempre la bebida efectiva para esas situaciones es el té de jengibre con cúrcuma, pero no soy muy fan de ese tipo de bebida, así que en alternativa yo suelo preparar esta receta que me ayuda a desinflamarme también.*

![fondo!!.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/quiubi/AKJ2dpsD6mwwkswKXZhXRrVdYNbfXZdEmd3o69WX9ur7LCJqyo4P9kxSUfXPTw4.jpg)

<center>**🍋INGREDIENTES:🍋**</center>

| *1 lemon tea bag.* | *1 tsp honey.*| 
| --------|---------|
| *1 tsp turmeric.* | *Any berries you like; I chose raspberries.*| 
| *1 tangerine.* | *300 ml water.*| 
| *1 tsp lemon juice.* | 

---------------------------------------

**ESP**


<center>**🍋INGREDIENTES:🍋**</center>

| *1 saqueta de té de limón.* | *1 cdta de miel.*| 
| --------|---------|
| *1 cdta de cúrcuma.* | *Algún fruto silvestre de tu agrado; yo escogí la frambuesa.*| 
| *1 tangerina.* | *300 ml de agua.*| 
| *1 cdta delimón.* |  

![ingre.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/quiubi/AK3fxRmkXbbaLo9zdQjNR7wmVXpSPCLeVXivXeojbDwTHhXicVs8YsBywS9vYz7.jpg)

<center>**🥣PREPARATION.🥣**</center>

* *First, peel the tangerine and place it in the water along with your favorite fruit. Then add the lemon and the tea bag, and let it steep for a few minutes. Finally, add the honey and turmeric, stir everything with a spoon, then remove the tea bag and blend the drink—and you’re done! If you like, you can strain it through a sieve to remove any lumps, and if you prefer it cold, you can add some ice.*

------------------------------------------


**ESP**

<center>**🥣PREPARACIÓN.🥣**</center>

* *Lo primero que necesitamos hacer es pelar la tangerina y colocarla en el agua junto con la otra fruta de tu agrado, después agregaremos el limón junto con la saqueta de té, dejándolo actuar por varios minutos. Por último, agregaremos la miel y la cúrcuma, mezclamos todo con una cuchara y después retiraremos la saqueta para licuar nuestra bebida y listo; si deseas, puedes pasarlo por un colador para evitar los grumos y, si deseas la bebida fría, puedes agregarle un poco de hielo.*

![primer.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/quiubi/AJkT4GPdbYgrbuJM4ZVuKbcM7gRBitxupxo4FZudCR3d1qoJCffsuzrRjzVW65u.jpg)

![primer1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/quiubi/AJj1pdHmbqN8V6JXJc66mFcyiJKoLwb5aT9QRaDSW42kF4RvBWAMa53A2TK3Tr3.jpg)

![primer2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/quiubi/AJpkqcPdG3DroUZYjqTjUWPjgTKLs7L6x2nnKqpVTsrS9UXsaDgGuUHsrvPrKVV.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZFCMgPaud8FzY7xZf5QEvB6BAmeHdBAGcax96zR3MCw8/separador.png)

body.title: Into the Dark.
body.body: > I started slaying infected on my way to the town hall but soon faced the dangers of the night. After being spotted by multiple volatiles and suffering a few quick deaths, I engaged in a high-stakes chase toward my safe house. I narrowly escaped up a ladder and decided to spend the night watching the moon. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbH4fThLf9GqzwJstgdnMbR3KqBxt6bb26QJ31s4dnjTQ/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZNwdtYQis9oB3v2Di3bVLN3yVhCJyKtLNqNujXoN8ZvS/screenshot_2_.png) I started slaying infected on my way towards the town hall, feeling the weight of the city in every swing. I was really enjoying capturing photos through the photo mode. The detail on the enemies was incredible, and I wanted to document my progress through this dangerous urban landscape before things got worse. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmesrSEFynHPRB1SYZ8gwgBeY6u4WpGzAHesncMJDfmYkS/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc3spF7x3r3PiXZeR3FPdjHCfDSTXgkGBQLHjdnnRWCw2/screenshot_4_.png) On my way, I ignored a group of infected standing on the bridge who were staring at the setting sun mysteriously. It was a strange and haunting sight to see them so still and focused on the orange horizon. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVFQm8Wks9iugxVzZWcuuGwmX2eW1iLR3nQXvSUm6NU8y/screenshot_5_.png) I passed them by at first, wondering what was going on in their broken minds as the day faded away. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme6T9Fv41KFJ5TupwkZUvZqECgg95Wxh7bsrVXzzGMuXU/screenshot_6_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP33MhE94feDuJhA6DDhUB2zW3DYZ7Wk66PDYm5PLqvAp/screenshot_7_.png) I decided to go back for them as they were still turned around and unaware of my presence. I took down two more of them quickly, using the element of surprise to clear the path. It was a satisfying moment of control before the true dangers of the night began to crawl out from the shadows. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQJEkihQaLC7uFL2NB5QP7GLdBwmqpU6G1M68auvPeX5K/screenshot_8_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdRPH93WJGenY2fVbJNcDFS8Jp7Ccn6yb9afTUHYeEMJe/screenshot_9_.png) One of them somehow saw me after the struggle and started chasing me while I was on my way through the street. Darkness had already settled over the city, making the roads look much more threatening than before. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYuUcLe2WVotFtW4aus5Ne47qn3oJwAbxCzdGmrTy9QCF/screenshot_10_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdpz7AHRa7sHEgaGV3BihWEodxiyCeiQ2Q6dBicNTVY2z/screenshot_11_.png) I didn't want to fight them in the dark because I never know their movement when visibility is this low. I started ignoring them and moved towards the town hall. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNee3zNeYqeMavLovhoqAP6NWp2zhALhpADuenCKAbZZR/screenshot_12_.png) I was warned that at night, volatiles appear and that a chase starts if they spot me. Suddenly, I was spotted by a volatile that let out a terrifying scream. I didn't want to fight this scary monster, so I started running backwards to put some distance between us before it could leap. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPvqAK1atRBEFHGH6Y2HEH8qzFbW4HaFs2tpByz8xLkwf/screenshot_13_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTLKK6ajzkqANwb5fYLkGVsUZzt2kjcLJAYXbNnvKXvSz/screenshot_14_.png) I noticed through the photo mode that there was not just one, but multiple of those fast infected who were chasing me. And they caught up to me and initially took me down in a flurry of strikes. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZs4jusBepFkRxD9rxqDRmXsmymz5eCYeTvohe61qUvTa/screenshot_15_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc2rkYPs2a8fuG7wtYYFHoGc3FZbzhaAquwC7t4b7XdEb/screenshot_16_.png) At the restart, I found myself close to my tower safe house, but the danger was still very real. There was this volatile nearby who spotted me instantly and took me down real fast before I could even reach the safehouse. It was a brutal reminder of how vulnerable I was during the night hours. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNqtC6ppuRry1kGnvxzfAEuBb4nLipB9c9UEiaDAMoVR7/screenshot_17_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeRxsWRZsT6N4WuBRv4CtppjsiNe1zXEAhYgsvHaz4GLv/screenshot_18_.png) At the next restart, I just knew what to do to survive the encounter. I started running towards the safe house as fast as I could while those volatiles kept chasing me through the dark. I didn't look back once, focused entirely on the safe house. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdLvT37FNCdPbsxtZUReCH5bWgAHZZeQ8UdRS7EUVTyyW/screenshot_19_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNhKFS7MJtTLvvBDdFrXTLQR9AfZHQAoCrHU4wQQXR8sQ/screenshot_20_.png) After getting to the safe house, it became very hard for me to climb up on the ladder. The volatiles kept trying to snatch me back down with their claws. But at last, I climbed up to the top where they couldn't follow me. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRLJ1afiRhWRUmUPjYZaAd9pbEY9GvyahS5tT7ygrtEjm/screenshot_21_.png) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ8EFigDjyyo3kZfhNsFU5c7uVrEaA14nwi6kqd76KU8H/screenshot_22_.png) I decided to spend the night in that place because I was not interested in getting killed again by those volatiles below. I stopped on the edge of the tower and started just enjoying the beautiful moon in the dark. It was a peaceful moment after one of the most terrifying chase of my life. I'll show what happens next later. --- I personally took all the screenshots from my play and I used a logo of the game from online to use in the thumbnail. This is Pikachuuuuu signing off. Over and out. --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=pikachuuuuu/ebddca82)

body.title: A tangible symbol / Un símbolo tangible
body.body:
I remember that ever since elementary school, children in Venezuela have been taught the importance of both the country’s national symbols (the flag, coat of arms, and national anthem) and its natural symbols (the national tree, flower, and bird), but the reality is that when you go out on the street, you rarely see the latter around.

>*Recuerdo que desde la escuela primaria, a los niños en Venezuela nos enseñan la importancia tanto de los símbolos patrios (bandera, escudo e himno nacional) como de los símbolos naturales (el árbol, la flor y el ave nacional) del país, pero la realidad es que, cuando sales a la calle, de estos últimos poco se ve por ahí.*

<center>![IMG_20260208_112646.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EqNGavQT8XY2Qe8AVobjYyRMLUQHCVPn8xWoxqZonwATX3gypCKsncjBtzzCbDbc3Da.jpg)</center>

That’s what came to mind when I was walking down a street and the bright yellow of some flowering trees caught my eye. They were Araguaney trees (Handroanthus chrysanthus), the national tree. Around this time of year, they’re in full bloom and certainly don’t go unnoticed, but for a tree that’s supposedly our national tree “on paper,” I feel like they’re not very common in towns and cities.

>*Eso fue lo que vino a mi mente cuando pasé por una calle y el intenso amarillo de unos árboles florecidos captó mi atención. Se trataba de unos Araguaney (Handroanthus chrysanthus), el árbol nacional. Por esta época sueltan sus flores y no pasan desapercibidos, pero para ser \

nuestro árbol nacional, me parece que su presencia es poca en pueblos y ciudades.*

<center>![IMG_20260208_112701.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/244eEoZApKWq1mAs25qf44hNDJMGDSBnmtTLFF5vxu48zbGUjPHNGmuasqb6PpDiNZcPF.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260208_112717.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EpvjPt9teujLms6ckry9oVUZBddbELWyZniMKJk5HGeyRVYbXChMrroDS2Ne2xhtHwV.jpg)</center>

The same is true of the national flower, the orchid (Cattleya mossiae). It is not often found in public spaces, for example, serving to highlight Venezuelan identity.

>*Lo mismo pasa con la flor nacional, que es la orquídea (Cattleya mossiae). No es común que esté en espacios públicos, por ejemplo, resaltando la identidad venezolana.*

<center>![IMG_20260208_112739.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Ep5niFxJ1eD8p7jqgGuVAMYFsgE8yUsDvYgydkygnSjd5FnBJVyB3KbqNAC7Lxit6DZ.jpg)</center>

Several years ago, the Ministry of the Environment launched a reforestation initiative called \

, which covers not only protected areas but also urban spaces. I believe the Araguaney tree should be given its rightful place, not just symbolically, and that we should start planting it on a large scale in all of Venezuela’s towns and cities. It would be an amazing sight to see so many streets and avenues turn yellow every year between January and April 😍.\n\n>*Hace varios años el Ministerio del Ambiente creó un plan para reforestar llamado \

, que aparte de zonas protegidas también incluye a los espacios urbanos. Creo que al Araguaney se le debería dar su lugar no sólo simbólicamente, y empezar a plantarlo a gran escala en todos los pueblos y ciudades de Venezuela. Sería un tremendo espectáculo ver cada año muchas calles y avenidas teñirse de amarillo entre enero y abril 😍.*
![IMG_20260208_112820.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EoMF76J1tYScrVBqpzi5EYG8XVrGMcAgXvgxQ8ijy9pYBTMYyJyM6LbvBseGxdTEnLp.jpg)
![IMG_20260208_112830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Eo8TPv5kt5zt6pbBJBqLkqiambTFJinZvnF8Q54kG67dxo3NvD1yNac4375SLqqh3Bi.jpg)

河口是一个神秘而美丽的地方，它是淡水与海水交汇的区域，孕育了丰富的生态系统。在这里，常常能看到各种鸟类和海洋生物，仿佛是自然的舞台，展现出生命的多样性和神奇。走在河口边，听着水波荡漾的声音，感受到微风拂面，让人不禁沉醉于这份宁静与和谐。河口不仅是生物的栖息地，也是人类与自然相互联系的重要纽带，提醒我们珍惜和保护这一片宝贵的生态环境。

body.body:
**English**

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYkE1XbDJhGZHHsjwwFfb9SjJC2KaTQpWkZeV6YBU1UeP/1775940628248.png)</center>

Hello everyone! I took this photo on the famous Lenin Hill (Colina Lenin) in the municipality of Regla, Havana, Cuba. It is a well-known spot for those living in this part of the city because a monument to Vladimir Ilich Lenin was built here, and in the past, it served as a hub for family activities.

​From the top of the hill, there is a spectacular view of the municipality of Regla, where you can also see the bay and Havana's most famous buildings.

​This lookout is a great place to take photos and spend a pleasant day with friends. In Cuba, the municipality of Regla is known as the Sierra Chiquita (Little Sierra), and it is unique for being the only municipality in Havana where almost everything works well; the people there still have a strong sense of belonging to their community and defend their principles at any cost.

***
***

**Español**

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYkE1XbDJhGZHHsjwwFfb9SjJC2KaTQpWkZeV6YBU1UeP/1775940628248.png)</center>

Hola a todos. Tomé esta foto sobre la famosa Colina Lenin en el municipio de Regla, La Habana, Cuba. Es un lugar muy conocido por la gente que vive en esta parte de la ciudad porque aquí se le hizo un Monumento a Vladimir Ilích Lenin y era un espacio que en el pasado sirvió como centro de actividades para toda la familia. 

Desde la cima de la Colina hay una vista espectacular del municipio de Regla desde donde se ve también la Bahía y los edificios más famosos de La Habana.

Este mirador es espectacular para venir a hacer fotos y pasar un día agradable con los amigos. En Cuba al municipio de Regla le dicen la *Sierra Chiquita*, y tiene la particularidad de que es el único municipio de La Habana donde casi todo funciona bien; las personas aún conservan el sentido de pertenencia por el sitio donde viven y defienden sus principios a cualquier costo.

body.title: Unexpected Gift
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfCTWcvtZQEVqrpViUcGTkce7Qn8P5jbrSAaHa8a4YGk3/img_20260421_155725.jpg)

---


Good news reached me today. After a long time without having coffee at home, the miracle finally happened. One of my patients brought me a bit of ground coffee this morning at the hospital, and he doesn’t know the joy that unleashed in me. Well, maybe he knows a little, since my face didn’t hide a single gesture—he must have noticed.  

---
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbYkZ3gwBKbHGaPzdFpfro9rNrGaMjUxK8TZXG2d3RNg3/img_20260421_155907.jpg)

---
In Cuba, patients often give gifts to doctors for the services they receive, especially if they feel the care and treatment were of good quality. Some give more, some give less. Honestly, I prefer when the gift is simple, because otherwise I feel like I’m being paid for my services. And while I would love to live off what I do, the truth is I wouldn’t feel right charging an exorbitant price to someone who needs it but might not be able to afford it.  

Back to this particular gift: it seems my patient was very grateful, because the coffee is of extremely high quality. The aroma is so remarkable that my coworkers kept asking where coffee was being made, not knowing that I was the owner of that treasure.  

---
<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTzmceD3W16zQTTirkyLH7Nyni66ouojTxEfLNPjgJDiD/img_20260421_155826.jpg)<sub>Sorry, there's no more</sub></center>

---

At home there was no sugar, so with a bit of condensed milk we reached the perfect balance. My wife nearly fainted when she found out I had brought coffee. She was so happy that I think today she won’t argue with me about anything. The downside is that I probably won’t sleep well tonight, since I had a big cup in the afternoon. So insomnia is guaranteed.  

But it doesn’t matter. The pleasure of drinking homemade coffee is enough to endure the sleeplessness. I’ll just see what to do tonight while I count sheep to fall asleep.  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmedBwZf9LDx6XPGNa19jnkfkRJP9YYPAkdY2wp7o1UtAQ/beige_illustrative_call_to_action_blog_banner_20250414_100317_0000.png)

body.title: Online Learning Is Not for the Weak
body.body:
<div class=text-justify>



![IMG_4996.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teknon/23wC12DPEMiRbiZKMuDEj28wr5HuSA12BmzbqHMGeWnmZk5kFQ8z8auFVxGqFaqWoEVtq.jpeg)

I used to think taking classes online was easier than sitting in a physical classroom with an actual tutor. The idea just made sense in my head as I imagined it as comfort, flexibility and no pressure. I mean you could learn at your own pace, pause when you want, and rewind when you miss something. It literally sounds like the perfect setup.

But I was wrong. Oh, very wrong. Because what I didn’t consider is that online learning, especially when it’s self-paced, requires a level of discipline I hadn’t fully prepared myself for. It’s even worse when you’re not using a laptop, but your phone. The same device that holds your distractions, your social media, your messages, your entire world of ‘let me just check this quickly.’

So, I recently signed up for two online courses, *Business Management and Advertising*, and another on *Content Writing and Social Media Strategy*. At the end of it, I’ll get certificates I can proudly add to my CV. So yes, this matters to me.

I started with the business course, feeling all motivated and ready until I realized I wasn’t considering that somehow, my mind just refuses to stay in one place. I’d be watching a lesson, trying to focus, and suddenly I’m thinking about something else. Or reaching for another app, convincing myself I deserve just a short break that always turns into a long one. Then I come back hours later, disconnected and slightly annoyed at myself.

![IMG_4995.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teknon/23tmb45nqEbYf1M7L5o4D6LVbyocbwH3WZjL7SSfE4xVgyctScfXY23CB6rpqpUev35xt.jpeg)
<sup>screenshot from my mailbox</sup>

It’s frustrating ngl. The class itself isn’t bad, it’s just that my attention isn’t where it needs to be. I’ve even caught myself calling it boring, which I know isn’t entirely fair. It is definitely not the course, it’s me. I’m just not used to sitting still long enough, all by myself, to learn something that doesn’t immediately entertain me. This realization has humbled me though because this is something I actually want.

It is a skill I want to have as it can shape my future, open doors for me, and help me grow into the kind of professional I imagine myself becoming. So I really can’t afford to take it lightly.

I’ve also come to understand that online learning isn’t easy. It takes responsibility. To choose, over and over again, to stay focused even when your mind wants to wander, staying when it gets boring, pushing through when it feels slow and to build discipline, even when no one is watching.

Anyway, I’m still figuring it out and trying to do better. But at least now, I know what I’m up against.

<sup>[img1](https://pixabay.com/photos/online-learning-video-conference-5163039/)</sup>


</diva>

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@teknon/online-learning-is-not-for-the-weak-egm)

body.title: Thinking Beyond Code, in the agentic era
body.body: **Beyond Code, toward proof first**\n\nI like to say \
. We are now in the era where agentic workflows matter far more than code. So in this post I'll discuss what it means to think \

, and address the topic of agentic workflows.\n\nThe basic workflow that most people use when using AI, is to go to ChatGPT, prompt the chatbot, and perhaps learn prompt engineering skills. This is not generally a form of \
, this is essentially vibe coding. The novice tells the Chatbot \
and in one shot, the Chatbot builds an app. This typically results in AI slop, the code quality is usually low because the prompt simply was \

or some variation of that. Why is this a problem? From a cybersecurity perspective, the app is most likely to have bugs, from a UX perspective, the app may look like it works, but then under the hood the app has placeholder code, TODO, no error handling, etc. Unfortunately, vibe coding has caught on, and the easy way has become the standard way.\n\nI'm not here to discuss the standard way of doing things. The agentic workflows I'm introducing are not vibe coding. In fact, this workflow will require thinking about software in an entirely different way than even most software developers with decades of experience think about software. The word to start with, is abstraction, and the phrase is \

. The difference between vibe coder and agentic engineer, are that the vibe coder is a prompt engineer, they know how to prompt, but they don't understand the deep concepts behind software. For example, when you think about what the LLM actually does, it's an abstraction layer, it's not AGI, it's predicting the next token, it's primary abilities are pattern matching, search, translation, and with this tool you can go to a very high level of abstraction above the code level.

**From abstraction, to loop engineering**

You can think about software as state machines for example. When you do this, you abstract away the unnecessary parts and keep the vital parts. This allows you to map out the software and every behavior.  You can think use the LLM to search for disaster states, states which you want to be unreachable. How do you do this? You have to go beyond prompt engineering, and begin loop engineering, and the loop that enables this is the neuro symbolic loop. You connect the LLM to a formal checker, a proof assistant, and you treat the LLM as a proposer. The loop is propose, check, refine.

 This is basically abstracting the LLM itself into a component in the toolchain of your loop. By doing this, the code isn't the problem anymore. The programs become math formulas, proofs, state machines, and you can very exactly talk about the behavior of these programs in this form. You can't talk about software in code in this way because code is too ambiguous, too many lines, at too low level of abstraction. You can however speak in math, those formulas are not ambiguous, high level of abstraction, and the best part of all, you can prove the behavior of the math without having to know anything about the code. That's where things are today with software, and in the ideal world we would have a lot more high assurance software because of AI. In the actual world, we have a lot more software, but it also means more bug surface.

In future posts, I will go into some of the techniques, and the tools like Lean, Z3, Aristotle, etc.

body.title: The illusion of value
body.body:
![76BF1652-6B97-408F-AE49-6F1EE4EE318A.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23wqnMn65FkngyL76KK3iBgpME9wsnp4zUsdkaGmPXdxuoi7KeR1FGmZGQ3n9hw5XS411.jpeg)
***

What you wear doesn’t constitute your value. Nor does the excess jewellery you posses. Neither your physical assets.

It’s just a fraction of it. A portrayal for your external environment. To serve as an appeal. To sum up appreciation, respect and praise from others. But if you lack a sense of actual self value it will start to reflect subconsciously. And then it starts compounding in real-time. When it eventually erupts, your ego gets stripped down and your perceived “value” in a society that encourages doing-your-all for the sake of social status becomes diluted.

You cannot “fake it to you make it”. You cannot put on a persona or facade of genuine character or charisma that you lack. Value is communicated through kindness. Integrity. Having a grounded mentality and life perspective. It isn’t forcibly conceived. A lot of people try to conceal the “worst” aspect of themselves. They play the long game of fitting in and being socially acceptable. This can work in the short term. But it seethes out and doesn’t withhold in the long term.

Have you ever wondered why even the most visibly unattractive, the seemingly unwise or the least desirable-to-be person often makes it in life? Why even the person who looks or acts the dumbest, is the smartest? It isn’t a matter of life luck or fortunate enough circumstances. It’s there internal environment shedding its true nature. Confidence can beat looks. Same way brains beats brawn. Personally I’ve met many people with natural charisma and despite their perceived flaws they are phenomenal in many ways and aspects.

Understand that there’s more to what meets the eye. Although at times there is an unstable truthfulness to they saying that “don’t judge a book by its cover.” Because there are a few people who are truly as unfortunate as they seem. But observe people with intent. Not surface-level glances of perception. That’s how you know if there is value in someone.

body.title: Guía Maestra de Crianza Consciente.
body.body:
<div class='text-justify'>

*Criar en este 2026 no es tarea fácil. Entre la velocidad de la tecnología y las exigencias del día a día, es normal sentirse perdido. A lo largo de estas semanas, hemos construido un edificio de tres pisos que hoy terminamos de consolidar.*

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSnQd6H515Qoo3Ks6GJYktFVFMKmfb3EgxcdWcVQwHA3Q/image.png)
</center>
<center>[Fuente]https://www.tigercampus.hk/es/parental-involvement-in-student-success/)</center>

### Los Cimientos (Teoría): Primero entendimos el porqué. 
Aprendimos que un niño no \

. Cambiamos el chip del control por el de la conexión. Sin esta base, nada de lo demás se sostiene.

### Las Paredes y el Techo (Gestión de Crisis): 
Luego pasamos al cómo sobrevivir a las tormentas. Aprendimos a manejar berrinches, pantallas y mentiras. Estas herramientas son las que protegen la relación en los momentos difíciles para que el hogar siga siendo un lugar seguro.

### El Interior y el Futuro (Habilidades para la Vida): 
Finalmente, miramos hacia el mañana. Ya no solo apagamos fuegos, sino que sembramos semillas: gratitud, respeto al cuerpo, manejo del dinero y resiliencia. Estamos preparando a nuestros hijos para que no nos necesiten, porque ya tienen sus propias herramientas.

# La \

de Oro: 5 Pilares para No Olvidar Jamás
Si algún día sientes que vas a perder el control o no sabes qué hacer, vuelve a estos cinco puntos:

#### 1. Conexión antes que Dirección
Antes de corregir una conducta, conecta con el corazón.
Nadie escucha a alguien con quien se siente desconectado. Si tu hijo está en medio de un caos emocional, primero busca su mirada, baja a su nivel y valida lo que siente. Una vez que esté en calma, recién ahí podrá aprender la lección.

#### 2. Sé un \

en la Tormenta
En un avión con turbulencia, miras a la azafata: si ella está en calma, tú te calmas. Tus hijos hacen lo mismo contigo. Tu autocontrol es su mayor maestro. Si tú gritas para que ellos no griten, el mensaje se pierde. La calma es contagiosa, pero la ansiedad también.

#### 3. Límites con Amor (Firmeza y Amabilidad)
Los límites no son muros para encerrar al niño, son barandales para que no se caiga al vacío. Puedes ser muy firme con la regla (\
) y, al mismo tiempo, muy amable con la emoción (\

).

#### 4. El Error es una Oportunidad, no una Vergüenza
Ya sea que tu hijo rompa un jarrón, mienta o pierda un examen, el enfoque debe ser siempre: ¿Cómo lo reparamos? Eliminar la culpa y el miedo al castigo es lo que permite que la honestidad y la responsabilidad crezcan. Enséñale que equivocarse es parte de ser humano.

#### 5. Tu Hijo es el Dueño de su Historia
Desde el nombre de sus partes privadas hasta el dinero de su alcancía o el orden de su cuarto; nuestra meta es la autonomía. Cada vez que dejas que él decida o que asuma una consecuencia natural, le estás diciendo: \

.

***Reflexión Final***
Recuerda siempre la frase que nos trajo hasta aquí: \

.

_No buscamos ser padres perfectos (porque no existen), buscamos ser padres presentes, que reparan cuando se equivocan y que ven en cada reto una oportunidad para crecer junto a sus hijos._
