![IMG_9305.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23tH5ocMrQwfBKmgazfm5udcNiatwC123p6tCyF5Y19etAAbG6WoUyd1Z9mzTM151KZjF.JPG) ![IMG_9340.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/244xurTfNhviidQHGJ7RaKcxutMaEjpV1ymqCqx4TcMp1r1fY7KB19QvyvW822BBihNrP.JPG) ![IMG_9337.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23y8m6iAqVDgEGTw47SRs6yA6n8nQG54PTwGfHZS1DHMAtWThoNVrcsDwwjHc2JpyranM.JPG) ![IMG_9349.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23r1gcVPEna6aUkNLZZ2FYNoojZrt5Ni3xNY2CV7G8qkeL5BB9TjG82Y6k7G1HU5YR72u.JPG) ![IMG_9343.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/244UhBCZpzZRVb6kJvNKcMdoe1DJGxq83DnrzaptSApbah9j1PPv8NT9fVmbziyDFc7rT.JPG) #
*What is the geology of the area like?🌏🧭 / Como es la geologia de la zona*📍🌏
![IMG_9367.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23xVGvdf2ZYL49TYFXty2EFSbHzFw5CiTY9YMNqeHWMYRcN3dLzLe6io1LHCeEJB7Jjhs.JPG) ![IMG_9369.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23wWttJ1VvngNtz6jjvsUAekxNZ27BRam5w4YjM5HG6EYAfBWnDiAMs8RW8a38ffhe7oT.JPG) ![IMG_9419.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23wC3dW5TCULuMsuSVEsoqW3BSE7FLtxPg46KPpmPY4kza8Gid5tty1qagTvDjkcfh6Aw.JPG) ![IMG_9418.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23tvZvphBZQJ1VKvBDDRjqEq1SGQ9n9tff5QjHHwKAoUkT9xn46pk4zdjBX7RuWSdgNvv.JPG) ![IMG_9420.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23uaHLNBE3bx3mLUgJD7aGH6fJKrzhzXLS6eePJBcaNo3rZaP7cE5Rtnt3B9a9oofwXgT.JPG) ![IMG_9421.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23rz4pSYLfL7g92XSeCXVYbBPadd6f7wX5iV5A3XAjtUpwD5t887UyktNar8Vv92ey7wY.JPG) *I don't remember if I ever mentioned it on my blog, but Sintra is the result of a volcanic explosion millions of years ago, so it's common to see rocks like granite and syenite. This means you see rocks in places where it seems impossible they could have fallen.🏕️🌋* *No recuerdo si en alguna vez lo mencione en mi blog pero Sintra es el resultado de una explocion volcanica hace millones de anos, por tanto es comun ver rocas de tipo: Granitos, Sienitos, todo esto hace que se vean rocas en sitios donde parece que no hay forma que cayeran aqui📸🌏*
![gif6_dorado_shimmer.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23twC3hcw4x8Y1qsCn6goYEV4x9NWf6UVG34R2w6WFF2csuDuQtCy4TdwzfaVVon48NV1.gif)
#
*The mystery of the dolmen🌏🧭 / El misterio del dolmen*📍🌏
![BgxWBRxjvNho1d5owNvLc9kLkZETgqoQLu9zcBbNBbDDEp9W4DbuZJuZSPnNwG4dahUdZ7iLBeaEDuESopcTMCRgAazANoCQEq4zcnuQitM9YpG8qckzzYRdss1xYwxFWP2oQVUQuHgnP9WNxwUuBnuLMZQRaa6uX25iH5BL4G5CqTj.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23w2q22mgGyWkMGH9rtgBp2wYfXmBt2HunQSbnpeuGYC7aGMxcYJrUuQHo2iFD2q8Ndvn.gif)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRU3TTNpiXdUHzpDcxj4seWERZtBaEHJePG6LRspr1iik/bgxwbrxjvnho1d5ownvlc9klkzetgqoqlu9zcbbnbbddep9w4dbuzjuzspnnwg4dahudz7ilbeaeduev8xfikqmbn1e5g1vbbkvlr9fhd3uhiqsrmqnkd4g8rwlkkneqcijq382njssl5nnns1ojj7wnddbm1kmrhvxtzwa2vbb4yxf.gif)
![IMG_9469.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/244A6UQfE7jBRuxgsHLmghBct41aNZpF3j35K8z1zcnp5of38nBPcr9NcMMmFdffdQ6Gq.JPG) *I could say I have some experience with dolmens; it's not my field of research, but I've visited and researched many, so I have some technical knowledge about this prehistoric engineering work. If you want to learn more, just look for this post:📍📸* *Podria decirse que tengo un poco de experiencia sobre el tema de los Dolmenes, no es mi campo de investigacion pero ya visite muchisimos e investigue muchos tambien, asi que tengo un conocimiento tecnico sobre esta obra de ingenieria prehistorica, en realidad si quieres aprender mas basta con buscar este post:👨🏻‍🏫🙇🏻‍♀️* ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPPAKhnCd6XNSk8WA8GaeAiFbqTjEXe3XPQq4TR3Y8HGZ/image.png) https://peakd.com/hive-196387/@biologistbrito/route-of-the-dolmens-ruta-de-los-dolmenes-en-es
The dolmen was investigated in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. One of the key characteristics for determining whether a megalithic complex corresponds to a dolmen is the presence of buried bones or fragments of objects, all dating from the fifth to the third century BC. Although Adrenunes resembles a dolmen, no bones were ever discovered.📸🧭
El dolmen fue investigado en finales del siglo XIX y tambien principios del XX, una de las caracteristicas primordiales para descartar si un conjunto megalitico corresponde a un Dolmen es por que hay huesos enterrados o fragmentos de objetos, y todos datan de el quinto al tercer siglo antes de Cristo, apesar que Adrenunes tiene la similitud de un Dolmen nunca se descubrieron huesos.📍🚙
![IMG_9476.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23ywpnLYPurTuwRPs4CTHgxDy2F3WA7D8LyE9rsaWZohsDCZ4wePeKi7YVBmp5ottNytZ.JPG)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWwBpkvjsw8PVyvBLewWFVfDQCDzyVSivGoP8JUiYGHZt/img_9473.jpg)
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcFGKp5AdnQLKN6y9eu5SQU3kXwzRB1RfVjLMqEzs6DZS/befunky_collage_2026_04_21t173332.275.jpg)
The Dolmen has many interesting features that suggest it was used in prehistoric times and that people were buried there. However, I believe the most valid theory is that it was a structure built by people, not for burials, but for worshipping gods, since the setting sun illuminates the entrance, as if it had been intentionally placed that way.🏕️🌏🌋
El Dolmen reune muchas cosas interesantes como para pensar que si fue usado en la era prehistorica y que se enterraban personas, sin embargo yo creo que la teoria con mayor validez es que fue un local construido por personas pero no para enterrar, si no para hacer culto a dioses, ya que el sol en la puesta ilumina la entrada, como si hubiese sido colocado asi de forma intencional🌻🌺📍
![gif5_verde_animado.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/biologistbrito/23tcQwWKu1QjkmYPLdJN15WRfUrWr5Zze8TmQubBPDAMTVRodNmLrtSsE28CqDNnvviZy.gif)
#
*My final opinion🌏🧭 / Mi opinion final*📍🌏
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQdzQSjVXmAGoWNiYqDcs7gRFav99dVdteaBWSgA76FKD/img_9474.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfNzMV9FbkkpAkycJgf9H1rqQB1RekU5e1Y6gzDzKwCou/img_9481.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbN7xLpbs7B13xEevt6gBw6W2e5AwzXKrdkDoaUhQtuQR/img_9482.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZwjm4BRCrRFB5NUCTh8TcVZ61CYPQZmeMV5GqDgkgtB6/img_9483.jpg) ================================================================================= # En: * Personally, as a scientist, I need more evidence to prove that this is a dolmen; we cannot base our conclusion solely on its shape.📍 * It wasn't a coincidence of nature; many pieces of evidence show that there was human intervention here.📍 * A unique experience for adventurers and budget tourists📍 * A trail with a 4/5 star rating in my opinion📍 ================================================================================= # Es: * En lo personal como cientifico necesito mas evidencias que demuestren que esto es un Dolmen no podemos basarnos solo en la forma📍 * No fue una casualidad de la naturaleza, muchas pruebas demuestran que hay mano humana aqui📍 * Una experiencia unica para aventureros y hacer turismo economico📍 * Un sendero con una evaluacion de 4/5 estrellas para mi gusto📍 ================================================================================= #

body.title: Platonika
body.body:
Ten důvod, proč se zamilovaní oddávají platonickým hrám je veliká touha po přesahu, je veliká zvědavost po poznání dokonalosti, je veliká ctnost potřeby čistoty.

Mé skladby jsou platonické, ušima se blížím pojmům jako je jednota i mnohost, niternost, bolest, touha, číslo a tvary prožívání jsou zhmotněné geometrické objekty prožívání.

Rozděluji čísla do skupin, vytvářím pole jejich působnosti, dávám prostor pro vyniknutí čísla jako bodu prožití.

A to vše platonicky.

Hudba je nejvyšší formou matematiky, v které je poznat cit čísel, jejich gravitace, tenze a energie, v čísle se projevuje odraz nejen naší lidskosti, ale i univerzality našeho prožívání.

Proč se jim, těmto hrám, říká platonické?

Protože není prostor se takové věci dotknout, ustupuje o patro dál, kdykoli se chci vnořit do zvuku, třeba zoomováním spektrálním způsobem po vzoru Griseyho Partiels se dostáváme do zvuku jenom jako a i látku, kterou skládám já, nelze předat zcela.

Na povrchu je nosičem hudby barva, která nelze od jádra odlepit, vyjádření je vždycky obalené hávem zvuku.

Když si představujeme, co je pod ním, získáváme jakýsi návod, jak se takové platonické hry účastnit:

Studovat kontrapunkt a harmonii, abychom pronikli myšlenky o střetech tónů a jejich působení.

Úkolem umělce je vžírat se do materie, vžít se do čísla a vsnít se do významu a pokud možno milovat.

Milování nejde zkazit, ale v platonice se dají dělat chyby: Vnitřní logiky platonických vzorců lze překročit, lze havarovat a dělat lepší nebo horší kroky. Milování je pohon, je potřeba, ale ne záruka úspěchu.

Je potřeba se orientovat ve hře, kterou rozehráváme, a dělat dobré tahy, jako šachista v partii, partie lze hrát přímě, se zatáčkami a výkruty, vášnivě a až bezhlavě nebezpečně s citem vyhnout se havárii.

Některé mé partie jsou opatrné v direkci, tedy směru komponování, a jdou přímo, bezohledné můžou být ve zvukové mase, která se v partii projevuje nekompromisně s vidinou koupele posluchače v očistné sprše expresivní masy.

Slova jako kužel, válec a koule už neznamenají jen platonickou formu, ale i platonický vztah k tvaru: Láska se projevuje umem se mezi tvary pohybovat a sdělovat své stesky, bolesti, trápení, ale i radost a jednoduchý něžný cit.

Umělec platonik nedbá krásných šatů na pódiu, věhlasu nad virtuózním umem, ani na celkovém zvuku a jeho dokonalosti a čistotě.

Umělec platonik jde k jádru věci a když jádro objímá, vynáší ho ven, zvukem, mezi lidi, aby bylo slyšet, co je v nás stejné, ale i to, čím se umělcův pohled liší.

Naše univerzalita dovoluje číslu působit na lidi analogicky, hudba je kolektivním vlastnictvím, žije v nás stejně a žije díky světu idejí, tedy platónském světě forem.

Zamilovaní si hrají s těmito kuželkami, míči a narážkami, laškují, škádlí a rozesmívají. Vtip je příklad, zápletka je dramatickým prvkem cesty ke smíření, neutralizace je vášnivá výměna názorů, která mění zásadu i kyselinu a kde agrese v myšlenkách skončí, cítíme klid a dokonalost, životodárnou vodu a sůl, bez které je v pohádkách těžko.

Každý hudebník se potýká se zápletkami antitezí v sonátách a harmonických funkcích, dualismus tónové gravitace nelze vynechat, skladatel míří k prozkoumání rozkolu, prožití růstu a pádu, prožití protikladu, aby našel smír.

Vyndám-li já z vnitřku, v platonické hře, něco nepříjemného, neohlížím se na publikum, beru na sebe úkol problém přiblížit, zvěčnit ho a sdílet s těmi, s kterými je to potřeba. Někdy, poštěstí-li se, vyřešit.

Jednou přijdu k myšlence, která umí jen trýznit, nebo ustoupit, jednou k takové, která ukazuje jednoduchý cit, některé jsou o cestě mezi stavy, o zkažení čistých platonických cest směrem k drsnému jádru, jiné vystupují čistší na konci, po dlouhé hře, kde se snažil šachista nevzdat partii příliš brzo, dokud byla naděje.

Čím je esence jednodušší jako tvar, tím snáze chápu povahu problému. Jsou takové, jako například v Dodekafonní sonátě, kde hra o rozuzlení šla k jádru čistoty z velké dálky, jsou takové, jako můj Malý harmonický labyrint, které jsou v uchopení problému snad až příliš zodpovědné, vyčerpávající svojí hloubkou, drhnutím o dno myšlenky na modulaci, jsou takové, které rozehrávají hru o hudební historii, jako Dvanáctitónová pohádka, nebo Cesta, která k tomu důsledně vyčerpává jen jeden typ vztahu mezi akordy.

Každá má hra je formou a prostorem pro milování, možnost vyznat se shledávám v tom, jak dalece se ve skladbě skutečně \

. Hledě na význam pak poznávám sebe a svět, protože povaha problému se ve skladbě jednak zhmotní a jednak projdeme skrz poučeni emocí a situacemi ve skladbě jako o něco bohatější a znalejší duše.

Nitra máme tak podobná, že věřím tomu, že co se povede prožít v hudbě mě, k tomu může dojít i posluchač.

A svět, který je z tvarů a forem, svět platoniků, je prostředkem a prostředním dílem pro sdílení, pro milování druhého a druhým zpět.

Stát se jen takovým číslem...

body.body: <div class= 'text-justify'>\n\n      Nadie cree que el utility del infield venezolano Miguel Rojas, uno de los héroes de los Dodgers en la pasada serie mundial, vaya a poseer una placa en Cooperstown, NY. Pero sí podemos asegurar que nunca será olvidado en Los Ángeles, una de las ciudades más populosas del mundo. Los esquivadores andan de visita en Denver y ayer le dieron una sufrida derrota a los Rockies, aprovechando la altura de la ciudad. Cinco vuelacercas salieron de los bates angelinos y uno de ellos, fue largado por \
en la parte alta de la segunda entrada, haciendo un \

junto a Muncy. Ambos jonrones significaron la ventaja de una carrera, porque los Dodgers iban abajo 1-0 en el marcador. Miguel se fue de 3-3 con dos impulsadas y una anotada. Uno de esos imparables fue el número 1000 en su carrera, convirtiéndose en el 17mo. venezolano en coleccionar esa cantidad de imparables y un anillo de serie mundial. Muchos otros han acumulado esa cifra sin ganar un título. Enhorabuena Miguel. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Nobody thinks Venezuelan utility man Miguel Rojas, one of the Dodgers' clutch heroes from the last Fall Classic, is punching a ticket to Cooperstown. But you can bet your life he’ll never be forgotten in LA. The Blue Crew is currently hitting the road in Denver, and yesterday they handed the Rockies a tough L, making the most of that thin Mile High air. The Dodgers launched five moonshots, and one of those long balls was a no-doubter by 'Miggy Ro' in the top of the second, going back-to-back with Muncy. Those two jacks flipped the script since the Dodgers were trailing 1-0. Miguel went 3-for-3 with two ribbies and a run scored. One of those knocks was his 1,000th career hit, making him the 17th Venezuelan to join the 1K-hit club with a World Series ring to boot. Plenty of guys have put up those numbers without ever winning a chip. Tip of the cap to you, Miguel.

# ---

![Rojas.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23xARAQECBZq52vYcHRMscTe8HoxX1cfvQE5ETuv4BS8va53EaSmkJTmnKX94vpKxrgAN.jpg) Screenshot from [video](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/dodgers-vs-rockies/2026/04/20/824370/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
#
     Alguien a quien no nos hemos referido mucho en lo que va de zafra, ha sido al segunda base criollo de los Astros, José Altuve. Quizás porque no se ha visto envuelto mucho en las pocas victorias de los siderales, teniendo sin embargo, aportes al equipo en las derrotas. Antier le ganaron a San Luis para evitar la barrida y en ese partido, el pequeño gigante bateó 3 imparables y con uno de ellos, alcanzó los 220 juegos de 3 o más hits, superando al histórico e inolvidable oropéndola Eddie Murray (54.º de todos los tiempos en este departamento). Con Altuve, las probabilidades de subir al templo de los inmortales han crecido muchísimo. Tanto que, parece más bien cuestión de tiempo que de certeza. Se encuentra a un juego de superar los 2000 encuentros con los Astros, para convertirse en el tercer jugador de la franquicia en superar esa cantidad, junto a Jeff Bagwell y Craig Biggio miembros del salón de la fama. Su contrato expira en 2029, por lo que le quedan asegurados al menos 350 encuentros para superar a Bagwell (2150) en cantidad de partidos con los siderales. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

      One guy we haven’t been chirping about much this campaign is the Astros' Venezuelan keystone man, Jose Altuve. Maybe it’s because he hasn't been the main story in the few W's Houston has scratched out, even though he’s been produced in their losses. The other day, they took down St. Louis to avoid the broom, and in that contest, the 'Little Giant' collected three knocks. With that performance, he notched his 220th career 3-hit game, passing the legendary Hall of Famer Eddie Murray for 54th on the all-time list. With Altuve, his chances of getting a first-ballot nod for the Shrine are sky-high—at this point, it’s a matter of 'when,' not 'if.' He’s just one game away from hitting the 2,000-game mark with the Stros, joining icons Jeff Bagwell and Craig Biggio as the only players in franchise history to reach that milestone. His contract runs through 2029, so he’s a lock to log at least another 350 games and pass Baggy (2,150) for games played in a Houston uniform.

# ---

![Altuve.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wWy2rZ43LrVawq7qjNZjrjs9m9FEvXTsyG45Fzc9kbfvEvYw9iuNaKnWv9tSoMDHaqa.jpg) Screenshot from [Source](https://www.mlb.com/es/astros/video/game/824205) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     Junto a Derek Jeter, Willie Mays, Paul Molitor y Roberto Alomar (todos en el salón de la fama), es uno de los jugadores de pelota que ha alcanzado la combinación acumulada de élite: +2,000 hits, +400 dobles, +250 jonrones, +300 bases robadas y un promedio vitalicio superior a AVE .300. Ésta temporada se ha visto beneficiado por una zona de strike más delineada, por causa de la implementación del sistema ABS (Automatic Balls & Strikes) y de su estatura, lo que ha redundado en la elevación de su tasa de base por bolas recibidas a 16.5% (la más alta de su carrera). Sólo le faltan 6 juegos de 3 o más imparables para superar el registro de los Astros en juegos de ésta naturaleza, en poder de Craig Biggio (225) y no dudamos que le alcanzará. Un discreto AVE de .281 revela un comienzo fuerte que se ha frenado un poco en los últimos partidos, pero estamos seguros que aumentará conforme se vaya la primavera boreal y el verano asome su calor en el horizonte. Tanto como su elección segura al salón de los inmortales. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Alongside Derek Jeter, Willie Mays, Paul Molitor, and Roberto Alomar (all Hall of Famers), he’s part of an elite club with a career line of 2,000+ knocks, 400+ doubles, 250+ bombs, 300+ swiped bags, and a lifetime average north of .300. This season, he’s been getting a boost from a tighter strike zone thanks to the ABS system (Automatic Balls & Strikes) and his small frame, which has spiked his walk rate to a career-high 16.5%. He’s only six 3-hit games away from breaking Craig Biggio’s franchise record (225), and there’s no doubt he’ll catch him. While his current .281 BA shows a hot start that’s cooled off lately, we’re betting those numbers will climb once the weather heats up and the dog days of summer arrive. He’s a lock for Cooperstown.

---

![Narváez.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wqiMyEJSPyxT6ddMe7aGi2hV877EJzqekbtKekuiYrg61rFspcBXLWs4PZGDG3N8ReF.jpg) Screenshot from [Source](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/tigers-vs-red-sox/2026/04/20/824776/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     El receptor criollo de los Medias Rojas de Boston, Carlos Narváez, ha tenido un comienzo lento. Eso no quiere decir que el chico no haya aportado al movimiento de carreras de su equipo en lo que va de campaña y un ejemplo palpable fue el partido de ayer. En la parte baja del segundo episodio, el tipo tocó la pelota perfectamente, para provocar un mal tiro del lanzador a tercera, queriendo evitar la carrera del corredor. No pudo. Al internarse la pelota en la zona de foul, Narváez aprovechó para meterse hasta segunda. Luego, en el sexto, hizo algo que nadie esperaba: se robó la tercera base. No es conocido por hacer eso. pero funcionó y anotó la carrera impulsado por hit de Roman Anthony, lo que empataba el partido a 3 rayitas por lado. Al final, los \

anotaron carreras en los tres últimos tramos para llevarse el triunfo por 8 carreras a 6. Algo esperanzador dado que jugaban contra la maquinaria de Detroit y estos muchachos no pueden permitirse seguir alejándose de los demás equipos de su división. Eso esperamos. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     The Red Sox' Venezuelan backstop, Carlos Narvaez, has been off to a slow start. That doesn’t mean the kid hasn’t been chipping in to the team's run production this campaign, and yesterday’s game was a prime example. In the bottom of the second, the guy laid down a perfect bunt, forcing a throwing error from the pitcher trying to nail the runner at third. No dice. As the ball rattled into foul territory, Narvaez took advantage and swiped second. Then, in the sixth, he pulled a rabbit out of the hat: he stole third base. He’s not exactly known for his wheels, but it worked, and he came around to score on a base knock by Roman Anthony, knotting the game at three apiece. In the end, the Sox poured it on in the final three frames to secure an 8-6 W. It’s a promising sign, especially going up against that Detroit juggernaut—these boys can’t afford to fall any further behind in the AL East standings. Let’s hope they keep it rolling.

body.title: In the Land of the Golden Stump
body.body:
In 1991, novelist Douglas Coupland wrote a book called *Generation X: Tales for an Accelerated Culture*, which helped popularize the Gen-X term that refers to the sandwich generation between baby boomers and millennials. 

I was later surprised to learn that Coupland was also an artist who has in fact produced some well known eye-catching designs, including one that consisted of painting an entire building in colourful geometric shapes.

I came across another one of his works located near a Skytrain station. It is aptly called the Golden Tree.

<center>![Golden Tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/litguru/EoPKjRwHYNj8HVU8HVxoaz5AmZbimepm5j6YuX7MB1fbhEaTTd6HYQqDyNgbtpDoCxd.jpg)</center>

<center>![Golden Tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/litguru/23y8qa3bnJiVG5TKfBj9wYKsLRsGeSC64oQZuwewfKxyEfmpJEoGhMxf4VWE1Zd9vLbzz.jpg)</center>

The way I understand it, the Golden Tree mirrors another famous landmark called [the Hollow Tree](https://stanleyparkvan.com/stanley-park-van-tree-hollow.html) in Stanley Park. That tree is the shell of a Western red cedar that began its journey of growth 800 years ago, but is now just a hollowed out wooden stump. 

<center>![Golden Tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/litguru/23xoymREZBkB976Xs4oXKkTa33ytUx4jKDG9fSeTR3NUxyccEpaEmgTqEnv2WeKuGEwZP.jpg)</center>

As far as the deeper meaning of the art, that I'm not sure about. I read references to the tree representing the evolving city, and the natural environment that we inhabit, but I better not get any deeper than that, or I might end up summoning the tree elves.

<center>![Golden Tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/litguru/Eq9SucwKyJAiGWCXUpvk8u7q78dMPufu1vP4mzfGXmkE5qRSZy6JpVmAazRSHwB9fD3.jpg)</center>

body.title: Desde la oscuridad,Esp- Ing.
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmahEzvzhvxNQq5CrgtYdiFRLnJBTgimW3tCWQLX2LEtkk/1776790107512.jpg)


Desde la oscuridad

Caminamos en el astral en sueños sin sentido, mientras el corazón en automático con sus irónicos latidos nos recuerda que estamos vivos.

Sin diferencia en estar despiertos o dormidos, así caminamos mundos paralelos o tal vez mundos que ya existieron.

Así vemos la luz estando en la oscuridad, mirando la mentira que parece ser verdad. La vida se va tan rápido como reloj sin detenerse y sin reconocerse. Tu reflejo en el espejo te enseña que no estás viejo, solo te falta poder entenderte.

Gracias por leerme.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXXH2Wt7bNsJ6ahQsEpniXWiV61FMREdYFHLxuh17w4tB/1776790409174.jpg)


Traducción al ingles por google translate. 

Title: From the Darkness

From the Darkness

We walk in the astral realm through meaningless dreams,
while the heart, on automatic with its ironic beats,
reminds us that we are alive.

No difference between being awake or asleep,
so we walk through parallel worlds,
or perhaps worlds that already existed.

Thus we see the light while being in darkness,
looking at the lie that seems to be truth.
Life passes as fast as a clock without stopping,
and without recognizing yourself.
Your reflection in the mirror teaches you
that you are not old —
you just need to understand yourself.

Thank you for reading me.

body.body: >This is one of my Brawl Battles from today, featuring the newly introduced Eggceleration ruleset, alongside Aim True and Heavy Hitters. I particularly liked Aim True because it guarantees that no attack will miss—essentially granting every card a \

ability. However, what truly captured my attention was the Eggceleration ruleset; thanks to this rule, starting from the second round, the stats of every card remaining on the battlefield increase by +1. This means that the longer you manage to survive on the battlefield, the more powerful your units become. Consequently, adhering to a specific strategy, my first move was to select Dragon Archon Akane; her ability allowed me to grant the Ambush trait to two of my attackers, thereby creating the potential to inflict significant damage upon the opponent even before the actual battle had officially begun.

>Following that, the enemy didn't even get a moment to catch their breath. Although one of my cards was knocked out, I had included it in the team specifically to absorb one of the enemy's attacks—so that outcome didn't matter at all. Aside from that, however, you can see that all my other cards remained firmly in place, while the enemy's cards were knocked out one after another, ultimately allowing me to win <a target=\

>the battle.🔥 If there is a lesson to be learned from this, it is that strategy cannot be predetermined; before a battle even begins, the specific ruleset and Mana Cap dictate which moves are viable on that particular battlefield and which are not. Had I stuck to my usual, go-to strategy, I wouldn't have even considered using \

and my team likely wouldn't have consisted of more than two cards, as the cards required for that specific strategy typically carry a Mana cost of over 10. The bottom line, then, is this: before a battle commences, analyze the ruleset, check the Mana Cap, and only then decide which cards to assemble for your team.😎

\n\n

# Learn Zig Series (#25) - Mini Project: HTTP Status Checker

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

### What will I learn
- You will learn building a CLI tool that checks if URLs are reachable;
- You will learn TCP connection and basic HTTP/1.1 request construction;
- You will learn parsing HTTP response status codes from raw bytes;
- You will learn command-line argument parsing with `std.process.argsAlloc()`;
- You will learn concurrent checking with a thread pool;
- You will learn timeout handling for slow or unresponsive servers;
- You will learn colored terminal output for pass/fail results;
- You will learn tying together networking, strings, error handling, and I/O from previous episodes.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

### Difficulty
- Intermediate

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Zig Series`):
- [Zig Programming Tutorial - ep001 - Intro](https://hive.blog/programming/@scipio/zig-programming-tutoroial-ep001-intro)

- [Learn Zig Series (#4) - Error Handling (Zig's Best Feature)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature)

- [Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig)

# Learn Zig Series (#25) - Mini Project: HTTP Status Checker

Welcome back! In [episode 24](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-24-logging-formatting-and-debug-output) we covered logging, formatting, and debug output -- `std.log` with scoped loggers, `std.fmt` format specifiers, custom `format()` methods on structs, `bufPrint`, and compile-time format string validation. I gave you three exercises: a Money formatter, a TablePrinter, and a hexDump function. Let's look at those solutions first, and then we're building something real today.

This is a **mini project episode**. We're taking everything we've learned across the last 24 episodes -- networking from [episode 21](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets), string handling from [episode 5](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-5-arrays-slices-and-strings), error handling from [episode 4](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature), structs from [episode 6](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions), formatting from [episode 24](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-24-logging-formatting-and-debug-output) -- and combining them into one useful CLI tool: an HTTP status checker. You give it a list of URLs, it checks each one and tells you if it's alive or dead, with colored output and concurrency. This is the kind of tool you'd actually use in the real world (I have a similar thing in Python that I run against my own server list regularly). Here we go!

## Solutions to Episode 24 Exercises

**Exercise 1** -- Money struct with custom formatting:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{result});
}
```

The key trick is converting cents to absolute value first, handling the sign separately. That way you get `-$5.00` instead of `$-5.00` or worse. The `{d:0>2}` for the remainder guarantees two digits after the decimal point -- so 5 cents prints as `.05`, not `.5`.

**Exercise 2** -- TablePrinter:

```zig
const std = @import(\

;
    try hexDump(test_data, stderr);
}
```

The classic hexdump format: 8-character hex offset on the left, 16 hex bytes in the middle (split into two groups of 8 with an extra space), and printable ASCII on the right with dots for non-printable bytes. This is literally the same format as `xxd` or `hexdump -C` -- if you've ever debugged a network protocol or a binary file format, you've stared at output exactly like this.

Alright, solutions done. Time to build something ;-)

## The project: what are we building?

We're building `httpcheck` -- a command-line tool that takes a list of URLs and checks whether each one is alive. For each URL it opens a TCP connection, sends a minimal HTTP/1.1 GET request, reads the response status code, and reports the result with colored terminal output. Green for success (2xx), yellow for redirect (3xx), red for error (4xx/5xx), and a timeout indicator for servers that don't respond.

Why HTTP specifically? Because HTTP is the protocol that glues the entire internet together, and building a minimal HTTP client from raw TCP sockets teaches you more about networking than any library ever could. We already built TCP sockets in [episode 21](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets) -- now we layer HTTP on top.

Here's the usage we're targeting:

```
$ ./httpcheck http://example.com http://httpbin.org/status/404 http://10.255.255.1
[200] http://example.com           -- OK (124ms)
[404] http://httpbin.org/status/404 -- Not Found (89ms)
[---] http://10.255.255.1          -- Connection timed out (3000ms)
```

We'll build this step by step: URL parsing, TCP connection with timeout, HTTP request construction, response parsing, colored output, and then tying it all together.

## URL parsing: extracting host, port, and path

Before we can connect to anything, we need to break a URL like `http://example.com:8080/some/path` into its parts: the scheme (http), the host (example.com), the port (8080), and the path (/some/path). We're only handling plain HTTP here -- HTTPS requires TLS which is a whole different beast.

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{url})` and get a readable breakdown.

## TCP connection with timeout

Next up: actually connecting to the server. We did raw TCP in [episode 21](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets), but back then we didn't worry about timeouts. In the real world, some servers don't respond (firewalled, down, blackholed) and you can't wait forever. Zig's `std.net.tcpConnectToHost` does DNS resolution and connection in one call, and we can set socket options for read/write timeouts after connecting.

```zig
const std = @import(\

This is the same mechanism you'd use in C, Python's `socket.settimeout()`, or any other language -- it's all the same OS call underneath.

## Building the HTTP/1.1 request

HTTP/1.1 requests are just ASCII text over TCP. The minimal format is:

```
GET /path HTTP/1.1\r\n
Host: hostname\r\n
Connection: close\r\n
\r\n
```

That's it. Three lines plus a blank line to end the headers. `Connection: close` tells the server we're not keeping the connection alive -- send us the response and we're done. Let's build this:

```zig
fn sendHttpRequest(stream: net.Stream, host: []const u8, path: []const u8) !void {
    var buf: [1024]u8 = undefined;
    const request = try std.fmt.bufPrint(&buf, \
body:
pattern -- fan out the work, wait for everyone to finish, process the results.

For 5-10 URLs this approach is perfectly fine. For hundreds of URLs you'd want a thread pool with a fixed number of worker threads and a queue of jobs, but that's overkill for a diagnostic tool. Keep it simple until the simple approach doesn't work anymore.

## The complete program

Let me show you the complete `main.zig` with everything wired together. I've organized it into logical sections so you can follow the structure:

```zig
const std = @import(\

);
    run_step.dependOn(&run_cmd.step);
}
```

If you remember our build system episode ([episode 15](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig)), this is a standard executable build with a `run` step. Compile with `zig build` and run with `zig build run -- http://example.com http://httpbin.org/status/404`. The `--` separates build system arguments from program arguments.

## What we built and why it matters

This mini project touched pretty much every major Zig concept we've covered so far:

- **Structs** ([ep6](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions)) for `UrlParts`, `CheckResult`, `Ansi`, `ThreadContext`
- **Tagged unions** ([ep6](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions)) for `ConnectResult`
- **Error handling** ([ep4](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature)) with `catch` blocks returning early on every failure path
- **String/slice operations** ([ep5](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-5-arrays-slices-and-strings)) for URL parsing, response scanning
- **Memory management** ([ep7](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators)) with `GeneralPurposeAllocator` and `defer`
- **Formatting** ([ep24](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-24-logging-formatting-and-debug-output)) with `bufPrint`, format specifiers, custom `format()` on UrlParts
- **Networking** ([ep21](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets)) with `tcpConnectToHost` and raw socket I/O
- **Build system** ([ep15](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig)) for compiling into a proper binary

The point of a mini project is to show that these concepts don't exist in isolation -- they compose. A real program isn't \

. It's all of them, working together, in a way that feels natural once you've internalized each piece individually. If you could follow this code without getting lost, you're further along than you might think.

The tool is also genuinely useful. I have a similar script in Python (using `requests`) that I run against a list of servers every morning. The Zig version does the same thing but compiles to a single static binary with zero dependencies. Copy it to any Linux box and it runs. No Python, no pip, no virtualenv, no Docker. Just one file.

## Possible extensions

If you want to keep building on this project, here are some ideas:

- **HTTPS support**: Zig's standard library includes `std.crypto.tls` for TLS connections. Adding HTTPS means upgrading the TCP stream to a TLS stream before sending the HTTP request. The HTTP protocol itself stays identical -- TLS is transparent at the transport layer.

- **Concurrent checking with a thread pool**: Our current version checks URLs sequentially. Spawning a thread per URL (as we showed in the concurrency section) would make it much faster when checking many targets. You could take the `std.Thread.spawn` approach and join all threads before printing results.

- **JSON output mode**: Add a `--json` flag that outputs results as a JSON array instead of colored text. We covered JSON in [episode 20](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-20-working-with-json) -- you could use `std.json.stringifyAlloc` or build the JSON manually with `bufPrint`.

- **Config file**: Read URLs from a file in stead of command-line arguments. File I/O from [episode 10](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io) plus our `LineIterator` from [episode 23](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-23-iterators-and-lazy-evaluation) would make this straightforward.

- **Follow redirects**: When you get a 301/302 response, parse the `Location` header and check the redirect target. That's just more byte scanning on the response headers.

Each of these extensions exercises something we've already covered. The foundation is solid -- building on it is just more of the same patterns applied to new problems.

## Dus, wat hebben we nou geleerd?

- **URL parsing** is just byte scanning -- find the scheme, the host, the optional port, and the path. No external library needed.
- **TCP connection with timeout** uses `tcpConnectToHost` for the connection and `setsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` for the read timeout. Standard POSIX socket options.
- **HTTP/1.1 requests** are ASCII text: `GET /path HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: hostname\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`. That's literally all you need for a basic GET.
- **Status code parsing** means scanning the response for the three digits after the first space. Defensive parsing returns `null` for anything malformed.
- **ANSI escape codes** give you colored terminal output: `\x1b[32m` for green, `\x1b[31m` for red, `\x1b[0m` to reset. Works everwhere.
- **Thread-based concurrency** with `std.Thread.spawn` lets you check multiple URLs in parallel. One thread per URL, collect results after joining.
- **The mini project pattern**: real programs combine structs, error handling, string processing, networking, formatting, and memory management all in one place. If you can follow this code, you can build real tools in Zig.

This was our second mini project (the first was the step sequencer in [episode 11](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-11-mini-project-building-a-step-sequencer)), and it's a good checkpoint. We've covered Zig's core language features, its standard library data structures, networking, formatting, and now built a practical tool with them. Going forward we'll start exploring lower-level territory -- custom allocators, C interop, inline assembly, and more system-level programming. The groundwork is laid ;-)

De groeten!

@scipio

body.title: Montague Summers, an Expert on Monsters
body.body:
/>

If you browse the catalog of the American publisher **Dover**, known for reissuing out-of-print and unusual books, you’ll find new editions of some unique **texts on witches, vampires, and werewolves**.

These thoroughly documented studies on monsters were written by a rather strange figure—someone who could also be described as a wolf in sheep’s clothing: **Montague Summers**.

Born in **England**, he even took vows to become an **Anglican pastor**. But he was accused of pedophilia, so he resigned and converted to **Catholicism**.

Although he could easily be mistaken for a Catholic priest, the Church never recognized him as one. The thing is, **Summers** was ordained in 1909 by **Bishop Ulric Vernon Herford**, who had been removed from the Church more than 40 years earlier for not following Roman doctrine.

So Summers dressed like a priest and called himself a reverend, but it seems he wasn’t really one. Meanwhile, he devoted most of his life to studying and writing about witches and the occult.

It’s said he had dealings with **Aleister Crowley** (also known as **The Great Beast**), and that the admiration between them was mutual.

Summers, whose sexuality was often questioned, has been accused of taking part in **diabolical rites**. One of the main reasons for his fame is that he produced the first English translation of the **_Malleus Maleficarum_**, the misogynistic manual on witchcraft that became a go-to book for inquisitors during a witch hunt that lasted 300 years and led to countless deaths in the Middle Ages, especially of women.

Even though some circles still admire Summers’ “immense erudition,” it’s worth keeping in mind that his books do little more than reinforce belief in superstitions that, for centuries, have caused far more ignorance and suffering than any real benefit or meaningful idea.

\-- _This article was originally published in Spanish on my blog._

So I ended up capturing things that naturally drew my attention. > बाज़ार जाते समय मैं तस्वीरें लेना चाहती थी, लेकिन समझ नहीं आ रहा था कि क्या क्लिक करूं। इसलिए जो भी चीज़ें अपने आप मेरा ध्यान खींचती गईं, उन्हें ही कैमरे में कैद कर लिया। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPZLwTZfUgmUbxFv94k7a7rKcZDoR1oQLCdGeZfW2CoTJ/img_2807.heic) First photo is of two people walking uphill on a quiet street.Shops were closed, wires were crisscrossing above, and sunlight was falling from one side as it was a few hours before sunset. > पहली तस्वीर में दो लोग एक शांत सड़क पर ऊपर की ओर चलते हुए दिख रहे हैं।दुकानें बंद थीं, ऊपर तार आपस में उलझे हुए थे, और एक तरफ़ से धूप पड़ रही थी क्योंकि यह सूर्यास्त से कुछ घंटे पहले का समय था। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRxemR3NF2GaS7FAvTee1Yec5hUcgjBpANqFB8sMUf2wK/img_2808.heic) Two men were walking together, carrying bags.One was older, using a walking stick, the other younger.It looked like a simple moment of companionship and routine. >दो आदमी साथ-साथ चल रहे थे, उनके हाथों में बैग थे।एक उम्रदराज़ था और लाठी का सहारा ले रहा था, दूसरा उससे छोटा था।यह एक साधारण सा साथ और रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी का पल लग रहा था। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSEc2XLWJyJYGzAzEm8gPX26gtxFs379VTHdC3VMdFLFh/img_2811.heic) A little ahead both parted wags now the elderly man was walking alone on a road. Trees and shadows surrounded him. I feel this moment had a slightly emotional feeling. >थोड़ा आगे जाकर दोनों अलग हो गए और अब वह बुज़ुर्ग आदमी सड़क पर अकेले चल रहा था।चारों तरफ़ पेड़ और उनकी परछाइयाँ थीं। मुझे यह पल थोड़ा भावुक सा लगा। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWqWMR52oayePPVrefkVXtNdJDpQrekAcXJPrGDZNRYw4/img_2813.heic) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZv4c4bfxDLZtZgdL3pPXknTBSGueGzexK3vJqSc2WAWj/img_2814.heic) There was a small child playing with a toy car. He was asking people to clear the street so his little car could pass. He was quite energetic and it was a moment of growing up. > वहाँ एक छोटा बच्चा खिलौने की कार से खेल रहा था।वह लोगों से कह रहा था कि रास्ता खाली करें ताकि उसकी छोटी कार निकल सके। वह काफी ऊर्जावान था, और यह एक छोटे-से बड़े होने जैसा पल लगा। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdGLiZ85mmdABdFtqHLcqkv8SgMQco89LGPjwe5GrQg8B/img_2826.heic) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR7zbkqBtjv6P25Q2jtKDXp4Bu8tcrK6gxcHkkizRB2AE/img_2827.heic) Lastly, I captured a photo of a white langur sitting on a tree branch. I was a bit scared to take the shot since they can sometimes get aggressive, but I still managed to click it and felt really happy afterward. > आख़िर में, मैंने एक ग्रे लंगूर की तस्वीर ली, जो पेड़ की एक डाल पर बैठा था।उसे फोटो में कैद करते समय मुझे थोड़ा डर लग रहा था क्योंकि वे कभी-कभी आक्रामक हो जाते हैं, लेकिन फिर भी मैंने हिम्मत करके तस्वीर ले ली और बाद में बहुत खुशी महसूस हुई। That’s all for today folks. Happy snapping. 💜💙 Thankyou for visiting 🌸 > आज के लिए बस इतना ही दोस्तों। तस्वीरें लेने का आनंद लें। 💜💙 आने के लिए धन्यवाद 🌸

body.title: Remote Engineering/Tech Job opportunity
body.body:
![243305.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/244UxEWyCamKoV1uWmsSDBCTdzez8XVEQjgVssP2PqwpUUh92GXuh73A6DqGg6BXHTiMW.png)



<hr>

I have some who is strongly looking for remote tech job opportunities. They were previously contributing to some projects but couldn't continue because of their education but after their education they haven't been able to find projects like that. 


The company he worked for employed more people after he left and since he couldn't get back to the job after school. It was a great job, and the company was based overseas and was good for the portfolio. 


I'm not a tech guy, but I do a lot of research, and I found a lot of opportunities for this person but so far, none of this jobs has clicked. We've applied through Fiverr, linkedin, and other platforms, but so far we've not got anything positive. 



I understand that it's a saturated market, but even as at that many companies are still putting up remote, physical and hybrid opportunities and don't seem to be taking a lot of people, or perhaps they're being selective in the opportunities they're offering. 


Also I believe these people/tech companies gets a lot of offer on a daily and they might find it difficult to scrutinize who is qualified or not. The person I'm talking about is qualified, has worked many firms and many other tech gigs as well. 


### AI is making it difficult 

AI is taking over many tech gigs, this is true, Infact most tech companies based in Europe and US are leveraging on AI, paid versions to actually run some of their protocols without needing the help of real people.

 However they still need software bros to coordinate their workflow, they still need paid interns, lead engineers and all that. So these opportunities are there, but they're beginning to leverage the paid versions of the likes of GEMINI or CHATGPT to run some of their minor code. 

However if a company salary budget is $5M a year for example, with AI this might be reduced to $3 a year, saving a massive $2M in the process.


 No company will choose to overpay if they have the easy way out, no matter how much they make in a year, I'll be very impossible for them to choose to overpay. 

For example YouTube makes $60B in a year, and maybe pays 20 to 30% of that in revenue for creators, but still they're demonitizing creators for mass producing contents or for low quality.

 Also whether a person is monetized or not, YouTube places ads on video where they see traffic and pockets all that. 

My point is no company wants to pay, and this is why the likes of CLAUDE PRO will be taking over from tech gigs and tech bros and this will render software engineers jobless. 

> Not all, but many. 


The lead software engineers and the rest are still going to have their own jobs and all that, but over 50% of regular engineers will lose their role, the remaining roles will become too competitive and then becomes saturated. 



However, if anyone knows a tech gig for a full stack engineer, I'd like to know, or if they have or know any opportunity that can work out for someone who is a full stack software bro, I'd like to know.

body.title: Next Day, Next Week, Next Year… But What Really Matters?
body.body:
Sometimes I sit and think about how much we worry about the future. Next day, next week, next month, even next year. It’s like our mind is always running ahead, trying to figure everything out before it even happens. I do it a lot too, if I’m being honest.

There was a time I couldn’t even relax properly because I was always thinking about “what’s next?” What will I do tomorrow? Will things work out next month? Where will I be next year? Those thoughts can become heavy without you noticing.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUErNNfZxFJ5HpG4BsAd8oDt6qFFrRfu2QiLhnmvA2neZ/1776789933428.jpg)[source](https://unsplash.com/photos/woman-in-brown-and-black-jacket-sitting-on-concrete-bench-during-daytime-iX_OPtDa7IU)

My parents used to look at life in a simpler way. My mother would say, “Face today well, tomorrow will come on its own.” I didn’t really like that advice back then. It felt too basic. I wanted something more detailed, something that could guarantee a better future.

But life has a way of teaching you slowly.

I started to notice that no matter how much I worried about the future, it didn’t really change anything. Tomorrow still came the way it wanted. Some days good, some days not so good. So I began to shift my thinking, little by little.

What really matters, I’m starting to understand, is what you do now.

Not in a big dramatic way, just small things. How you use your time today. The effort you put into what you’re doing. The way you treat people around you. These little actions don’t look important in the moment, but they quietly shape what tomorrow becomes.

My father once told me, “The future is just many small days put together.” That line stayed with me. Because it made me realize that next week or next year is not something far away, it is built from what I’m doing right now.

Of course, planning is still important. You can’t just ignore the future completely. But overthinking it too much can steal your peace today. And if today is not handled well, tomorrow might not be as good as you expect.

I still think about the future, I won’t lie. But I try not to let it control me too much.

Right now, I’m learning to focus on the present more. Do what I can today, even if it’s small. Improve little by little.

Because maybe what really matters is not how far ahead we think… but how well we live the moment we are in.

body.title: Encouraging the youth || MCGI topic review
body.body:
Greetings!

https://youtu.be/_O85f0adFYM?si=EX7ny60n8DymHHYi

Hi everyone, I'm happy to review the word of God has  spoken or preached by God's servant, Bro. Eli Soriano and I'm very sure we will all be a beneficiary of the undiluted word of God.

We live in a time where many young people feel lost, lacking clear direction and purpose. It can often seem as though the world is working against them. But the question remains—how can we help them understand that there is still hope, and that their lives can still produce something meaningful and fruitful?

Many bright and promising youths are being led astray due to the challenges around them—family background, societal pressure, or the influence of those they associate with. These factors can easily push them off the right path.

However, we must remember that youths are the future of our families, churches, and nation. Even when they struggle to meet expectations, they should not be written off. Instead, they need continuous encouragement and guidance, reminding them that success is still possible despite life’s difficulties.

From my perspective, a young person truly discovers purpose when they begin to make themselves useful—first to themselves, then to God, and ultimately to their families and society. Purpose brings clarity, and clarity leads to growth.

Young people should not be left to figure everything out on their own. While they may appear mature, they still need guidance, support, and correction from time to time. Encouragement should come not only when they are doing well but also when they are struggling or going off track.

Thank you for reading.

body.title: ADDICTION A TOOL FOR GROWTH OR DESTRUCTION
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdoUfaKk9y3uMnHiVKAQRt2hELWCu6MmgctMNckUyZCdc/Gemini_Generated_Image_9b16kb9b16kb9b16.png 

image generated using Geminin AI

A habit is tagged good when it brings about growth, self-development and makes your life and health better, a good activity can become bad for someone when it affects them negatively and when they cannot do without it, it becomes a bad addiction, whereas, when a person seems not to be able to do without a certain activity or substance and the said activity or substance enhances the person's life in return, that can be seen as a positive or good addiction. 

It is usually said that too much of everything is bad, when someone is too good, while this also can be tagged as to be bad, I believe that it can only be seen as bad only when it affects the person negatively, something can be too much and still good for a person, so long as it adds to one’s life and does not subtract to it. For instance, a person who is good and puts others before himself may have behaviours that negatively affect them when they don't take care of themselves, take care of others, and forget themselves. When this behaviour makes one have a sense of purpose and social connection, to that person, the act of selflessness or putting others first can be seen as good. It is noble to put others first, but whenever we do so, we should try not to neglect ourselves in the process. A person who is not healthy, for instance, may not fend for another who is ill; this is what separates good addiction from a bad one.

A good addiction could be one where a person develops a hunger for new information, trying to always learn new things or develop new skills, looking for new information through studying, keeping the brain always active and engaged. A person who is addicted to watching educational and informative movies will also see their addiction as a positive or good addiction since it helps them learn and stay informed.

An activity in the end is a positive addiction when it makes one better than what they were, where there is a sense of self-development, mentally, professionally, socially or otherwise. While a bad addiction is one that only takes from you and does not give, and is a part of your destruction.

The theme is entirely school-related, so I designed it with the little ones or their teachers in mind; but it can also serve as inspiration for you to create your own design, completely to your liking. I thought about grouping a couple of pencils together, and for the other idea, I came up with a little apple; I don't think I've ever made a design like this before.</center>

> **🔸Without more to add, then I leave you with the step by step:**

---

<center>![portada defi.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EoGyx4FP7fbnUBh9VZuTXirYxVpzWSu2hSq2tHJdCfFA56k66u1jnoqssAnWM7fsEAL.JPG)</center>

---

<div class=\

> **♥️ESPERO QUE TE GUSTE, ¡Empecemos!**
**♥️I HOPE YOU LIKE IT, Let's start!**
---
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> - Foami escarchado rosa. - Foami amarillo. - Foami azul. - Foami lila. - Foami crema. - Foami gris. - Foami rojo. - Foami verde. - Foami blanco. - Foami marrón. - Pinturas y marcadores. - Pegamento. - Tijeras. - Regla. - Hoja blanca. - Lápiz.
- Pink glitter foam. - Yellow foam. - Blue foam. - Lilac foam. - Cream foam. - Gray foam. - Red foam. - Green foam. - White foam. - Brown foam. - Paints and markers. - Glue. - Scissors. - Ruler. - White paper. - Pencil.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 1: Lo primero, como siempre, es tomar una hoja blanca y comenzar a plasmar nuestra idea o ideas y decidirnos por la que más nos guste. En este caso, ya les dije al inicio que mi idea era hacer elementos escolares o cosas relacionadas con esto. Es por eso que al final pensé en hacer un grupo de crayones y un lápiz en medio, agarrados de un lazo como primer diseño, y para el otro, pensé en algo más básico, como una manzana, bastante sencilla, pero ambos diseños tenían como extra una pequeña margarita. Al tener lista la idea, transferimos a los colores correspondientes de foami, como explico a continuación: ✨Cuerpo de lápiz: 4 cm x 1.8 cm en foami amarillo. ✨Cuerpo de crayones: 5.2 cm x 1.8 cm en foami lila y azul. ✨Puntas: 2 cm x 1.6 cm en foami crema. ✨Metal del lápiz: 2 cm x 0.5 mm en foami gris. ✨Borrador: 2 cm x 1 cm en foami rojo. ✨Lazo: 5.5 cm x 2.5 cm, 4 cm x 3 cm y 2 cm x 1.5 cm en foami rosa y escarchado rosa. ✨Manzana: 5.5 cm x 4.5 cm en foami rojo. ✨Tallo: 2.8 cm x 0.8 mm en foami marrón. ✨Hoja: 2.5 cm x 1.8 cm en foami verde. ✨Flores: 2.5 cm y 1 cm en foami blanco y amarillo.

> ###### ✨STEP 1: The first step, as always, is to take a blank sheet of paper and start sketching out our idea or ideas, then decide on the one we like best. In this case, as I mentioned at the beginning, my idea was to make school supplies or things related to school. That's why I ended up thinking of making a group of crayons and a pencil in the middle, tied together with a ribbon, as the first design. For the second, I thought of something more basic, like an apple—quite simple. But both designs included a small daisy as an extra touch. Once we had the idea ready, we transferred it to the corresponding colors of foam, as I explain below: ✨Pencil body: 4 cm x 1.8 cm in yellow foam. ✨Crayon body: 5.2 cm x 1.8 cm in lilac and blue foam. ✨Tips: 2 cm x 1.6 cm in cream foam. ✨Pencil metal: 2 cm x 0.5 mm in gray foam. ✨Eraser: 2 cm x 1 cm in red foam. Bow: 5.5 cm x 2.5 cm, 4 cm x 3 cm, and 2 cm x 1.5 cm in pink and pink glitter foam. ✨Apple: 5.5 cm x 4.5 cm in red foam. ✨Stem: 2.8 cm x 0.8 mm in brown foam. ✨Leaf: 2.5 cm x 1.8 cm in green foam. ✨Flowers: 2.5 cm and 1 cm in white and yellow foam.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260410_105741.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EogRjU3iq9AqCLfoQeWH9QE9CQkwvuoaW5ee9NHYR9S12Yc3mJVNneyBouQWx8Pu257.jpg)|![IMG_20260410_105813.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EogQGcSENndunLQ3Txxc4HAeomYyEXqKUfW5cNqFUdAVi4dPRdz7u4LkeZ7jF5iYGfP.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 2: Al estar todas las piezas recortadas y listas, es momento de dar color a los bordes, con pinturas o marcadores; en mi caso utilicé marcadores. Vamos a darle a los bordes colores que sean más oscuros o que hagan contraste; por ejemplo, en el caso de la manzana y el tallo, utilicé un color negro, mientras que para el cuerpo del lápiz utilicé un color marrón y el resto de las piezas, colores más oscuros que el de cada pieza.

> ###### ✨STEP 2: Once all the pieces are cut out and ready, it's time to color the edges with paint or markers; I used markers. Use darker or contrasting colors for the edges; for example, I used black for the apple and stem, brown for the pencil body, and darker colors for the rest of the pieces.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260410_111055.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/Eoc9tmohHXTMEAYtj3F18XRNmGZy1yR4T2GkFvFBVDs2QknTyZKPYjPTv8d5ZCKUWuW.jpg)|![IMG_20260410_111019.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/Ep7ySYJBaPdEFZNxUpLMoamJL3DE53dTr6n7CXfXgLbaRZMfH7QLobRWxSUsisDD5aF.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 3: Al estar secas las piezas, es momento de hacer los detalles más específicos, cosa que me encanta y es mi parte favorita. Así que, por ejemplo, vamos a hacer los detalles a lápiz, crayolas, definir mucho mejor el lazo y todas sus partes. En cuanto a las puntas, les di sus colores correspondientes a cada una; definimos mejor el tallo de la manzana, la hoja y todos los detalles que creamos que serían ideales para embellecer estas piezas.

> ###### ✨STEP 3: Once the pieces are dry, it's time to add the more specific details, which I love and is my favorite part. So, for example, we'll add details with pencils and crayons, refining the bow and all its parts. As for the tips, I assigned them their corresponding colors; we further defined the apple stem, the leaf, and all the details we thought would be ideal to embellish these pieces.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260410_112017.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EokgyQZfJwUaM1dfB3qBWdLvJ4MoadmgyCmKZgdMuXpimx286hctxSxrTMQteVCt3n2.jpg)|![IMG_20260410_112053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EoyRrRHH7nfwStdY2Gtrk3YXoXUjjCG7f8zwvNfF4d5bLePKq9SrwNcGJfr9GaWDi2b.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 4: Al estar todo listo, es momento de comenzar a pegar todas las piezas, hasta formar cada uno de forma individual y luego, pegamos cada una de las decoraciones al gusto. En mi caso, uní los crayones a los lados y luego, con la punta hacia abajo, el lápiz en el centro y en medio de todos, pegué el lazo y pegué también la manzana, haciendo un corte donde va el tallo para dar un mejor acabado. Finalmente, pegué las flores a cada decoración.

> ###### ✨STEP 4: When everything is ready, it's time to start gluing all the pieces together, forming each one individually. Then, we glue on each of the decorations as desired. In my case, I attached the crayons to the sides, and then, with the tip facing down, the pencil in the center. In the middle of everything, I glued the bow and the apple, making a cut where the stem goes for a neater finish. Finally, I glued the flowers to each decoration.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260410_113311.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EokeUFiCcXy2Qzoa2UJKD8Y73Bhp3MPJTxCNjSbx8S3eyqjEg3LFjua2Gy8PTBMvWzY.jpg)|![IMG_20260410_114302.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/Ep5q7aqdCFj1rLERWQvyaP8WQQLcz4xEKn8yKYMaBNeQCXWGgT6pqP2znX5joMJpdtp.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)

> ###### ✨PASO 5: Ya para finalizar, es momento de recortar dos rectángulos de 4 cm x 1 cm, damos color a los bordes y algún diseño que nos guste, pegamos formando un cilindro en la parte superior del lápiz o lapicera y en medio, pegamos las decoraciones.

> ###### ✨STEP 5: Finally, it's time to cut out two rectangles measuring 4 cm x 1 cm. Color the edges and add any design you like. Glue them together, forming a cylinder, at the top of the pencil or pen, and glue the decorations in the middle.
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
|![IMG_20260410_113849.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EpA6REaHdEEz3VC4oYPcuF8AWwxdbyAnEp5HBRDM9gJ9sMxuUufwNUZ1B7YdYdqaA3Q.jpg)|![IMG_20260410_113951.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/EpJaZB9TysbhMdj1Z1sn91iTgnGkdvnHPeuQhX6F5RcE3hwo6PzJngAVScTLb4wc5Dx.jpg)| |-|-|
![separador 2023.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valenpba/23uFnpKyJ7meMSyw1pqmfQu94TYy7tCuEmTPQy9gugnkC5oXaC7gcejs3b2EPAGmUMGRT.PNG)
✨Así es como pueden elaborar una linda y creativa decoración para los lápices o lapiceras de los pequeños. Recuerden que pueden hacerlas como gusten, ya sean las dos, una sola o el diseño que quieran. Espero que les haya gustado el paso a paso y se animen a elaborarlo.
❤️Hasta la próxima publicación.
>
✨That's how you can make a cute and creative decoration for your little ones' pencils or pens. Remember that you can make them however you like—two, just one, or any design you want. I hope you enjoyed the step-by-step instructions and are inspired to make them.
>
❤️Until the next post.

body.title: By the Ocean · Madeira, Portugal
body.body: > Prainha is one of Madeira's finest beaches — a rare spot with volcanic sand in copper and rust tones.

> While most other beaches show off pebbles or imported white sand, Prainha keeps its authentic, almost wild texture. That coppery-red sand is a direct inheritance from the island's volcanic past. And this sand has a quiet trick up its sleeve: when a wave rolls in, the water shifts color. Transparent turquoise mixes with dark grains, creating the effect of shimmering metal.

> What defines Prainha is its seclusion and a raw ocean experience: no breakwaters, no artificial barriers, just a natural entry that drops off quickly. The beach hides behind a rocky headland, tucked right beneath the road leading to the Ponta de São Lourenço peninsula, and from the sea, it's almost invisible. But in season, its location is easy to spot — a chain of parked cars lines the roadside.
> From above, a panorama opens up: a compact bay, tightly squeezed between steep cliffs.

> Prainha rightfully makes it onto lists of the island's best beaches, but it has a character all its own. The waves here are often serious, so swimming rarely turns into relaxed splashing — it's more of a straightforward encounter with the elements. But the water takes on such an intense turquoise hue that you easily forgive both the long drive to the eastern tip of the island and the seasonal influx of tourists filling nearly every free meter of sand.

> Still, once you're on the shore, you quickly understand: the cliffs around you leave no doubt that this is Madeira — a volcanic island with a rough edge. And that unvarnished reality is exactly what creates Prainha's central paradox. It's simultaneously simple and slightly inconvenient. Small, crowded in season, without resort polish — but with character. You won't find postcard perfection here, but you will get that rare sense of a place that doesn't try to meet your expectations.
> Maybe that's exactly why it's considered one of the best.

>\n
@alexanderfluke's travels

body.title: COVERED BY GOD'S GRACE.. NOT BY LEAVES!
body.body:
Greetings amazing family... 

I learnt that sometimes we often focus on the fruit, but the real tragedy was actually the clothes. In the case of Uncle Adam and Sister Eve I'm referring to.

So In Genesis 2 and 3, everything changes from complete openness to two people suddenly feeling the need to hide.


![IMG-20260419-WA0047.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johnpetra/243qEoWwxjW4TYJHxfKRChRFMFG3tMLGSdb5rLTo7Ea9G5XS4PF1GjXYtEtdyxU1GJDMe.jpg)


Before anything went wrong, the Bible says, “Adam and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.” (Genesis 2:25 NIV). They had nothing to prove and nothing to hide. They simply lived in peace.

Then they made a choice. They disobeyed God’s command. After that, they realized they were naked and began sewing fig leaves together to cover themselves. Look closely at that moment. Their first reaction was not to make things right with God. Their first reaction was to hide what they had done.

Sin makes you notice the mess that grace used to cover. And sadly, many of us react just like Adam and Eve. We try to cover instead of surrendering.

Think about it. The first thing humans ever created was not a tool or a weapon. It was something to hide behind.

The Bible does not first mention guilt. It talks about feeling exposed. They took whatever they could find and tried to build a barrier between each other. Why? Because they suddenly felt unsafe.

The deepest pain in this story is not only disobedience. It is that closeness was broken right away. They looked at the one they loved and no longer felt safe being fully seen.

![IMG-20260321-WA0005.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johnpetra/EogNm6pYZSvD7i4YWG5y1VozCVsfPGirxe2c4SQKkP7Lgrk5FMtAASbW8XvbED9uFA1.jpg)


Later, when God walks in the garden, He asks, “Where are you?” (Genesis 3:9 NIV). Of course, God knew. But the question shows that something had changed. Distance had entered the relationship.

When Adam answers, he says he was afraid because he was naked, so he hid (Genesis 3:10 NIV). He was not only hiding from God. He was also hiding from himself. He did not know how to face what he was feeling inside.

But look at God’s response. He does not leave them there in their weak covering. The Bible says, “The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.” (Genesis 3:21 NIV).

God replaced their temporary solution with something real. Even after their failure, He stepped in and cared for their need.

Many of us are still wearing our own version of fig leaves today. Is it the image you try to keep in front of others? Is it a perfect life you show at church while things are not okay at home? We think these layers protect us, but they actually keep us alone.

Maybe it is a struggle you keep hiding. Maybe you built habits just to silence the guilt.

This is not just an old story about Adam. It is a mirror of how we live now. The most dangerous moments are not always the ones people see. Sometimes it is when you are smiling but hiding pain inside.

body.title: “Bitcoin has no real use case.”
body.body:
“Bitcoin has no real use case.”
That sentence usually says more about where you live… than about Bitcoin itself.

If you live in a country where:
- your bank works 24/7
- your currency holds value
- your savings aren’t at risk overnight
- sending money is easy and cheap
Then yes… Bitcoin might feel optional.

But zoom out for a second.
For millions (actually billions) of people, reality looks very different:

- Inflation destroying savings
Argentina, Turkey, Lebanon… where holding local currency means guaranteed loss.

- Capital controls
You earned your money… but you can’t move it.

- Banking exclusion
No access to accounts, loans, or even basic financial infrastructure.

- Censorship
Accounts frozen. Payments blocked. Donations stopped.

- Remittances
Sending money home can cost 5-10%… and take days.

Now look at Bitcoin again:
- Borderless
- Permissionless
- 24/7
- Non-discriminatory
- No central point of failure

Suddenly, it’s not a “nice-to-have”. It’s financial survival infrastructure. The gap is experiential.

If you’ve never needed Bitcoin, you’re lucky.
But that doesn’t mean it’s useless.

It just means it wasn’t built for you first. 🧡

/></center>

[source](https://learning.segsa.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/LMS-BBBEE.jpeg)





At the end of January a proposal was put through by the Department of Trade, Industry and Compliance also known as the DTIC. The proposal is a real shocker and basically is an extra tax burden on every business sin South Africa.

The proposal is about creating more funding for Black Economic Empowerment (BEE) which is targeting 3% of annual business net profits after tax. What is being proposed is that all companies pay in the 3% to earn a maximum 20% BEE status points.

This is only the tip of the ice berg as the rest of the proposal is just as ludicrous. Points are awarded for businesses purchasing from black owned businesses and receive an additional 7 points. There are additional bonus point structures allowing for an additional 2 points to be earned depending on the percentage of purchases and whether those black businesses are less than 2 years old.

What this means is the government can grab an extra R100 billion from businesses and you have no say in where this goes or how it is being used. This is another ploy at stealing money where there was no money before and have made up new rules to create more wealth through \

theft.

If BEE was run out as it should in the beginning offering those a helping hand then this would not be up for discussion with the only problem it only benefitted a few and will carry on benefiting those who are already wealthy.

This is going to put even more pressure on businesses trying to force them to comply with paying the extra 3% and who they procure their products from. This is starting to look like the tender game where price has no baring and is more about who you support. Tenders in my view should be down to price and service and not paying an over the top price to another company just because of ownership as that is crooked and not how business should be done.

This is going to impact businesses like never before because companies will lose business unfairly because of the ownership and not because they offer great service with a great price. This will directly impact employment and if this gets passed which it probably will at some point because it has already been put forward. Those voting on this will no doubt be the ones in line benefitting from these new changes.

This will destroy the current supply chains and increase the cost of those products with new companies springing up offering the same services at inflated prices because businesses are being forced to use them. At the same time this will dry up investment and those invested will leave the country. This is not a fair playing field and is more racist policies that will back fire resulting in increased unemployment.

This is the problem when you have government officials who do not understand business and the effects of their decisions on the economy. Those that are wealthy may think they are businessman, but in all reality they never made their wealth through normal channels so have no understanding how a business works. When you exclude businesses from being able to grow like they would under normal circumstances or even compete then you are removing the ability to trade and that is what is going to happen.

Velocity and Acceleration as Derivatives of the Position Vector + Example of an Object moving in 2D

In this video, I show that the derivative of the position vector of a particle moving in 3D space is just the velocity, and likewise the acceleration is obtained as the derivative of the velocity. Thus, just knowing the position vector, we can obtain the velocity and acceleration vectors of the particle. And the speed of the object is obtained by calculating the magnitude or length of the velocity vector, which we can calculate via the distance formula. I go over an example of an object moving in 2D to illustrate this, as well as making an awesome calculator with GeoGebra!

links.title: What is behavioral data?
links.body:
Quick question for people who work in UX or analytics: when you say “behavioral data,” what exactly are you referring to? At first I thought it was just analytics metrics, but apparently it’s broader than that. It includes navigation paths, interactions, clicks, and other signals that show how users actually use a product. I was reading about it earlier and found this explanation pretty helpful: [what is behavioral dat](https://clay.global/blog/ux-guide/user-behavior-data)a. It breaks down the basics and how teams use behavioral insights for product decisions. Do most teams rely mostly on analytics tools for this, or do you combine it with qualitative research too?

links.title: 关于预期……
links.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![lJbR6M3yRRV1XkCM_1000026615.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/muwangxuan/images/lJbR6M3yRRV1XkCM_1000026615/lJbR6M3yRRV1XkCM_1000026615.webp)
![raPm1eh6XowWpIEO_1000026614.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/muwangxuan/images/raPm1eh6XowWpIEO_1000026614/raPm1eh6XowWpIEO_1000026614.webp)
![rylPbrxlyCo8Uqna_1000026613.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/muwangxuan/images/rylPbrxlyCo8Uqna_1000026613/rylPbrxlyCo8Uqna_1000026613.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

作为一个经常喜欢追剧的人，有时候会被推送一些新剧的上线时间。
在看完各种宣发后，我再去看那个上线时间时，心里总会情不自禁的升起要是现在时间就去到上映当天就好了。
其实也不仅仅是电影宣发或者其他的，我发现，只要是这种带有滤镜的时间，我们都会升起这种巴不得时间过快点的想法。
小时候老师给我们勾勒的上了大学就舒服了，让无数人希望快点到上大学。
等参加工作时，社会和家里人又会告诉你，买点社保，以后老了就轻松了。
有人曾说，社保对于人最大的影响，或许就是它竟然让一群风华正茂的人，放弃了对当下时间的感知，甚至巴不得快点老去，到拿养老金的那天……
可有时候想想，退休的人，又能多舒服嘛？
不一定的，要是无病无灾，且子女不说多孝顺，但至少不怎么啃老，那还行。
否则那是什么局面？子女嫌弃，养老金还不够看病的钱，这才是常态。
当然，哪怕已经知道了这点，但可惜的是，当我在看到一些宣发消息的时候，还是会升起那种希望能穿越的想法。
由此可见，人就是会被预期所左右，这或许是人的本性。
因此，很多厉害的人，都是懂得去操控预期的人。
以前我刚出社会，就是觉得老板整天就知道画大饼。
后面慢慢知道了其实这就是操控预期，当然，有的人这方面的能力比较强，有的老板就不行。
大多数老板其实也只是学到了形式，根本就没真正的去研究，画饼真的是一种能力，而且画饼不是纯画饼，是得和行为结合的。
读书时的上了大学就轻松了，其实也是一种操控预期。
大多数父母都会这么和自己孩子说。
而我一家长辈就从没这么说过，他很小的时候传递给他孩子的就是人就是得苦一辈子的，读小学苦，读中学也苦，等读了大学也轻松不了……
自然而然的，他孩子也从没有过到啥时候会轻松的，一直都很刻苦努力……
其实这就是改变了预期。
当然，每个人的育儿方式不一样，这种方法也不一定好。
只是说，它的底层逻辑，就是预期！

---
