title.title: TWELVE POSTCARDS FROM THE RENAISSANCE ROME
title.body:
I'm playing mostly the Dead Space remake these days, but late last night, I felt the need to take a break from the deep space horror, so I took a scenic walk through the streets of Rome, and I also spent some time in a small boat on the Tiber River. It was all virtual, of course; it was an excursion inside the world of the Assassin's Creed Brotherhood game.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfUBS9eeZoUA287nxvpifL8uHHJ346c3HGsQZ8gpoM78z/acbsp_2026_04_21_09_54_22.png)

I mean, my avatar inside the game is very good at jumping, climbing, and doing all kinds of crazy acrobatic stuff, so I was using the streets only to reach good spots for climbing the houses and palaces, and then spent most of my in-game time wandering across the rooftops.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQQrwmZ2q4CDnvRr2phzDmkFL3c8rVDLD391VbpdkBuXn/acbsp_2026_04_21_09_57_24.png)

The detailed reconstruction of the 16th-century city looks amazing from that elevated point of view, so I started taking screenshots like a real tourist takes snapshots with a phone.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP5ExX1aDaF3roR7BG3KmsvNqnk4G25PxePnvQKHAvRpi/acbsp_20uuuuu.png)

After half an hour of casual playing, I noticed that some of the vistas provided by the game look like amazing postcards. That flash of insight is what inspired this post. I decided to wander around the city in search of scenes that could make a perfect postcard.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmddvPXtWnC4kVgYjf2JmhTGDDr5yhq8P3fJ7AgPgNdfTg/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_37_00.png)

Here you can see my avatar watching the distant colosseum very early in the morning.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRACPgXA2SQP8Z8bq8wYGFbZBRUTCtDt7eHe5L5GmNBpU/acbsp_202to_jw_tp.png)

In this postcard screenshot, you can see him posing near the biggest ship I encountered on the river.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVie7xwmQHgJgCYHoHsa96mKkjfXSUwnW9CV5jYy8JSBg/acbsp_2026_04_21_10_25_52.png)

Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood is a pretty old game, it was released in 2010, that still looks amazing in its vanilla state, but I needed a bit more flair and sharpness for the postcards to be perfect, so I used only one HD textures mod to enhance the visuals just a bit, without altering the colors and atmosphere of the original game.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSZaJcxJib4ktf4TaqR9YFd2DdqunUoLdCZod5y61JcN9/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_45_48.png)

When the full moon rises above Rome in this game, it creates a breathtaking atmosphere. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcnbfaqz6WKM8PS7yuoi635SKkDADVyEkqJ6ZZsBmQ12Z/acbsp_2026_04_21_10_28_38.png)

In this screenshot, my avatar is posing among the wildflowers; the plant in question is probably sage. The vegetation in bloom isn't that prominent in the original game; the modded version I'm playing is a bit more colorful in some places. Not in many places. The architecture, which is the main feature of the in-game world, looks mostly the same

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS2NNkqTuJQczRZqhy5nNC6SzvrmtgqAtRZ3AFj1BtS4Y/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_35_13.png)

The architecture is so beautiful that I often forget to play missions and wander around for hours just observing the details like a tourist would in the real world.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVAJ3zEWM4Z7PNL6ZN8CfAMmGQ3ixJ2RWVRjD1U3p3g4c/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_48_10.png)

The view from the river is also great for the most part.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQuXTmDx4wzevtg9dnLw1eqH8uiEkohYoWLJBwT7EvKPs/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_36_05.png)

Here you can see the ruins of the Roman civilizations surrounded by fields and hamlets. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWJpHo3PmhUXBHDKYhBNtKJUJ8tiGCV3uBsNZqYGZhkdf/acbsp_2026_04_21_11_42_44.png)

And that's it, this is the final postcard from Renaissance Rome. The post ends here - THE END.

This is my entry for the Gaming Photography Weekly Contest - Theme: Gaming Photographs. Here's the link to the contest announcement post by @gamingphoto

title.title: A Quick Nap [Fiction]
title.body:
![susbany-people-106556_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kemmyb/EqdBPbm1bUecVWPFJUZJzrxxhHyPdVHAJx5U9FjgxFVp31woCKa3qj6ak6iCLxt8bSB.jpg)![divider curl .webp](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/kemmyb/a75ed810b8aaff74d2505ddf85186840400c52a1.webp)


<div class=text-justify>

It was supposed to be a quick nap. At least that was what Tony Idoko told himself before he fluffed the pillows and lay down. He glanced at his wrist watch and nodded. He had twenty minutes to rest his mind and body before the next task of the day.

*Four hours later.*

His eyes slowly opened as he raised his hands and stretched, letting out a yawn. That was the best sleep he'd had in a long while, especially after a forty-hour shift at work. 

He sat up and shook his head, his hyperactive mind alerting him to his next task, as it always did. He furrowed his brows. Something was amiss and he couldn't place his fingers on it.

It was his day off and he remembered promising to help his wife with something but his mind couldn't summon this information to the surface. 

After a few minutes of searching his memory and nothing came up, he shrugged and went into the kitchen to start their meal prep. 

Then his phone buzzed. It was a text from his wife. 

*Are you back home with our children? Their lunch is in the oven. Love you.*

His heart beat twice as fast as he grabbed his car keys and dashed out of the house. He was a dead man unless the children were safe.

![divider curl .webp](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/kemmyb/a75ed810b8aaff74d2505ddf85186840400c52a1.webp)

title.title: Wedding Transport Guide: Cars for UK Wedding Ceremonies
title.body:
## Wedding Cars for Your Wedding Day

Wedding transport sets the flow of your ceremony day in the UK. It controls timing, comfort, and arrival experience. You need a car that fits your venue, outfit, and guest schedule. A well-planned choice removes delays and keeps movement between locations smooth. Poor transport planning creates stress and late arrivals. That affects photos, the ceremony start time, and reception entry. Wedding cars also shape first impressions at the venue entrance. Guests notice the arrival style immediately. You should align the vehicle with your wedding theme, whether traditional, modern, or minimal. A clear plan for pickup, waiting time, and drop-off points keeps everything structured.

## Types of Wedding Cars in the UK

The UK wedding car market offers a wide range of vehicles. Classic cars remain the most requested option for formal ceremonies. Rolls-Royce and Bentley models dominate this category due to comfort and appearance. Vintage cars suit countryside weddings and heritage venues. Modern luxury sedans like the Mercedes S-Class work well for city hotels and shorter travel routes. Limousines serve larger bridal parties who need shared transport. Executive minibuses support guest transfers for rural venues with limited parking. Each type serves a different purpose. You should match the vehicle size with dress requirements, road conditions, and the distance between the ceremony and the reception. Narrow roads in rural UK locations suit smaller vehicles. City routes support larger chauffeur-driven cars with easier access points.

## Costs and Booking Timeline

Wedding car pricing in the UK depends on vehicle type, distance, and duration. Standard executive cars usually range from £150 to £300 for a few hours. Classic luxury cars fall between £300 to £600. Premium chauffeur vehicles cost £500 to £900 for half-day hire. [Vintage options](https://www.waivio.com/) sit around £350 to £700 depending on condition and demand. Guest transport minibuses cost £100 to £250 per trip. Peak wedding season runs from May to September, and Saturday slots book quickly. Early booking improves choice and reduces cost pressure. Most couples secure transport 6 to 9 months before the wedding date. Late booking limits access to high-demand cars like the Rolls-Royce Phantom or the Bentley Flying Spur. You should confirm all timing details in writing, including waiting time and travel gaps between venues.

## Wedding Car Hire in Manchester

Wedding transport in Manchester covers city hotels, banquet halls, and nearby countryside venues. Traffic patterns in the city affect timing, especially on weekends. Professional chauffeur services plan routes and adjust pickup schedules to avoid delays. [Wedding Car Hire Manchester](https://www.atlanticprestige.co.uk/our_services/wedding-car-hire/) gives access to a wide fleet of classic, modern, and luxury cars suited for different wedding styles. Wedding Car Hire Manchester also supports multi-vehicle bookings for bride, groom, and guest transfers, which helps manage larger weddings with multiple locations. You should confirm venue access points early because central Manchester hotels often have restricted entry zones and controlled parking. Wedding Car Hire Manchester providers often include ribbon decoration, waiting time, and return journeys in standard packages, which simplifies coordination on the day.

## Practical Tips for Smooth Wedding Transport

Strong transport planning reduces delays and keeps your wedding schedule stable. You should confirm exact pickup times for every journey and allow buffer time between the ceremony and the reception. UK city traffic often causes unexpected delays during peak hours and weekends. A 15 to 20 minute buffer helps maintain control over timing. Inspect the vehicle before the wedding day to confirm cleanliness, seating comfort, and space for your outfit. Chauffeur presentation matters because they appear in arrival photos and guest interactions. Confirm backup vehicle availability in case of breakdown or delay. Match vehicle size with dress volume to avoid discomfort during entry and exit. Review insurance, cancellation policy, and total cost before final payment. Guest transport works best with shuttle minibuses for rural venues with limited parking. This reduces confusion and late arrivals.

## Conclusion

Wedding cars play a direct role in timing, comfort, and presentation on your wedding day. You need early booking, clear scheduling, and the right vehicle for your venue and guest needs. Strong coordination with your provider keeps travel smooth and avoids delays that affect the entire event flow.

title.title: Lecciones de barro y luz
title.body:
Cada mañana me siento a estrenar el mundo
con el placer de degustar un café.
No sabía ayer lo que hoy me pesa en los bolsillos, y lo aprendido tropezando me sirve para caminar.

No hay diploma que cuelgue en la pared del pecho,
ni guia para remendar descosidos
Voy anotando en hojas sueltas lo que el día enseña:
hasta una herida bien mirada también sabe a miel.

A veces el error me agarra de la solapa,
obligado a ver el fondo del plato sin mentir.
En ese silencio que da miedo, 
descubro que lo roto también sirve para seguir.

Así voy, con la libreta a medio uso,
con manchas de barro y algo que empieza a brillar.
No soy un sabio, si acaso un alumno
agradeciendo cada noche tener otro día para estudiar.

Porque vivir no es llegar, es ir haciendo el camino,
borrar, volver a escribir, perder y amanecer.
Y todo lo que aprendo, aunque duela me empuja. 
Y alcanza para el próximo paso.
Para seguir siendo.

Aprendiz de la vida, 
casi todos los días descubro cosas nuevas, 
aprendo 
y lo que aprendo me sirve para seguir viviendo.

title.title: Undertone - The noise of silence
title.body:
There are films that don’t tell their story out loud, yet continue to echo in our minds long after they’ve ended. We keep questioning the reasons behind the noise lurking beneath the silence. And we ponder whether certain elements of the surreal might actually be real. The film Undertone offers precisely this kind of experience. Although it has a simple, even at times slow moving narrative on the surface, it harbors intense psychological tension and emotional unraveling beneath. 

https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/mUpxARLqGbNJsWX3YuF0uUKpecO.jpg
[source](https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/mUpxARLqGbNJsWX3YuF0uUKpecO.jpg)

The film focuses more on what the characters do not say or show than on what they do. You’re certain that something is about to surface and take control at any moment, but you don’t know when it will happen. This constantly amplifies the tension in the story, making you feel it at its peak. You realize a simple element of fear is being created, yet you feel it’s quite effective. In other words, you start to fear the chain of events that haven’t yet unfolded. 

The characters’ dialogue is kept to a minimum. It’s fair to say they don’t speak unless necessary, instead, their glances, silences, and the atmosphere of the setting do the talking. I think this choice is quite successful because while watching the film, you become an interpreter rather than just an observer. You can’t help but interpret nearly every scene in your mind or with the person you’re watching it with. Questions like What is really being conveyed here? or What kind of horror is about to unfold? lurk in the back of your mind, waiting to be asked. 

The film doesn’t rush through the story. This might be a drawback for those who are impatient, but for viewers like me who get fully immersed in the film, it can be a reward even a deeply emotional connection. It also has the side effect of making you feel the tension and fear even more intensely. 

https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/8P7DLHSqtuGX5hzWfRHXnU5Pov0.jpg
[source](https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/8P7DLHSqtuGX5hzWfRHXnU5Pov0.jpg)

The acting performances were one of the film’s strongest points. In particular, the lead character conveys the fractures in their inner world through a nearly introspective performance, without resorting to exaggeration. This simplicity enhances the story’s realism and allows the audience to empathize with the character.

Of course, the film isn’t flawless. It’s fair to say that some parts of the narrative are overly cryptic, while this adds mystery to the film, it can also diminish the impact of certain scenes. There are moments you’d want to pick apart with a fine tooth comb and others where you’d wish for a bit more detail. The ambiguity in the final sections may feel satisfying to some, while others might perceive it as a shortcoming. For me, it was entirely open ended. I think they intended to leave the door ajar for a potential sequel. 

Overall, I can say that Undertone is one of those films that requires reflection and takes some time to fully digest. While it conveys fear and tension at the highest level, it offers an experience that invites plenty of contemplation. It’s a rare gem for those who love exploring the subtle nuances of human psychology, but it’s the kind of film that those interested in loud action movies will quickly grow bored of. 

https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/9CuJHodHb4RmhWU1mn9qiseFGFp.jpg
[source](https://media.themoviedb.org/t/p/w500_and_h282_face/9CuJHodHb4RmhWU1mn9qiseFGFp.jpg)

Instead of a fast paced story, it takes a quiet, measured path. The silence sometimes plays with your nerves, but overall, it stood out as one of those films that proves you can make a powerful statement without raising your voice. If you think this film speaks to you, I recommend watching it at the first opportunity without delay. If it doesn’t resonate with you, don’t force yourself you might not find any of what I’ve mentioned in the film, as its narrative progression is tailored for those who choose their genres and select films based on their current mood.

Thank you for being here and reading this. Take care of yourself, and goodbye.

Come sempre lo spettacolo è bellissimo, il sole sul mare con la parte di isola in controluce mi offriva mille spunti per dipingere. title.title: 3DP, Thumbtack Job, Varied List, Fire, Grilling - Monday 4-20
title.body:
I found a couple parts models for my Varia yesterday morning as I want to connect it to the saddle bag on my bike. The 3 pc one ended up getting mounted as it screws together and will not come off. No ride for the day as I had to go to a job mid morning. ![IMG_20260420_082019.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23u62hrzUmDH1AjeF319wbFaoUcaAjCyaVnDTEXbQbcVojubDBiZsSkquBK37j3y4ibxC.jpg) I was at the job before 10am and was handed a list of tasks to do. I went with only one known task so did not have all the tools I needed. I ran home then hit Home Depot for the lumber and picture hangers. Being right across the Y I stopped at Green Leaf for carts since the sales for the day were far too good to pass up. I was then not far from the job. ![IMG_20260420_110559.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23vsQPH171upDWWddsDYiaNZtqKXjJ3qrtq98g9GNAdNMpJhFCBRygbVr9LnW2mbA6jnq.jpg) First task was to remove wasp nests all over the place. I used my pole saw to get the ones on the house then used my trenching shovel on the 50+ nests on and in the shed. The shed door had to be remounted after it came off in the last wind storm. Then in this corner she had a roll of chicken wire which I install on the fence and over the gaps by the gate. The yard was all about escape proofing it for her young corgi. ![IMG_20260420_121451.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23wgL5EuoLbYGpVAuySwdNCZWkA45rCRekeLtz4pxZvUH4N3XcY9q41U4DynCGM119b8M.jpg) The gate latch was not set right so after fiddling with the gate itself I realized I could just raise the latch and everything worked smooth. I then installed fence on the base and instead of staples used screws and wire. The fence is held strong but can be shifted down as the wire bends and wears. ![IMG_20260420_123730.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23vsQfjJ3KFwFKc17VogtkWFtgn5zgPSqm4hMaKtkvy4bVcXsvzXNA2j15sLXh7267Gyw.jpg) The fence between the neighbor's dog and hers had gaps between the wall bricks and the fence. I used the pressure treated 2x6s to fill the gaps. I used my new chainsaw to cut the boards and it worked perfectly. So much faster than other saws. ![IMG_20260420_130743.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23zGefYucv2J4uBefaB8xFsKfTGUJuyd7PBDCN4JFFRmU92EEK2myzbKg9YTut1caNTX9.jpg) The board under the front fence was a bit harder as the concrete of the parking pad did not allow the board to sit fully beneath the others but It is in really tight as I got it. Then I installed a screen over the back door that splits in the middle and allows the dogs in and out the dog door. She mainly wants it for cooking and letting the smokey air out. I then had paintings to hang in her bedroom, her college diplomas in her office, and a larger painting by the front door. In the end it was a 4 hour job and I wasn't even home yet when I got the notification of her 5 star review she left for me on Thumbtack. ![IMG_20260420_135434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23tmKrpdonQWrFs7eChSXuornm19vVFGjgzvKCh8idUCfmZNPaT3fYsSC9JQ1kXxQXmj5.jpg) I was home in time to be able to unload the car before going to pick J up from track practice. It was super nice out so I figured burgers would be good for dinner. The fire took a bit to get to a good heat. ![IMG_20260420_171840.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23y8iuvQtGDtrp4fo9Pkb3dYDZRs8FuvfwVUeydYqbWojMGHN3z2XLG9P5DEjdUyA3JUL.jpg) ![IMG_20260420_182554.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23xVEdyhSZAmS3ykaFGMAWvZ1XgyvxYW3zunXDVFxxnRk2EgKFwyRchoYULLyM1a4MF6n.jpg) Soak before bed but my skin was not too happy after a while. ![IMG_20260420_195454.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/flemingfarm/23vho8J4fgUT4eSJV7PKeZSgXHmUvmXaxY4KJugYsZreRs9qFvX9JZK72t18sFVHyWhyA.jpg) Boys to school in a while then need to get a ride in before heading to town for couple's session and lunch. Not sure what else I will work on today. ---

title.title: Somebody Did Something - April 20, 2026@goldenoakfarm
title.body:
![Seedling tending supervisor crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EoEqTdJJEqZ62BCAebT5Q2XRZMNoMzEt7Hsk7aYRNdPBXQ3hSxpS75mvLy8mv5rkUEU.jpg)

On Monday morning I was up at 5:30AM and got my post up. I got the stoves going as it was to be cold all day. Then I tended the seedlings; raising lights, reorganizing, watering. I sat down for a while then got the laundry started.

![New Herb - tall stuff out crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EpnCmvZKQBvZZLG2A9gXLYfr3AjRYkJiACo77UREmxitxUrN27p8n44C5vmiTdZXZec.jpg)

My #2 intern arrived around 12:30PM and had dressed to be out in the cold, her choice. I had her cut down all the tall stuff in the New Herb garden.

![Wind chimes collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23yTojpguLavzj9N63AF4hoj5RDx3cmZprpWvKj5fB1G2G2L8G8qKaZUCpcJG8cWVnzgq.jpg)

When she came in, we decided to sit and repair wind chimes. The shell one that had been repaired earlier this year had its little bird drop out of the center. We got that back in and put back on all the shells that fell off in the process.

She had to go but I continued working on the 2 I’d gotten out of the New Herb garden. The snow had been deep when we repaired wind chimes earlier so these were left.

I got the laundry finished and that was about all for the day.

On Tuesday I hope to be able to get out and rake some in the backyard. I will very soon have to mow. I need to check the cold frame to see how well the plants survived the deep cold. I need to see if the mesclun has come up. And I also hope to get the doors and the glass washed today on 3 or 4 doors.

We will see…

![Mini bio framed Jan 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xyn876JURgHHjsp757ZTvXeEEBjdDeLXWynRcLCeuqwPPsqtEtXTosSPyKZdAgWivJB.jpg)

title.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1776775488423-750ead4751f7f289.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=gamingnature/c86c5db0)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=gamingnature/c86c5db0)


---

Hello gaming lovers today I want to share with you a car racing.Today there is no war, no shooting, no bombs.Today I tried to have fun, just a car driving competition in HD print.Actually in the gaming world, we see many types of gaming videos.

Those who love gaming love to play different games at different times, so I am no exception.So today I had a different attempt in the gaming world.But it's not a very big effort, it's a simple game.

Actually every person wants to do many things for entertainment and when I do something, I want to write a lot.

I find similarities with my childhood with any content creation or gaming, so I try to portray those scenes through writing sometimes.Actually when I start writing, a lot of things come to my brain.

For example today I am sitting in my room playing a car racing game.Even while playing this racing game, I remember a lot of things from the past.It seems those moments from the past have returned.

It seems those moments from the past have returned online.Look I played a car racing game today and when I was a kid, I once had a plastic car like this as a toy.

title.title: Learn Ethical Hacking (#6) - The AI Slop Epidemic - Why AI-Generated Code Is a Security Disaster
title.body:
trap**: functional code that is fundamentally insecure;
- How AI-generated **infrastructure** (Terraform, Docker, CI/CD) ships with default-open permissions;
- Why AI **cannot reason about security context** -- and what that means for the industry;
- How this theme connects to every vulnerability class in this series.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- Your hacking lab from Episode 2;
- Python 3 installed;
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

### Difficulty

- Beginner

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Ethical Hacking` series):

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#1) - Why Hackers Win](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-1-why-hackers-win)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#2) - Your Hacking Lab](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-2-your-hacking-lab)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#3) - How the Internet Actually Works - For Attackers](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-3-how-the-internet-works-for-attackers)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#4) - Reconnaissance - The Art of Not Being Noticed](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-4-reconnaissance)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#5) - Active Scanning - Mapping the Attack Surface](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-5-active-scanning)
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#6) - The AI Slop Epidemic - Why AI-Generated Code Is a Security Disaster](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-6-ai-slop-epidemic) (this post)

### Solutions to Episode 5 Exercises

**Exercise 1 -- Full Nmap vulnerability scan:**

Your full-scan.txt should reveal 20+ open ports with numerous NSE vulnerability findings including: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor (CVE-2011-2523), distcc remote code execution (CVE-2004-2687), UnrealIRCd backdoor (CVE-2010-2075), various Samba vulnerabilities, and Java RMI vulnerabilities. The exact count varies but Metasploitable2 typically has 15-20 distinct exploitable entry points on a single machine.

The key insight: a single poorly secured server can have more attack vectors than most organizations' entire perimeter. Defense requires addressing ALL of them; attack requires exploiting just ONE.

**Exercise 2 -- Python scanner enhancements:**

```python
import socket, json, sys

def scan_udp(target, port, timeout=3):
    try:
        s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        s.settimeout(timeout)
        s.sendto(b\

, (target, port))
        data, _ = s.recvfrom(1024)
        return True, data.decode(errors='replace')[:100]
    except socket.timeout:
        return True, \
# UDP: no response != closed\n    except:\n        return False, \
, 53) for DNS\n# JSON output: json.dump(results, open(\

), indent=2)
```

The key insight: UDP scanning is fundamentally ambiguous -- silence could mean open (service running but not responding to our probe) or filtered (firewall dropping packets). This is why UDP scanning is slower and less reliable than TCP.

**Exercise 3 -- Scanner comparison:**

Typical differences: Nmap may detect 1-2 more ports due to superior timing/retry logic, your scanner may miss ports where the timeout is too aggressive, and services like RPC (111) may appear differently because Nmap uses specialized probes. The lesson: no single tool catches everything, which is why professionals use multiple tools and manual verification.

---

# Learn Ethical Hacking (#6) - The AI Slop Epidemic

This is the episode I've been wanting to write since we started this series. Because there's a quiet catastrophe happening in software development right now, and almost nobody in the mainstream tech press is talking about the security implications honestly.

**AI code generation tools are producing vulnerable code at industrial scale**, and developers are shipping it to production because \

Let me be very clear about what I mean. This is not a hypothetical. This is not FUD. This is measured, documented, reproduced.

I'm putting this episode here -- right after we finished the recon and scanning phase, before we start breaking into actual vulnerability classes -- because _every single vulnerability type_ we'll cover from here on out is being amplified by AI code generation. SQL injection, XSS, deserialization, misconfigurations, all of it. AI tools are generating these bugs faster than developers can find them. Understanding _why_ gives you a massive advantage as a security researcher.

### The Numbers

In 2022, researchers at Stanford published a study: _\

_ The answer was yes. Developers using AI assistants wrote significantly less secure code AND were more confident in its security. Let that sink in. _Less secure AND more confident._

A 2023 study by NYU specifically testing GitHub Copilot found that for security-sensitive code generation tasks, **approximately 40% of generated code contained vulnerabilities**. Not edge cases. Not theoretical. Actual exploitable vulnerabilities: SQL injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal, hardcoded credentials.

And here's what really gets me about these numbers: the 40% figure is for _security-sensitive_ tasks. When researchers specifically asked the AI to generate code that handles authentication, processes user input, or manages file access, nearly half the output had vulnerabilities. For general code (string manipulation, sorting, UI rendering) the rate is much lower. The AI is worst at exactly the code that matters most.

The pattern is consistent across every study I've read: AI code assistants optimize for _functionality_ (does it work?) and _pattern matching_ (does it look like training data?). They do NOT optimize for security, because security requires understanding _context_ -- who calls this function, what data flows into it, what trust boundaries exist, what the consequenses of failure are. AI doesn't reason about any of that.

### Real Examples: AI Writes Vulnerable Code

Let me show you concrete examples of code that AI assistants have been documented generating. I'm going to show the vulnerable version AND the secure version, because this series is about understanding BOTH.

**Example 1: SQL Injection**

Ask an AI to write a \

and you'll frequently get:

```python
# VULNERABLE -- AI-generated
def get_user(name):
    conn = sqlite3.connect('users.db')
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute(f\

` and your database is gone.

The secure version:

```python
# SECURE -- parameterized query
def get_user(name):
    conn = sqlite3.connect('users.db')
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute(\

, (name,))
    return cursor.fetchone()
```

One character difference (`?` instead of `{name}`). Same functionality. Completely different security posture. The AI generates the first version because _that's what most code in its training data looks like_. The training data is full of tutorials and Stack Overflow answers that use string formatting because it's simpler to explain. The AI learned the common pattern, not the safe pattern.

We'll spend two full episodes on SQL injection later in this series (episodes on SQLi basics and advanced SQLi). When we get there, you'll see just how devastating this single vulnerability type can be -- and how reliably AI tools produce it.

**Example 2: Hardcoded Secrets**

```python
# VULNERABLE -- AI-generated
import boto3

client = boto3.client(
    's3',
    aws_access_key_id='AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE',
    aws_secret_access_key='wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY'
)
```

AI assistants generate this because their training data is FULL of examples with placeholder credentials. Some developers then replace the placeholder with their REAL credentials and commit the code. The AI doesn't warn them. It doesn't suggest environment variables. It just... generates the insecure pattern.

Having said that, this particular issue has a human element too -- it's not _entirely_ the AI's fault that a developer commits real AWS keys. But the AI is setting the stage by normalizing the pattern of putting credentials directly in source code. A good tool would generate the secure version by default:

```python
# SECURE -- credentials from environment
import boto3

client = boto3.client('s3')  # uses AWS credential chain automatically
```

This is one of those cases where the \

code is actually _less_ code. Boto3 has a built-in credential resolution chain that checks environment variables, AWS config files, instance roles, and more -- all without hardcoding anything. The secure version is simpler, shorter, and more portable. But the AI generates the long version because that's what appeared most frequently in its training data.

If you remember from episode 4 (recon), we talked about searching GitHub for exposed credentials. Tools like truffleHog scan git history for API keys. A significant percentage of the credentials they find were AI-generated code where someone forgot to replace the placeholder. The AI creates the vulnerability; the human makes it permanent by committing it ;-)

**Example 3: Insecure Deserialization**

Ask for \

and AI often generates:

```python
# VULNERABLE -- arbitrary code execution!
import pickle

def load_config(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        return pickle.load(f)  # NEVER use pickle on untrusted data
```

`pickle.load()` on untrusted data allows **arbitrary code execution**. An attacker who can control the config file can run any Python code on your server. We covered `pickle` in the Learn Python Series -- and I explicitly warned about this exact issue. Here it is, being suggested by AI tools to developers who might not have taken our series.

The secure version:

```python
# SECURE -- JSON can't execute code
import json

def load_config(path):
    with open(path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)
```

Same interface, same functionality, completly different risk profile. JSON is a data format. Pickle is a _code execution format disguised as a data format_. The AI doesn't understand this distinction because it can't reason about what \

means in context.

**Example 4: Path Traversal**

This one is sneaky. Ask an AI for \

:

```python
# VULNERABLE -- path traversal
from flask import Flask, send_file
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/files/<filename>')
def serve_file(filename):
    return send_file(f'/uploads/{filename}')
```

An attacker requests `/files/../../etc/passwd` and reads your system password file. The `../` sequences navigate up the directory tree, escaping the intended `/uploads/` directory. Your Flask app just became a file server for the entire filesystem.

The secure version validates and restricts the path:

```python
# SECURE -- path validation
import os
from flask import Flask, send_file, abort
app = Flask(__name__)

UPLOAD_DIR = '/uploads'

@app.route('/files/<filename>')
def serve_file(filename):
    safe_path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, os.path.basename(filename))
    if not os.path.abspath(safe_path).startswith(os.path.abspath(UPLOAD_DIR)):
        abort(403)
    if not os.path.isfile(safe_path):
        abort(404)
    return send_file(safe_path)
```

`os.path.basename()` strips directory components, and the `startswith()` check ensures we never leave the upload directory even if someone finds a creative bypass. The AI almost never generates these checks because path traversal isn't something you can detect from the function signature alone -- you need to understand that `filename` comes from user input and might contain malicious path components.

### AI-Generated Infrastructure: The Invisible Risk

It's not just application code. AI generates infrastructure configuration too, and the defaults are typically wide open:

```hcl
# VULNERABLE -- AI-generated Terraform
resource \

]
  }
}
```

Then there's this:

```yaml
# VULNERABLE -- AI-generated Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11
USER root                         # Running as root in container
COPY . /app
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt  # No pinned versions
EXPOSE 8080
CMD [\

]
```

Running as root in a container means that if an attacker breaks out of your application (via any of the vulnerabilities we've been discussing), they have root access inside the container. And if there's a container escape vulnerability (they exist -- CVE-2024-21626 was one), root inside the container becomes root on the _host machine_. The fix is one line: `USER nobody` or creating a dedicated non-root user. But AI defaults to root because most Dockerfile examples in its training data don't bother with user management.

And perhaps the worst:

```yaml
# VULNERABLE -- AI-generated GitHub Actions
on: pull_request_target            # Runs with repo secrets on EXTERNAL PRs!
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}  # Checks out attacker's code
      - run: make build             # Executes attacker's Makefile with repo secrets
```

That last one -- `pull_request_target` with external checkout -- has been exploited to steal secrets from major open-source projects. The AI generates it because it saw it in training data from BEFORE the community understood it was dangerous. This is a pattern we'll see repeatedly: the AI learns from historical code, including code that was later discovered to be vulnerable. It's essentially amplifying past mistakes into the present.

### Why AI Can't Do Security

The fundamental problem is that security requires **contextual reasoning**:

- \
-- depends on the call chain, the deployment context, the threat model\n- \
-- depends on what the function protects, what data it handles\n- \
-- depends on the principle of least privilege for this specific use case\n- \

-- depends on the entire system architecture, not just this code snippet

AI pattern-matches against training data. It generates code that LOOKS like code it's seen before. It can't evaluate security properties because it can't reason about the system the code will run in. It doesn't know your threat model. It doesn't know your trust boundaries. It doesn't know what's sensitive.

Think about it this way: if I show you a function `get_user(name)` that takes a string and queries a database, you immediately think \

These questions require understanding the _context_ around the function -- who calls it, what data flows into it, what happens downstream. An AI sees the function in isolation and generates the statistically most common pattern, which (as we've established) is often the insecure one.

This isn't something that will be fixed by training on more data or making models larger. It's a fundamental limitation of statistical pattern matching applied to a domain (security) that requires causal reasoning about adversarial behavior. A bigger model might generate fewer _obvious_ vulnerabilities (like raw SQL string concatenation), but the subtle ones -- missing authorization checks, TOCTOU race conditions, business logic flaws -- require reasoning about system behavior that current AI architectures simply don't do.

### The Supply Chain Angle

Here's where it gets really interesting from a security researcher's perspective. Remember the vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor from episode 5? Someone compromised a source distribution and inserted malicious code. That was manual, targeted, one-time.

Now imagine that millions of developers are using AI tools that suggest code snippets from a training corpus that _itself_ contains vulnerable code, backdoors, and malicious patterns. The AI doesn't know the difference between a legitimate code example and a backdoor example. It just knows what's statistically common. If someone contributes enough \

containing a subtle backdoor pattern to public code repositories, the AI might learn to suggest that pattern to other developers.

This isn't proven to have happened at scale yet -- but the attack vector is real and researchers are actively studying it. The term in the literature is **data poisoning**: deliberately corrupting the training data of an AI system to influence its output. For code generation models, this could mean: contribute thousands of subtly vulnerable code snippets to popular open-source projects, wait for the model to retrain on them, and then the model starts suggesting your vulnerability pattern to millions of developers.

_Think about that attack surface for a moment._ One vulnerability manually inserted into one codebase (vsftpd) affected thousands. One vulnerability pattern learned by a code generation model could affect _millions_.

### The \

Trap

There's a psychological dimension to this problem that we need to discuss, because it affects how you'll approach security testing in the field.

When a developer asks an AI for code and the code runs without errors, produces the expected output, and passes basic tests -- there's an overwhelming temptation to ship it. It _works_. The ticket gets closed. The sprint velocity looks good. Nobody reviews whether `cursor.execute(f\

)` is safe because the function returns the right user when you pass a normal name.

The Stanford study found that developers using AI assistants were _more confident_ in their code's security than developers who wrote code manually. This is the dangerous part -- not just that the code is insecure, but that the developer _believes_ it's secure. They trust the AI. They don't double-check. They don't think adversarially about inputs.

As a pentester, this is both a concern and (honestly) job security. The more organizations rely on AI-generated code without security review, the more vulnerabilities exist for you to find. But more importantly, understanding this dynamic helps you predict _where_ vulnerabilities are likely to be. New code, recently written features, areas where development moved fast -- these are the places where AI-generated vulnerabilities concentrate. They're your best targets during an engagement.

### What This Means for the Series

Throughout the rest of this series, we'll revisit the AI slop angle for every vulnerability class we study. When we cover passwords and authentication, we'll look at how AI generates weak password hashing. When we cover cryptography, we'll see AI suggesting deprecated algorithms. When we cover web vulnerabilities, we'll see AI producing XSS-vulnerable templates and CSRF-unprotected forms.

It's not a separate topic -- it's woven into the fabric of modern security. Every time we explore an attack, we'll ask: \

The security landscape shifted fundamentally when AI code generation went mainstream. If we don't address that shift, we're teaching 2020-era pentesting in 2026. And that's not what this series is about.

_De toekomst is... interessant. En niet altijd op een goede manier._

### Exercises

**Exercise 1:** Open your AI code assistant of choice (or use a free web-based one) and ask it to generate these 5 things: (a) \

. For each generated snippet, identify the vulnerability (if any), classify it (SQLi, path traversal, XSS, deserialization, misconfiguration), and write the secure alternative. Save your analysis in `~/lab-notes/ai-code-audit.md`.\n\n**Exercise 2:** Write a Python script called `ai_code_auditor.py` that takes a Python source file as input and scans for common AI-generated vulnerability patterns: (a) `f\

body.body:
![b O o O.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/herosik/23u6Dqf6PTHmJa3nJDoVmpRSYgm8fS1Rp7f5SYFs5VGhGXtA5FbVF86KfpCSQrR5qosrM.jpg)



[Introduction & A Few Things Explained]
This text is based on data from boxofficemojo.com. For a film to start earning money, it must earn 2.5 or 3 times its budget (3 times for a production with a truly extensive advertising campaign). Different sources give different estimates, as this is due to various factors. Typically, 2.5 times the budget plus a \

(from several hundred thousand to several million dollars) is enough to earn money. As a rule, most productions can be treated this way. The bigger the budget, the bigger the marketing. And the money allocated to marketing often exceeds the resources allocated to production. That's why it's said there are two budgets – one for production and one for promotion. Otherwise, no one will see your product. Smaller, medium-sized, or even quite expensive marketing usually pays for itself through the sale of merchandising, VOD rights, streaming, DVDs, etc. In the case of bigger films, this is usually higher, but sometimes there is a production like \

, which gives less chance to capitalize on more or less unnecessary items.

Why exactly 2-3 times as much? Because cinemas also take a portion of the revenue. The closer to America, the more they pay back to the studio. This means a lot in the US, less in South America and Canada, similarly/slightly less in Europe, and the least in Asia. Therefore, for averaging purposes and to simplify the calculation, it's assumed that the studio takes 50% of the box office. However, it's increasingly common to say that double the profit is sufficient, as it's increasingly easier to make money from toys, mugs, figurines, etc.

[Animated Films]

Zootopia 2 - The film may not have grossed $2 billion, but Disney certainly isn't crying. And if it does, they're wiping their eyes with thick wads of cash. $1,866,647,950 gross - NICE!

Hoppers - The new Pixar film cost $150 million. Its advertising campaign was strong, but not big enough to inflate the marketing budget. So far, it's grossed $367 million. If you have the chance to see it, I highly recommend it. It's one of the studio's best films.

GOAT - The new animated film from Sony is receiving very positive reviews and quite good earnings. The film is still grossing, but it's unlikely to break the $200 million barrier (data from April 20th - $190,343,206). GOAT cost $80-90 million, so it paid for itself.

[Movies]

Something for theater, Japan, and art lovers (and supposedly devastatingly good films). For several months now, the Japanese have been raving about the film Kokuho. Apparently, it's a cross-generational phenomenon (kind of like Top Gun 2, only on a smaller scale). The film cost $8 million and currently has $134 million. Kokuho's earnings have changed slightly, so I'm leaving this part of the post unchanged.

Dhurandhar The Revenge - The Indian blockbuster cost $30 million to make and grossed over $152 million.

They Will Kill You - The film cost $20 million to make and grossed $18.7 million. Maybe it'll reach $20 million, since it's still in theaters and making money.

Scream 7 - The film grossed almost $213.5 million. I heard it had terrible reviews, but so what if it cost $45, so it paid for itself?

Send Help - Disney's new film cost $40 million and earned just over $94 million.

Is This Thing On? - I couldn't find any budget information, but the film did quite well for a production Google knows nothing about (at least not in terms of budget). I know Disney wants to make a sequel. I'm not surprised, as the film, being a complete no-name, earned $10 million. Several times in my reviews, I've mentioned films with larger budgets and earned less.

Lionsgate lost money on I Can Only Imagine 2 - it earned roughly the same amount as its budget, which was $18 million.

Reminders of Him - Universal's new film cost $25 million and earned $85 million. Since it's still in theaters, it'll probably reach several thousand.

Project Hail Mary - Even though I complained about this film's trailer from the start (and I wasn't the only one, as it gave away almost the entire plot), according to reviews, it's one of the most outstanding films of the year. The film cost $248 million and is still growing!

On the other hand, Crime 101, the new Amazon-MGM production, didn't even make its budget of $90 million and earned... less than $73 million.

Melania is a similar flop. The film cost $40 million and earned less than $20 million. Well, after reading the reviews, I'm not surprised at all.

Angel, on the other hand, can be considered a success, costing $4 million and earning $26 million.

Anaconda cost $45 million and earned just over $135 million. A good result.

Shelter is another flop. The film cost $50 million and grossed less than $53 million.

Gore Verbinksy's new film cost $20 million and grossed almost $9.5 million. Not great, but apparently Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die is doing really well!

Apparently, the new version of Wuthering Heights sucks, but it paid for itself. The film cost $80 million and grossed $241 million. I assumed it would stop at $220, nice!

Ready or Not 2: Here I Come - Distributed by a Disney-owned studio, it cost $14 million and grossed over $38 million. A success.

The Bride! - A huge flop. The film cost $80 million and grossed almost $24 million.

Avatar: Fire and Ash didn't reach $1.5 billion, as I had speculated. James Cameron's latest production stalled just shy of $1.486 billion.

The President's Cake - The Sony film cost $1 million and grossed $2.7 million. A good deal.

A Private Life - The budget for this Sony production is unknown (apparently due to its limited release), but the film grossed $8.6 million overall.

The Choral - The budget for this Sony production is also a secret, but the gross is healthy – almost $9.5 million.

Luc Besson's new film, meanwhile, grossed almost $42.5 million, falling $10 million short of even breaking even.

The Strangers: Chapter 3 - The budget was a maximum of $10 million, and the film grossed $10.3 million. But they'll make up for it on streaming, as production wasn't expensive.

Fox released a film that cost $10 million and grossed $2.5 million.

Nirvana the Band: The Show the Movie - A film from Neon Studios cost $2 million and grossed $4.3 million, which is not bad.

The Secret Agent - Another Neon production cost $5 million and grossed just over $19 million – a success! Especially since it's a Brazilian film.

Sentimental Value - The film cost almost $8 million and grossed almost $23.7 million – not bad!

Studio Focus can't boast such luck, as they invested $4 million, while Midwinter Break earned $1.7 million.

One Battle After Another is another flop. Although the film is being dragged by its ears, hair, and panty line to squeeze out as much Oscar buzz as possible, it's... underperforming. The budget was $175 million (the maximum amount; it's difficult to establish a full cost estimate due to taxes and other factors), and the film grossed $213 million.

Marty Supreme recently ended its run and did much better than Paul Anderson. It had a budget of $70 million and grossed $180 million. So the film probably paid for itself in the end.

How to Make a Killing, another A24 film, cost $15 million and grossed almost $19 million, meaning it failed.

The Moment - It also failed to make a profit. It had a budget of $4 million, but grossed just over $5 million.

Pillion, on the other hand, was a success, costing $1 million and barely making $6.5 million.

Undertone is an even bigger success – the film cost $500,000 and recently surpassed $18 million. It's unlikely to reach $19 million, but with such a ridiculous budget, every few thousand dollars counts.

Chloe Zhao can also call it a success. The budget could have been a maximum of $35 million, but it grossed over $106.5 million.

The Housemaid – The film starring Sydney Sweeney grossed a very handsome sum. It had a budget of $35 million, but grossed over $401.5 million.



![b O o O.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/herosik/23u6Dqf6PTHmJa3nJDoVmpRSYgm8fS1Rp7f5SYFs5VGhGXtA5FbVF86KfpCSQrR5qosrM.jpg)



[Wstęp & Wyjaśnienie paru rzeczy]
Podstawą dla tego tekstu są dane ze strony boxofficemojo.com. Żeby film zaczął zarabiać pieniądze, musi zdobyć x2.5 lub x3-krotność swojego budżetu (x3 w przypadku produkcji z naprawdę dużą kampanią reklamową). Różne źródła różnie podają, bo wynika to z różnych czynników. Zazwyczaj 2.5-krotność budżetu + \

(od kilkuset tysięcy po kilkanaście milionów dolarów) wystarczy do zarabiania. Co do zasady, można w ten sposób traktować większość produkcji. Im większy budżet, tym większy marketing. A pieniądze przeznaczone na marketing, niejednokrotnie są większe niż zasoby przeznaczone na produkcję. Dlatego mówi się, że są 2 budżety - jeden przeznaczony na produkcję, drugi na promocję. Inaczej nikt nie zapozna się z naszym produktem. Mniejszy, średni, a nawet całkiem drogi marketing, zwykle zwraca się ze sprzedaży merchandisingu, praw do VOD, streamingu, płyt DVD etc. Ten w przypadku większych filmów z reguły jest większy, no ale czasem zdarzy się produkcja typu \

, która daje mniejsze szanse na kapitalizacje mniej lub bardziej zbędnych przedmiotów. 

Czemu akurat 2-3 razy tyle? Ponieważ kina też biorą dla siebie część pieniędzy. Im bliżej Ameryki, tym więcej oddają studiu, czyli w USA dużo, Ameryka Płd i Kanada - mniej, Europa podobnie / nieco mniej, Azja - najmniej. Dlatego dla uśrednienia i ułatwienia liczenia, przyjmuje się że studio zabiera dla siebie 50% kwoty z biletu. Aczkolwiek coraz częściej mówi się, że podwójny zysk wystarczy z uwagi na to, że coraz łatwiej można zarobić na zabawkach, kubkach, figurkach etc. 

[Filmy animowane]

Zootopia 2 - Film nie zarobił co prawda 2 miliardów dolarów, ale Disney na pewno nie płacze. A jeśli już, to wycierają oczy grubymi plikami banknotów. 1,866,647,950 zarobku - NICE!

Hoppers - Nowy film od studia Pixar kosztował 150 milionów. Jego kampania reklamowa była, ale nie na tyle duża, by wywindować budżet marketingowy. Na ten moment zarobił 367 milionów. Jak macie okazję na pójście do kina, bardzo polecam. To jeden z najlepszych filmów tego studia. 

GOAT - Nowa animacja od Sony zbiera bardzo pozytywne opinie i całkiem niezłe zarobki. Film ciągle zarabia, ale raczej nie przebije bariery 200 milionów (dane z 20 kwietnia - 190,343,206). GOAT kosztowało 80-90 milionów dolarów, więc zarobił na siebie. 

[Filmy]

Coś dla miłośników teatru, Japonii i sztuki (oraz podobno miażdżąco dobrych filmów). Od kilku miesięcy Japończycy mają pozytywny szał na film Kokuho. Podobno to międzygeneracyjny fenomen (coś jak Top Gun 2, tyle że na mniejszą skalę). Film kosztował 8 milionów, a ma na ten moment 134. Zarobki Kokuho zmieniły się nieznacznie, więc zostawiam tę część wpisu bez zmian. 

Dhurandhar The Revenge - Hinduska superprodukcja kosztowała 30 milionów, a jej zarobki przekroczyły 152 miliony. 

They Will Kill You - Produkcja filmu kosztowała 20 milionów, a zarobił 18,7. Może dotoczy się do tych 20, bo jest ciągle w kinie i zarabia. 

Scream 7 - Film zarobił prawie 213.5 miliona dolarów. Słyszałem, że miał fatalne recenzje, ale co z tego skoro kosztował 45, więc zarobił na siebie? 

Send Help - Nowy film Disneya kosztował 40 milionów, a zarobił nieco ponad 94. 

Is This Thing On? - Nie znalazłem informacji o budżecie, ale film poradził sobie całkiem nieźle, jak na produkcję, o której Google nic nie wie (przynajmniej w kwestii budżetu). Wiem, że Disney chce zrobić jego kontynuację. Nie dziwię się, film będąc kompletnym no name title, zarobiło 10 milionów. Parę razy w swoich przeglądach, wspominałem o filmach, które miały większe budżety i zarabiały mniej. 

Lionsgate straciło pieniądze na I Can Only Imagine 2 - zarobiło mniej więcej tyle samo, ile wyniósł budżet, czyli 18 milionów. 

Reminders of Him - Nowy film od studia Universal kosztował 25 milionów, a zarobił 85. Z uwagi na to, że ciągle leci w kinach, pewnie dojdzie kilkanaście tysięcy. 

Project Hail Mary - Mimo że od początku narzekałem na trailer tego filmu (i nie tylko ja zresztą, zdradzał niemal całą fabułę), to według recenzji jeden z najwybitniejszych filmów roku. Film kosztował 248 milionów 573 i ciągle rośnie! 

Za to Crime 101, nowa produkcja Amazon - MGM nie zarobiła nawet na budżet, który wyniósł 90 milionów a zarobki... niecałe 73 miliony. 

Podobną wpadką jest Melania. Film kosztował 40 milionów, a zarobił mniej niż 20. Cóż po przeczytaniu opinii na jego temat, nie dziwię się ani trochę. 

Za to o sukcesie może mówić film Angel, który kosztował 4 miliony, a zarobił 26. 

Anaconda kosztowała 45 milionów, a zarobiła nieco ponad 135. Ładny wynik. 

Shelter to kolejna wpadka. Film kosztował 50 milionów dolarów, a zarobił niecałe 53. 

Nowy film Gore Verbinksy'ego kosztował 20 milionów, a zarobił prawie 9.5 miliona dolarów. Słabo, ale podobno Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die ogląda się naprawdę dobrze! 

Podobno nowa wersja Wuthering Heights ssie pałkę, ale zarobił na siebie. Film kosztował 80 milionów, a ma 241 milionów na koncie. Zakładałem, że zatrzyma się na 220, nice! 

Ready or Not 2: Here I Come - Film dystrybuowane przez studio należące do Disneya, kosztowało 14 milionów, a zarobki przebił 38. Czyli sukces. 

The Bride! - To olbrzymia wpadka. Film kosztował 80 milionów, a zarobil prawie 24. 

Avatar: Fire and Ash nie dobiło do 1.5 miliarda dolarów, jak spekulowałem. Najnowsza produkcja Jamesa Camerona wyhamowała tuż przed 1,486 miliarda dolarów. 

The President's Cake - Film Sony kosztował milion dolarów, zarobił 2,7 miliona. Dobry deal. 

A Private Life - Budżet tej produkcji Sony nie jest znany (podobno z uwagi na to, że to produkcja o limitowanej dystrybucji), ale film łącznie zarobił 8,6 milionów. 

The Choral - Budżet tej produkcji od Sony również jest objęty tajemnicą, ale zyski są niezłe - niemal 9.5 miliona. 

Z kolei nowy film Luca Bessona zarobił prawie 42.5 miliona, czyli zabrakło mu 10 milionów by się chociaż z nim zrównać. 

The Strangers: Chapter 3 - Budżet wyniósł maksymalnie 10 milionów, film zarobił 10,3. No ale odkują się na streamingu, bo produkcja nie była droga. 

Fox wydało film, który kosztował 10 milionów, a zarobił 2.5. 

Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie - Film studia Neon kosztował 2 miliony, a zarobił 4.3, czyli nieźle. 

The Secret Agent - Kolejna produkcja Neon kosztowała 5 milionów, a zarobiła nieco ponad 19 - sukces! Tym bardziej, że to Brazylijski film. 

Sentimental Value - Film kosztował prawie 8 milionów, a zarobił prawie 23,7 - nieźle!

Studio Focus nie może się pochwalić podobnym szczęściem, gdyż zainwestowali 4 miliony, a Midwinter Break zarobiło 1,7 milionów. 

Kolejną wpadką jest One Battle After Another. Mimo, że film jest ciągnięty za uszy, włosy i gumkę od majtek, by wycisnąć ile się da z uwagi na Oscary, to... Słabo idzie. Budżet wyniósł 175 milionów (maksymalna kwota, trudno ustalić pełen kosztorys z uwagi na podatki i nie tylko), a film ma 213 milionów dolarów. 

Marty Supreme niedawno temu zakończył swój run i poradził sobie dużo lepiej niż Paul Anderson. 70 milionów budżetu i 180 milionów zarobku. Czyli film raczej ostatecznie zarobił na siebie. 

How to Make a Killing kolejny film studia A24 kosztował 15 milionów, a zarobił prawie 19, czyli nie udało mu się. 

The Moment - Również nie udało się zarobić. 4 miliony budżetu, a zysk nieco przekroczył 5. 

Sukcesem jest za to Pillion, który kosztował milion, a otarł się o 6.5 miliona zysku. 

Jeszcze większym sukcesem jest Undertone - film kosztował pół miliona dolarów, a niedawno temu przekroczył 18 milionów. Do 19 raczej nie dojdzie, ale przy tak śmiesznym budżecie liczy się każde kilka tysięcy dolarów. 

Chloe Zhao też może mówić o sukcesie. Budżet mógł wynieść maksymalnie 35 milionów dolarów, a zarobił ponad 106.5 milionów. 

The Housemaid - Film z Sydney Sweeney zarobił bardzo ładne pieniądze. 35 milionów dolarów budżetu, a zarobek przekracza 401.5 milionów.

body.title: How do we overcome doubts and anxities
body.body:
Doubts and anxities affect everyone in this life both those who believe in God and those who doesn't believe in him. Scripture teaches that we overcome them by trusting in God’s character and promises rather than our changing feelings. When we fix our hearts on who God is faithful, loving, and all powerful our fears begin to lose their grip. As it is written, 

>“Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding” (Proverbs 3:5).

https://youtu.be/3J4EEXHfIMo?si=_QkZyg3dDNrAto7t
Prayer is another key way to overcome anxiety and doubt. The Bible encourages believers to bring every worry before God, knowing that He listens and cares deeply for us. Through honest and continual prayer, we exchange our burdens for His peace. The bible reminds us that when we present our requests to God with thanksgiving, His peace will guard our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

body.title: Diy// step-by-step illustration of how to cut and sew three-quarter Ankara buba gown with bold Aso-oke collar
body.body:
Hello hive 





![Collage 2026-04-21 12-11-05.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/AKSd3rHe7fZn8HFVZsXNCzEVi2RHM83RePbYAz1U3M92pmds9Ubdp4X2cK2iG1e.png)



Good afternoon, DIYhud community! ✂️✨

Happy Tuesday to you all! May today be filled with fresh inspiration, creative energy, and beautiful results from every stitch, cut, and design you bring to life.

Keep creating, keep learning, and keep shining—your hands are building something amazing! 💫



![IMG_5509~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/244e6NsXc33cT8Vp2VCQcuN69V7Ebcu8kZCoA3JMe7DiK26snkpJ5TPvFc211wgUpAXY4.jpg)



I'm so glad to share, step-by-step illustration of how to cut and sew three-quarter Ankara buba gown with bold Aso-oke collar, side pockets, and slits, easy to make and does not consult time.




✂️ MATERIALS NEEDED
2 yards of Ankara
Aso-oke (for collar and yoke)
Matching thread
Scissors
Measuring tape
Ruler
Chalk





**FOLDING & BASIC CUT**



![IMG_5377.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23tm9LYrbdWxTxEgCW1NfKtFeCgV3VZKvsbgZ4zywXxpvVsd38ReNVWoekZXqrDK4t3FA.JPG)



Fold your Ankara into two (lengthwise), then fold again to get front and back together.
Mark your full length (45 inches).
From the top, mark your shoulder line.





 **NECKLINE & SHOULDER**

Mark neck width (3 inches).
Mark:
Back depth: 1 inch
Front depth: 2.5 inches
Extend the neckline downward by 4.5 inches to form the front opening (for the Aso-oke detail).
Slightly slope the shoulder ( 1 inches).

 **BODY WIDTH (FREE BUBU SHAPE)**
Use your hip measurement as the widest point:
36 ÷ 4 = 9 inches
Add 6 inches ease = 15 inches total (on fold)
Apply this measurement across bust, waist, and hip for a loose fit.
Draw a straight down to the hem.

**SLEEVE FORMATION**

This style uses a kimono/free sleeve (no separate sleeve cutting).
Extend from shoulder outward about 8_10 inches depending on desired sleeve length). But I used 10 inches for mine.
Mark sleeve opening width and cut.


**SIDE POCKET & SLIT**

From the shoulder, measure 17 inches down – mark pocket position.
From the hem, measure 11 inches upward – this is your slit opening.


**CUTTING AND SEWING OF THE ASO-OKE (Front Panel)**



![IMG_5386.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23tSaUNEDmiTqWXKUfYGXpB83kXd7vicFL3qd6JCm5uAsdt5iKCJ6DQBc9bSTbGJhpmkC.JPG)

![IMG_5391.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23u64tcusGiWUCzkHo4JcoQzRenxfn4dxJXCEcGj8d2WVArWCVzcU6Fk885EC8bWdYHbB.JPG)

![IMG_5387.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23uFRhRByBKnde12HecTzp5ZXMH9NyyUs3VtnKDx1Uo2KZ7z1B7DtxG6vku8AP6N9CWj9.JPG)

![IMG_5385.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23tmG18g14kh4Ats2mjnF8Cons8Z7m1HLt4mGd8sFBSpuVHRXAzZKHXhzhK35xUCo3JBz.JPG)

 
Cut a curved panel using Aso-oke (as seen in your image).
Place it on the chest area and stitch neatly on the Ankara.


**After that joint the front and back seam shoulder.
Attached the Aso-oke to sleeves area**


**CUTTING AND SEWING OF THE COLLAR**



![IMG_20260320_101329_084.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/Eo4D2YJ965Qbx54LYyEfEaBbVvzYhi4JQEt6Gpp3fsQqwd8EFcNtryayMsxiW48WN8K.jpg)

![IMG_20260320_103354_099.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23w2f44ikTLbPNqQCexDUvuJPSFwstnFmUTcrhVLVyFu7eY7BnkJMvp9782yF6hjouWiK.jpg)



Measure round the neck area.Cut a straight collar strip from Aso-oke 17.5inche. cut out two pieces of it then run a stitch before attaching it to the neckline area then Topstitch for a clean finish.

**Sew side seams:**

Sew from sleeve down to pocket
Skip pocket opening
Continue sewing below pocket
Stop at slit point



![IMG_20260320_095415_372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/23yTj8HZTRS4in6kuhhQWCRTZzsHWmEk8K1eCMwwxHC9ekGHGiFVG4vH8t8aNUNdhcFKZ.jpg)

Attach pocket pieces neatly inside and hem slit side and down of the dress. Press the garment well




![IMG_5500~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/242hS4rUND9VYZRnfeGkUu7NZqkFaUG1g6RwtQ2fQcUAgmgjoRTMo8kP7Ww4nAQqHud8n.jpg)

![IMG_5519~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deborahstitches/244xsKNpUSbpfE2oY7goxSeNF1iZERLARTHoa21UoJ2THpZT9MhEW9CoEyNtvMMB3Z5Az.jpg)



✨ FINAL LOOK
You’ll achieve:
A loose, comfortable buba fit
A bold Aso-oke collar and chest panel (yoke)
Clean side slits for easy movement
Functional hidden side pockets.



Thanks for word of encouragement that has keep me going and make me to do better, do you have a fruitful day.

body.title: They All Should Be Punished
body.body:
I think it's fair to say that I got lucky when growing up as a kid. I never really had a case of being bullied other than once or twice that it happened, and I honestly think this was because I always knew how to stay away from trouble or out of the sight of those known bullies. Also, I was always a smart kid, so I was friends with people whose presence kind of shielded me from that stuff.

Although, if I'm being honest, it wasn't like I made friends with those guys specifically because I was avoiding getting bullied, but it just happened, and everything just kind of aligned, I guess.

But then again, we all know that bullying doesn't just affect kids. There are adults out there who still get bullied by other adults, and some of this bullying isn't always physical; it could be online.

Today's contest asks us which is worse, the physical bullying and harassment or the online one, and to be honest, my first instinct had been to say the physical bullying, because this is what always comes to mind whenever we talk about bullying, but after giving it a thought, I now find myself leaning toward the online side, and here's why.

When it comes to physical bullying, I genuinely feel like it is something that easily can be handled without it escalating quickly. Especially as adults, there are a lot of ways you can handle a bully, one of them being by involving the police; it all just depends on how dangerous the bully is.

But when it comes to online bullying, I feel like there are a lot of things attached to it. Because for one, online bullying doesn't necessarily have to come from one person. I mean, at first it will be you against one person, but then other people start to come in with their own opinions, and you suddenly find yourself against thousands of people, if not more.

Unlike physical bullying, it rarely escalates unless the bully decides to involve his friends.

Then again, another thing about online bullying that makes it dangerous is that it can quickly turn into a physical one; it all depends on how good the bully is with whatever it is they're bullying you with. A good story from your bully could make people start hating you in real life, and before you know it, you can't even go to the market without people pointing their fingers at you, saying all sorts of things.

It also could affect you at your place of work; it could affect you mentally and in more worse ways than some of us can even imagine. And this is why I feel that online bullying is a lot more dangerous than that of the physical ones.

But when it comes to punishing these bullies, I sincerely feel that both punishments should be equal, as the goal is to discourage bullying totally and not give them options on what type of bullying the bully should take on.

body.title: Bitcoin Hashrate Drops as Prices Collapse | Data on Hash Rate, Mining by Pools and Country | April 2026
body.body:
The bitcoin mining process is a key element of the Bitcoin network. It is basically what makes the whole system tick. As most know, the miners are incentivized to keep running the code and processing blocks and transactions with Bitcoin rewards at a rate of 3.125 BTC every ten minutes. These rewards keep cut in half every four years with the last halving in April 2024. 

In 2023 and 2024 the hash rate kept growing, setting new heights month after month. The trend continued in 2025 as well. This is the basic parameter that shows how secure the network is. There is some debate about this topic, since the equipment used to mine Bitcoin, the ASICs keep getting more efficient each year, meaning that for the same price of capital, one is getting more hash rate. Because of this some argue that the parameter that should be used as a security of the network is the cost of capital that is involved in the Bitcoin mining, but this is not as easy to calculate having in mind all the different type of equipment, the different producers, deals made etc. Although one can get the latest prices and make some theoretical calculations. 


 

![01.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23uEzR5qVNdPoJNFYaQjg8H8ufQHJZfGrEpR69hn9xyfBrQo3BN7NGDMweTwLFtcnL9S6.png)





As already mentioned, the Bitcoin hash rate has increased in the last years, with some oscillation in 2024 due to halving. Usually after the halving the hash rate drops as some miners turn off machines because they can compete with the rewards cut in half. 

We will be looking at:
-	Hash Rate
-	Mining by Pools
-	Miners Revenue
-	Mining by Country
-	Current Countries Share
-	Hash VS Price

The data presented here is mostly gathered from [the blockchains charts](https://www.blockchain.com/charts) and mempool.space. 


## Hash Rate
The ultimate Bitcoin value is network stability and security. The network security in a proof of work chains is measured in hash rate, or how difficult it is to mine. The bigger the completion, the higher the hash rate.

 

![image001.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23t76bthTZB8WzoWnLNyyQW6G53g5hC8bcHVoxpPkMTrxUH8TyzDTwH4iNKum6ApfmqYE.png)




Almost constantly going up with few dips here and there. The most significant dip happened in the summer of 2021 when China banned mining. We can see that in the last period there is some volatility in the hash rate because of the halving in 2024 and somewhat slowing down in the hash rare. But every dip is just a tiny pullback and the hash just keeps on growing.

**When we zoom in 2024 - 2026 we get this:** 


 

![image003.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23t79CBdGU8Y7DqbXNcLj9tTX8WREz5ERQZWHungGqzDDF6rh7Uu9e6gbDUduybXdXYCo.png)




A steady growth up to October 2025 with more than 1000 EXA in hash rate. Since October 2025 the hash rate has slowly been going down and dropped from around 1150 EXA at the top to sub 1000 EXA recently.
Overall, in the last months the hash rate has been hovering around 1000 EXA.



## Mining Pools

The way Bitcoin mining works is usually with miners all over the world joining in mining pools and sharing the rewards. Here are the top mining pools and their evolution.




![image005.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tGVYfPT4Bv8TWoGngrY67FtqgwAYmyY2LZuSEnCVsaY5KmKFKGc1HpK5FNWT4PtxS3a.png)



The chart starts from 2019, because prior to this year, the data is quite small. 
We can notice that trough the years Foundry has been consistently in the top pools followed by AntPool and the F2Pool. The ViaBTC pool is also in the top, although it seems that it has dropped a bit in the last period. 
Overall, a steady share in the last years by the mining pools. 



### Top Mining Pools Share

The current share of the top mining pools looks like this:




![image007.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23t77B8AXvCXtujorGb7rZC1h6pjGdyocCP9xoFSZPSiknqdGYb3sEEm23j8jnqqhzfz9.png)




Foundry USA is on the top here with 32% of the blocks mined in the last month, followed by the AntPool and ViaBTC. These three miners have more than 50% share of the mining hashrate. 

Note that not while a lot of these pools are US based or Chines, it doesn’t mean that the physical location of the mining equipment is in that country, as they join the pools through the internet and can be located anywhere. We will take a look at the countries share below in the post. 


### Miners Revenue


What is the miner’s revenue over time. Here is the chart. 




![image009.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tkjzfCeEKmXSAnWBuRWFYxiumxJ8LcPecop1YULxcG6sDn6HBo8zWakyExzScQEzwwE.png)




We can see that back in 2016 the daily miner’s revenue was under 1M USD. Then it started growing a lot in 2017 and reached more than 50M per day. After the bull run in 2017, the miner’s revenue dropped to under 10M. It went sideways for the next two years in 2018 and 2019 and then increased again at the end of 2020. In 2021 the miner’s revenue reached a new ATH with more than 70M USD revenue per day. A drop in 2022, and a growth again in 2023. 
After the growth of close to 60M in 2025, it dropped and in the last few months it is around 30M.


**On  a yearly basis we have this:**


 

![image011.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tGVGGGyKNQBdkyxNvWXJoXBSmJJpxuLiKrk2SgB9MjKKjQQEu6SLeC8MY5BrwFqtkGy.png)




Even with the halving in 2024, the year was still the best for miners in revenue. This is due to the increase in the price of BTC and a new ATH for Bitcoin reaching 100k. 
A 15 billions dollars in miners revenue in 2024. 
What’s even more interesting is that 2025 surpassed 2024 and ended with 17B in miners revenue, while the whole year was with smaller block rewards. Even with the low fees for BTC in 2025, the miners revenue will still hit a new ATH on a yearly basis. Now for 2026 the odds looks like it will be hard to beat previous year revenue. 

## Top Countries Mining Bitcoin
When we rank the countries as the latest data available in 2026 we get this. 




![image013.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tRt95HJnutkrG3X2bbRvSJ5VK7cMTmmyUAEuvjs7UBL5LzwvTAGfztJsm78nCndYhZD.png)




This data is according to the [Hashrateindex](https://hashrateindex.com/blog/global-hashrate-heatmap-update-q2-2026/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The US is on the top, followed by Russia and China. Paraguay is next with the UAE and Oman. Oman seems to be a new entry this year. 

## Hash Rate VS Price
When we plot these two together, we get this. 





![image015.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tGXdeNXXfD2BucGAEfMgNWtJMjfK1EUXG8cENHGfFTrpxCqGT9qc9TPEafnztQgbAxU.png)
 



At first glance these two don’t seem corelated. There seems to be small periods when there is some correlation. 
First at the end of 2018, there is a dip in the hash rate and in the price as well. Then again, a small dip in March 2020, and the most obvious in the summer of 2021 when both the price and the hash rate dipped hard due to the China ban. 

In the last six months there is a follow-up of the hash rate after the price crash and then so did the hash rate, but not as much as the price. 

At the end the chart for the **Bitcoin yearly candles** on logarithmic scale:

 


![image017.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/Eo1uyQgNTJAUYWq8QqVcNbV2ezR9XKkczRJyTH82TCDkvQESefGqP3wMQ9KBxZqbGzb.png)




The last year, 2025 barely visible here has a small red candle. This is off from the previous cycles as 2025 should have been green as well, and then maybe 2026 a red one. Will see how 2026 turns out to be. 



All the best
@dalz

body.title: A Strong Weekend
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWYzSLh1s3TFEdyn4NuAuKyAiAujaPzFLnCfE36aMA8Po/pxl_20240324_163237473.webp)

---------------------------

Overall, I would have to say it was a pretty good weekend for the Tiffin Dragons Softball team.  I wouldn't say it was a perfect weekend, but winning three out of four games isn't too bad.  I think the only unfortunate part is the game they dropped was versus the team they are fighting against for the top spot in the conference.  

Actually, I take that back.  Looking at the GMAC standings, it appears that Ohio Dominican has been on a bit of a slump and is no longer in the top spot where they used to reside.  Tiffin has now claimed that spot with Ashland hot on their heals.  Oddly enough, University of Findlay has more overall wins on the season, but when you break it down to conference play, they are lagging behind by two games.

Tiffin started their weekend with a double header on Friday against Ursuline College in Pepper Pike Ohio.  I wouldn't say I am an expert on Ohio, but Pepper Pike is a town I have never heard of.  Without looking at a map I would guess maybe it's down by Cincy?  Maybe someone can help me out here.  Or I could just look at a map...

Well, I figured it was one way or the other.  Turns out I went the wrong direction.  I figured South when it was actually North. Pepper Pike is up by Cleveland.  

Anyway, geography lesson aside, Tiffin had a nice pair of wins in their double header against Ursuline College.  They took the first game 5 to 0, and then they had another shut out in the second game winning 16 to 0 in a five inning run rule.

Then on Saturday, they played in Columbus, OH against Ohio Dominican University.  Our niece who used to play with the Dragons made the quick drive into the city to watch the games.  It was a double header again like on Friday, and Tiffin started things off well with a 5 to 3 victory over ODU.  Unfortunately, things fell apart in the second game with the Dragons falling 6 to 1.

While a loss is never a good thing, the Tiffin team is an impressive 14 and 2 in their last sixteen games.  That is some good momentum to be riding into the conference tournament in just a few weeks.  They have three more series before the G-MAC Tournament starts on April 29th.  

First they take on Wayne State University in a double header tomorrow before facing Walsh University twice on Saturday for senior day down in Tiffin.  Finally, on Sunday they have another double header against University of Findlay.  I'm looking forward to seeing how Tiffin finishes the season.
