body.title: From A Pom's Eye View
body.body:
*I should probably give a quick explanation of the term Pom. I used to think that everyone knew what it jokingly referred to, but unless you're British or Australian apparently it isn't actually common knowledge. A Pom is what Australians call British people who come to Australia. There are different theories as to how the term originated, but nothing conclusive. The most likely theory seems to be the [reference to pomegranites.](https://wavelengthmag.com/why-do-aussies-call-brits-poms/)* I'll be honest, when I first immigrated to Australia I wasn't entirely sure what expect, probably something akin to the film Crocodile Dundee. We chose to move to Adelaide, South Australia (SA) and arrived in winter so it didn't initially seem much different to England. It was chilly and rainy, a time of year when lots of things are green and growing, so we weren't yet seeing the yellows that come with the summer drought. The language is the same and South Australians are generally teased by the rest of Australia for sounding like Poms, so the Aussie accent here isn't even that strong. (A couple of South Aussies have even mentioned that when visiting the UK some people there didn't twig that they had Aussie accents.) The only thing at the time that stood out as being a bit different was that the architecture and infrastructure layout had a slightly Germen feel to it. I don't know if that's because SA had a lot of German migrants in it's early settlement or if it's just because Germany is the only other country I've visited that had a similar vibe. Because there are a lot of similarities between British and Australian culture, it took time to pick up on the differences. Naturally the climate and weather are the most obviously different, more so or less so depending where you are in the country. These differences will also dictate a difference in way of life. Other than a brief visit to Queensland, I've only experienced South Australia, so my comparissons will be biased towards that. The states and territories all do things a bit differently.
![17766471578765080497891495527010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/minismallholding/EnoJn6eLLDkGafj7nMiKUj6ZfPniUaKQwRSmjhmhc6dXKNeXti3RjbqNsMNrC9CrNjZ.jpg) My daughters at a South Australian beach

Talk About the Weather

The weather in SA is described as mediterranean but I'd say it's more extreme. It's the driest state in the driest country and in summer can usually go without rain for a month or more. We've experienced some years where it's been 3 months without rain. Ironically the total rainfall here is comparable to the UK, the difference being that most of that falls in winter here (flooding isn't uncommon then) and the summer heat quickly dries up any reserves in creeks or ponds. SA's humidity levels are generally quite low even in winter, so when we experience 18°C it feels much colder than it would in the UK. 35°C here doesn't feel anywhere near as unbearable as it does in the UK. While the UK's season when vegetation grows like mad is the summer, in SA it's the winter when it's cooler and wetter, so thankfully stinging nettles come out in winter when you **don't** have bare legs. When you walk into a shopping centre here on a hot day, instead of feeling warm air blowing on you as the doors open you feel cool air. It's like things are reversed and you get hot air blasting you when you walk back out. People who don't have good or any air conditioning at home will sometimes go to the shopping centres to stay cool. Either that or the beach if that's close enough. On the subject of shopping centres, something that I found unusual when we came here was that they have supermarkets in them. So you'll have your fashion, accesories shops, jewellers, chemists etc, then you can go and get your groceries. It's also not uncommon to see people browsing in clothing shops with a trolley full of groceries. In the UK practically all houses have central heating and radiators in each room. I've never seen a radiator in SA, but nearly every house has air conditioning. Some houses have such bad heating that it's common for Australians to just dress up warmer when inside in winter or wrap themselves in blankets. Ugg boots and Oodies are also popular here for winter. While Oodies are made more for indoor use in some areas (certainly in my area) you'll see people in the shopping centres wearing them. Indeed you'll also see them in their bedroom slippers, pyjamas and dressing gowns on occasion. In summer some go barefoot, *although I don't know how the don't burn their feet on the tarmac.* There's a bit of a joke on social media that when you move to Australia your dress sense when you go out gets more and more casual until you're dressing like a bogan. The closest British equivelent of 'bogan' is probably 'chav'; however, where chav's are more likely to dress blingy bogans dress daggy. I'm not sure why Australians tend to gravitate more towards casual, comfortable dress, but that could also be due to the heat. A suit is going to get uncomfortable when you're sweating and probably doesn't even look that smart once covered in sweat stains. It will also depend on the area as to how people present themselves. In the wealthier suburbs they will dress smarter and will look healthier in general too. I don't recall seeing such an obvious visual divide in people in the UK unless you're going to a completely different part of the country.

Hiearchy

Have you ever noticed how different countries have different things they see as reflecting your status? For example in the UK the type of car we drive is often the way people judge us, while in France it doesn't matter what car you're driving it's how you dress. In Australia it's where you live and where you went to school and what you drive, except their vehicle hiearchy is different to Britain's. In England sporty cars are held in high regard on the road. When I drove my little fiesta I was constantly being cut up, less likely to be let out from a side road in heavy trafic and more likely to be blocked if I needed to change lanes. When I drove my husband's RS Turbo it was like I was suddenly royalty! Everyone jumped at letting me in and I didn't get cut up once. In Australia the Ute is king. Anything that is traditional car shaped will be cut up by everyone else, including others like it. Bigger vehicles will basically bully their way in front of you and Utes respect only other Utes. In fact they are so sure of their superiority that they will sometimes even take on the big trucks/lorries, which doesn't always end well. Naturally here my husband has a Ute and wonders why he gets cut up when he has to borrow my car. I drive various vehicles for work and their size dictates how often I'm likely to be cut up. The smallest car is bright red and sometimes other drivers don't even see it, despite looking straight at it, until I'm nearly on top of them. My own car is black and is still seen more than that one, so I can only assume it's because it's a bit bigger. People still don't like it being in front of them, though. My daughter's car is a bit bigger again, and is tolerated a little bit more by other road users, but only a little.

Food Stuff

The food here took some adjusting to. The first place we ate out at that was recommended to us by a local we found the food very bland. Many of the European types of foods here are much blander and the range of Indian style foods is more limited. In recent years we've been able to find Indians which have better flavour and spicier food, but I think that's only come with demand as we have gained more immigrants from Asia. On our first visits to supermarkets here I had to do a double take when I saw the bottles of cordial, because for a moment I thought they were toilet cleaners, they were that brightly coloured. I hadn't seen food colourings so bright since my childhood and I have to say I didn't miss it. I used to like mayonaise back in England, but here it has sugar in it. Cadbury's chocolate was one of my favourites, but in Australia it tastes like it has antifreeze in it. Apparently they do actually add something which is a kind of antifreeze in order to stop it melting too easily in the hotter temperatures. It's not all bad, though, Tim Tams could quite possibly make up for any food faux pas Australia has ever made. I once said that we had nothing comparible in the UK and was horrified at the suggestion they were like Penguin biscuits! While the concept might be the same and they might look similar, Penguins can't hold a candle to the Tim Tam. The proximity to Asia means that we get a wider range of ethnic foods here than you get in the UK. Sushi is practically a staple here, as are Vietnamese dishes like banh mi, noodle bowls and rice bowls. Recently I've also been hearing a lot of praise for restaurants offering athentic cooking from some of the African countries in the bigger capitals. I'm not aware of Adelaide having anything like this yet, though.

The Language Barrier

Australians may speak English, but sometimes you can get tripped up or have some embarassing interactions due to differences in word meanings. When we first arrived my husband had to get a medical check to start work. The nurse asked him to take his top and pants off and got all flustered when she came back in to him naked and trying to cover his bits with his hands. If you aren't familiar with British English we call undies pants. Australians, like Americans, call trousers pants and we didn't know that. Thongs here are what we call flip-flops in the UK and it took a while before I could comfortably call them that and not feel like I was discussing underwear. I have had to learn to call plasters bandaids, otherwise I get a confused stare if I ask for one. Something that often amuses me is the propensity for Aussies to add 'ie' or 'y' to the end of some nouns. For example they call 'bikers' 'bikies'. To me adding that suffix makes things sound cuter, so adding cuteness to what are generally big, imposing looking people makes me chuckle. They do not, however, view them as cute. In fact they are often seen as potential criminals due to some gangs dealing in drugs and there are laws against them gathering in their club colours; essentially anti-association laws. *** *I know we have a quite a few people here on Hive who have experienced different countries either by living in them long term or visiting and I'd really love to know what your experiences have been. What's the good, the bad, the ugly, the amusing and even the surprising? I love to hear about different cultural experiences from different perspectives. Please, please share either in the comments or with a post of your own and don't forget to tag me if you do a post.*

body.title: Rael Caladiao Re-Practicing Kickflip Week #1 | TWS Skateboarding
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXw1BcXY1FcsF1KLWC1zZFNUEX6Cf8GgosPU6J8bdNBpw/for_bg.jpg)

**Rael Caladiao** is re-practicing his **Kickflip** again. The last time I saw him perfectly land his Kickflip was way back in **2012**. I don't remember the exact year, but he really landed his Kickflip. Since then, I never saw him do his Kickflip again, but after 14 years, he is so obsessed with getting back his Kickflip that's why he is re-practicing this trick again.

> ### Week #1
 
In the first week of re-practicing his Kickflip, I noticed he almost got his Kickflip, but there were a lot of problems that I saw while he was practicing his Kickflip. I've been doing a Kickflip so many times that I know why he is so hard to land his Kickflip, and I'm here to tell those problems.

## Highlights
***

I can't remember how many times he tried to land his Kickflip, but I provide at least three attempts practicing his Kickflip.

Let me tell you what the problems are with this attempt at his **Kickflip**. When I was watching the clips of this attempt, he almost got his kickflip, but he failed. His footing is right, and he popped the tail with enough height. But when he started to flick the board, his two arms put too much pressure on his back, so much that a lot of pressure was transferred to his back, and that is the reason he leaned back too much. As you can see, by the time he landed his kickflip, his back leaned so much that's why he fell off his board. 
 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS9QsQz3bVFQvLU3V11crs5VMZtaPPugPnfeSaK5f47wU/highlights.jpg)

This attempt is almost identical to his previous attempt what he did is almost the same. His footing is right, he popped and flicked his board very well, but again he leaned his back so much. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSdFu9nPu5Pyy5YyMoH5NdbSvBxzBgvxhhC4tprxi3xGF/highlights_2.jpg)

At least three problems that I found on **Rael's Kickflip**. First, the pop is most of the time. Every time he popped his board, he popped the board very low, that's why the board is hard to flip. The second problem is that he flicked the board, but he didn't flick the board at the right position. He flicked the board on his left side, that's why the board flip in the 90 degrees position. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPTfwJb6rUxV4kDdGHekQ2RDqqszh7UeKoxiZ8knWgqex/highlights_3.jpg)

In the first week of practicing his **Kickflip**, sadly, after multiple attempts, he failed to perfectly land his Kickflip. The good thing is he almost got his Kickflip not once but twice. I think that is a good sign if he always practices his Kickflip, one day he will perfectly land his Kickflip again. 

<center>

I also made a GIF format to see how **Rael Caladiao** is practicing his Kickflip.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZVBLAUQYgwbFxfksehBEzMX9E4q3bFW4VkYwDYyqYSzJ/gif.gif)

***

P.S.: I've been playing skateboarding since 2005 and started filming and editing in 2011. On the **TWS** skate video, you'll find a random of tricks and behind skateboarding, we are not pro skaters we just skate for fun and I really love this.

***

>
Hola, querida comunidad de Hive. Es un placer estar de vuelta con ustedes para compartir un poco más de nuestra música llanera. En esta oportunidad, me uno con mucha alegría a la semana 38 del Festival de Música Tradicional VDC, un espacio que se ha convertido en una vitrina maravillosa para nuestro folklore. Para esta edición, he preparado un tema que es pura tradición \

, de la autoría del recordado Dámaso Figueredo. Esta pieza es un pilar de nuestra música y siempre es un reto y un honor interpretarla. En esta ocasión, la presento en la tonalidad de Re mayor, buscando transmitir toda la fuerza y el sentimiento que esta letra exige. No puedo dejar de mencionar el lujo que me doy en el acompañamiento. Cuento con el respaldo sonoro del Maestro Ramón Páez, quien con la maestría de su cuatro le da esa base perfecta y auténtica que el tema necesita para brillar. Trabajar con músicos de su nivel siempre eleva la experiencia y hace que el proceso creativo sea mucho más especial. Espero que disfruten de esta interpretación tanto como yo disfruté grabándola. Gracias por el apoyo constante, por sus comentarios y por mantener viva la llama de nuestra música tradicional. Un abrazo enorme para todos con cariño, su amiga @Yoxibeth🎵🔥

***

# The Remarkable Adaptations of Penguins: Masters of the Cold

Penguins are fascinating creatures that have captured the hearts of many with their unique appearance and charming behaviors. These flightless birds are not just adorable; they are also remarkable survivors in some of the harshest environments on Earth. This post explores the incredible adaptations that enable penguins to thrive in cold climates.

## Physical Adaptations

### 1. Streamlined Bodies
Penguins possess a streamlined body shape that reduces drag while swimming. Their torpedo-like form allows them to glide effortlessly through the water, reaching speeds of up to 15 miles per hour.

### 2. Thick Layer of Blubber
To insulate against freezing temperatures, penguins have a thick layer of blubber beneath their skin. This fat layer provides not only insulation but also energy reserves during times when food is scarce.

### 3. Dense Feathers
Penguins have a unique feather structure that keeps them warm and dry. Their feathers are tightly packed and waterproof, providing excellent insulation and preventing heat loss. The outer layer of feathers is coated with a natural oil that repels water.

## Behavioral Adaptations

### 4. Social Structure
Penguins are highly social animals that often live in large colonies. This social structure provides warmth and protection against predators. By huddling together, they can significantly reduce heat loss during harsh weather conditions.

### 5. Parental Care
Many penguin species exhibit remarkable parental care. Both parents share the responsibility of incubating eggs and feeding chicks. This cooperative breeding strategy ensures the survival of their young in a challenging environment.

## Feeding Adaptations

### 6. Specialized Diet
Penguins primarily feed on fish, krill, and squid. Their excellent swimming abilities allow them to dive deep into the ocean to catch prey. Some species can dive over 1,800 feet in search of food.

### 7. Unique Hunting Techniques
Different penguin species have developed unique hunting techniques. For example, the Emperor penguin often hunts in groups, using coordinated efforts to herd fish into tight schools for easier capture.

## Conclusion

Penguins are truly remarkable animals, showcasing a variety of adaptations that allow them to thrive in cold environments. From their physical traits to their social behaviors, these birds exemplify the incredible resilience of wildlife. As we continue to study and protect these magnificent creatures, we gain valuable insights into the complexities of life in extreme conditions.

body.body:
# Neds Point Light Today I will share a few shots taken on visits to Neds Point in Mattapoisett MA, about an half an hour drive from home, I like getting there early well before sunrise and hope to be lucky enough to catch some nice colors as the sunr rises, but even if not its still a nice spot to start the day This post will focus on the lighthouse and here is a little bit about it Ned Point Light as it is official called I believe is a historic lighthouse on Ned's Point Road in Mattapoisett, Massachusetts. The lighthouse was built in 1838 at a cost of approximately $5,000, and named after Ned Dexter, a local farmer. Supervised by a local builder, Leonard Hammond, the lighthouse was constructed with a birdcage-style lantern similar to Bird Island Light found in Marion, Massachusetts. All the stone used for the construction of the lighthouse was locally sourced, with most of it originating from nearby beaches. Inside, Which I didn't get to see, are 32 granite steps that are cantilevered to the outside wall without the use of mortar. The original lantern used 11 whale oil lamps, each with its own parabolic reflector. And like other lighthouses I have read up on around here the Whale oil no doubt came from the New Bedford Whaling ships. The Great Blizzard of 1888 significantly damaged the keeper's stone house, resulting in it being demolished and the building of a wooden replacement. Following modernization in 1961, the lighthouse was reactivated in 1961 with its current 6-second isophase. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982. Mostly I post the shots from those taken earliest through to later in the morning, and for no real reason today I decided to do the opposite Its a lovely spot, to walk around if your like me, but also has a few benches and a rock wall one can sit on, or of course as most who visit there seem to do you can park, and relax in your car and enjoy the sunrise

body.title: Dan Saved My Phone Battery!
body.body:
I learnt a lot about [mobile phone battery management](https://ecency.com/hive-106817/@danielcarrerag/the-20-80-rule-why-i-stopped-charging-my-phone-to-100percent-engspa) today from @danielcarrerag. So here's how he helped me to improve my mobile phone battery life.


![Mobile Phone Charging](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcbWjaURfqWwm2Hzh3QFsqm1Wom23gUooeKjwAeq5fDme/1776766807172.avif)

<sup>This image is the work of Dan. Being the featured image in his post linked above. </sup>

Dan's post let me know how important it is to limit charging to 80%. And I'm aware that I have switched on the adaptive charging feature on my new (to me) Google Pixel 7a. But I don't remember anything about an 80% limit. So I delved deeper...

## Charging Optimization Settings


![Mobile Battery Charging Optimization](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYcU86FQh4t1ymGpWs7fyV9dyaaospws4gDabwEXu36Ws/1776766941506.png)

<sup>Screenshot of the Pixel 7a charging optimization settings. </sup>
In my Pixel's battery settings I've a choice of `Adaptive Charging` or `Limit to 80%`. But I didn't really understand the difference. And I was worried that by limiting charging to 80%, I might invoke some type of memory limitations on the battery that I have heard about. So I clicked the [Google link for more information](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/7106961). 


![Google Battery Settings Support](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcvEJjioyJdx1rSUaA67SwQQ5MA3b76FcmWjQE7muBkUS/1776767045506.png)

<sup>Screenshot of Google's battery settings support page. </sup>

That information told me how the different charging optimization options work. But I was left with a personal question... 

## Is 80% Battery Charging Enough?

Whenever I can, I like to be out and about. For walking, good battery strength is nice for step counting and photos. But for socialising, I absolutely need access to my phone for payment and for my Uber home. 

As I thought about limiting my battery charge to 80%, I remembered the excellent power saving options for my phone. In my previous phone, with extreme power saving mode on, the phone was so restricted that it was easier to turn it off. But with my new phone, I have easy access to apps that have been restricted. And I just get a prompt to temporarily override the restriction.


![Extreme Battery Saver Override](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXsnK39YJu9YrhyZvX8QbBy6sWdHVxHNUWcZF2dgJSGiV/1776767118319.png)

 <sup>Screenshot of Pixel 7a extreme battery saver override. </sup>

So I'm confident that I can improve my mobile phone battery life by restricting normal charging to 80%. Safe in the knowledge that I will get a 100% on every 10th charge.

Dan also explains about keeping the lower charge limit at 20%. And fortunately, I get a warning when my battery charge level drops to 20%.

*How do you manage charging your mobile phone?*

#### Mobile Phone Charging Footnote

As a thank you to Dan for inspiring this post, he is a beneficiary. But if you don't want to upvote me, please tip Dan or [upvote his post](https://ecency.com/hive-106817/@danielcarrerag/the-20-80-rule-why-i-stopped-charging-my-phone-to-100percent-engspa).

body.title: A Night of Pride and Love: Our First Family Dinner Celebration
body.body:
***The end of the school year always brings a mix of emotions—relief, joy, pride, and a quiet sense of accomplishment.***

![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23vsLXB92pW4P2BMQoPjTD8UrTc9skyKLjZykE8ruEpu6wwtTm8Y4MC413qdBB7wL2ryy.jpg)

This year, however, felt extra special for our family. It wasn’t just about closing another chapter of academic life; it was about celebrating milestones, honoring hard work, and, most importantly, coming together for our very first family dinner dedicated to these achievements. **It became more than a simple gathering—it was a heartfelt celebration of love, unity, and shared success.**

For weeks, everyone had been busy. Students in the family were focused on finishing requirements, preparing for recognition days, and dreaming about graduation. Parents and elders, on the other hand, were equally occupied—supporting, encouraging, and quietly praying for the success of their children. When the school year finally came to a close, it felt like we all crossed the finish line together.

![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wMYfAAbFu8NtwcmXR3vrWfAXVJeGi4ZhqaqfgxeEnoELDcASKTys2aUF9XDgKFgeU31.jpg)

The idea of having a family dinner came naturally. We wanted to mark the moment in a meaningful way, something that would allow us to pause and truly appreciate what everyone had accomplished. It wasn’t about extravagance or fancy arrangements; it was about being present, sharing stories, and celebrating each other.

![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23y8wfPBQdP46Eczu8ZtKndBzk6Bss8222C5zcUsh9DWqEdLhZHg3eBx4Jxv3uCdsfZLN.jpg)

That evening, as we gathered around the table, there was a different kind of warmth in the air. It wasn’t just the delicious food laid out before us—it was the laughter, the smiles, and the sense of pride that filled the room. Each dish seemed to carry a story, and each person brought with them a journey worth celebrating.

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wC5ZpgkWsKupJc8ZkcAJtxeZrURrVGhLUoawLTf62nxtQ1EfGQWuRwYu9HGRNt9Npxx.jpg)

The graduates and completers were, of course, the stars of the night. Watching them sit there—smiling shyly, yet proudly—was a reminder of how far they had come. Behind every medal, certificate, and recognition was a story of hard work, sleepless nights, challenges, and perseverance. Some had struggled silently, others had pushed themselves beyond their limits, but all of them stood as proof that determination truly pays off.

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23vsBsMU5QAJyeN7x94bhJaPQ67RV6CQgN9E4oNXYyrjadGn5Rwza8XccXrGvx9k8NqRV.jpg)

As we took turns sharing our experiences, the room echoed with stories that were both inspiring and touching. One spoke about the challenges of balancing school and personal struggles. Another shared how support from family made all the difference. There were even moments of laughter as funny memories from the school year were recalled—small mishaps, unexpected surprises, and unforgettable classroom moments.

But what made the evening truly special was the realization that these achievements were not individual victories alone—they were family victories. Every success was built on a foundation of support, encouragement, and love. Parents who sacrificed, siblings who cheered, and relatives who believed—all played a part in shaping these accomplishments.

![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wMUDFRM62bcySdMsdsyNRwWbnVdsLH7kzsEpdn3dt5nMwNHC1oa1XyaZVyk1FRaL4Bj.jpg)

In between conversations, we found ourselves simply enjoying each other’s presence. In a world where everyone is often busy and preoccupied, moments like this are rare and precious. That night reminded us of the importance of slowing down and making time for what truly matters—family.

There was also a deeper kind of gratitude that filled our hearts. Gratitude for the strength to overcome challenges, for the guidance we received along the way, and for the opportunity to grow and learn. It was a quiet acknowledgment that while the journey may not have been easy, it was certainly worth it.
As the night went on, the celebration became less about achievements and more about connection. The laughter grew louder, the conversations more heartfelt, and the bond among us even stronger. It was in those simple, genuine moments that we realized the true essence of the gathering.

This first family dinner may have been planned as a way to celebrate the end of the school year, but it turned into something much more meaningful. It became a reminder that success is sweeter when shared, that love is the foundation of every achievement, and that family is our greatest source of strength.

As we ended the night, there was a collective sense of fulfillment. Not just because of the food we shared or the accomplishments we celebrated, but because we were together. And in that togetherness, we found joy, pride, and a renewed appreciation for one another.

![99.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wC7ULYZD6b7NpALGSHrfU9N4YgsH5oAoLrmhYcC1Zzmx2znyQ6AkKewVFbTsLZWRJj2.jpg)

***This experience is something we will carry with us—not just as a memory, but as a tradition we hope to continue. Because beyond the awards and recognitions, it is these moments of love and unity that truly define success.***

***And as we look forward to new beginnings and another school year ahead, we do so with grateful hearts, knowing that no matter what challenges come our way, we have each other—and that is more than enough.***

body.title: Television Review: The North Remembers (Game of Thrones, S2X01, 2012)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/gatJmQDn8ipBRWvFZVexWZ6SYdx.jpg)

**The North Remembers (S02E01)**

Airdate: 1 April 2012

Written by: David Benioff & D.B. Weiss
Directed by: Alan Taylor

Running Time: 52 minutes 



The inaugural season of *Game of Thrones* was, by almost any measure, a remarkable piece of television. Many would argue—with considerable justification—that it remains the series’ finest hour, a sentiment that can be attributed to its unparalleled fidelity to George R. R. Martin’s dense literary source and, perhaps more importantly, to the sheer novelty of its concept. It arrived unburdened by the crushing weight of expectation and the emerging cult status that would later define the phenomenon. Season two, adapting the 1998 novel *A Clash of Kings*, thus faced a formidable challenge: to maintain momentum while expanding an already sprawling narrative. *The North Remembers*, the sophomore season’s opener, commences in a satisfactory manner, deftly re-establishing the chessboard of Westerosi politics. Yet, for all its competence, it cannot quite replicate the electric, world-building shock of the [series premiere](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-winter-is-coming-game-of-thrones-s1x01-2011). It is a workmanlike and efficient episode, but one that already hints at the narrative compromises and diluted focus that would occasionally plague the later seasons.

Bolstered by HBO’s confidence and an increased budget, the episode exhibits a slightly grander scope in its plot, settings, and dramatis personae. Showrunners David Benioff and D. B. Weiss perform a commendable juggling act, updating almost every major storyline and packing them into a single hour. The result is a densely woven tapestry that tackled a huge amount of exposition and scene-setting but never wasted a word. This leanness is the episode’s greatest strength; it is a thematically focused instalment that, unlike some of its predecessor’s more scattered instalments, zeroes in on the corrupting nature of power and the vacuum left by Ned Stark’s death.

The action resumes in King’s Landing, where the boy-king Joffrey celebrates his name day with a tournament that is less a contest of skill than a sadistic spectacle of slaughter. In a moment of quiet cunning, Sansa Stark manipulates the monstrous monarch into sparing the life of the drunken knight Ser Dontos Hollard (Tony Way), revealing a survivor’s intelligence beneath her courtly façade. This scene is swiftly followed by the arrival of Tyrion Lannister, who assumes the role of Hand of the King with characteristic wit and immediately begins needling his sister Cersei over the strategic folly of Ned Stark’s execution. Meanwhile, the City Watch, under orders from Joffrey and Cersei, hunts down and murders every male infant suspected of being Robert Baratheon’s bastard—a brutal sequence of infanticide that underscores the episode’s central theme of power exercised without conscience. The sole survivor of this purge, the blacksmith Gendry, is revealed in the final scene to be travelling northwards with the disguised Arya Stark, whose disappearance vexes both Lannisters and Starks alike.

Concurrently, Robb Stark, now the King in the North, attempts to parley with the Lannisters. His terms—full independence for the North and the return of his sisters—are predictably unacceptable, making the continuation of war a near certainty. In a fateful decision, he heeds the counsel of his captive-turned-ally, Theon Greyjoy, and releases him to treat with his father, Balon, on the Iron Islands. This narrative thread, while briefly touched upon, sets in motion one of the season’s most tragic arcs. North of the Wall, Lord Commander Jeor Mormont’s ranging party finds the wildling settlements deserted, save for the holdfast of the repulsive Craster. Robert Pugh’s portrayal of the incestuous patriarch, who lives with his daughters as his wives, is suitably unsettling, serving as both a source of supplies and grim foreshadowing of the horrors beyond the Wall.

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys Targaryen’s storyline enters a period of desperate hardship. The mother of dragons possesses her three mythical hatchlings, but they remain small and symbolically potent rather than militarily useful. She, Ser Jorah, and her decimated khalasar are forced to trek through the desolate Red Waste, a plotline that emphasises her vulnerability and the long road ahead.

The most significant new narrative, however, erupts on the island fortress of Dragonstone. Here, Stephen Dillane’s Stannis Baratheon, stern and unyielding, declares himself the rightful heir to the Iron Throne. He is counseled by the pragmatic smuggler-turned-knight, Davos Seaworth (Liam Cunningham), but is increasingly under the sway of the mysterious Red Priestess, Melisandre (Carice van Houten). Their introduction brings a potent new religious dimension to the series, with the cult of the Lord of Light positioned as a disruptive force against the established Faith of the Seven and the old gods of the North. This subplot culminates in the tragic poisoning of the loyal Maester Cressen, a scene that efficiently establishes Melisandre’s otherworldly power and Stannis’s ruthless new path.

Directed by Alan Taylor, *The North Remembers* is, by its own admission, an episode light on forward plot propulsion. Much of its runtime is devoted to exposition: at Craster’s Keep, we learn of the desertion of Mance Rayder; in Essos, the complexities of the geography are hinted at. While necessary, this occasionally gives the episode a feeling of table-setting.

The introduction of the new Dragonstone characters, however, is handled with superb economy. Dillane’s Stannis is a masterpiece of repressed fury, Cunningham’s Davos provides a much-needed moral compass, and van Houten’s Melisandre simmers with enigmatic menace. The production also benefits immensely from new filming locations in Croatia, particularly Dubrovnik, whose ancient walls and sun-bleached stone provide a perfect, tangible embodiment of King’s Landing, elevating the show’s visual grandeur.

Not every element succeeds. Some scenes feel like pure filler, such as the heavy-handed moment where Cersei threatens Petyr Baelish’s life—a exchange that, while showcasing Lena Headey’s commanding presence, adds little to the narrative. Similarly, a brief scene of the captive Jaime Lannister menaced by a direwolf feels like a gratuitous showcase for the series’ improved CGI capabilities rather than an organic story beat.

Nevertheless, as a season opener, *The North Remembers* is undeniably a success. Critics praised Tyrion’s development and the compelling new cast. It is a solid, confident piece of television that successfully re-immerses the audience in Martin’s world, managing its enormous cast and multiple threads with impressive dexterity. It may lack the pioneering brilliance of the first season’s premiere, and its pace is more deliberate than thrilling, but it fulfils its primary duty: it remembers the past, sets the stage for the coming clash of kings, and promises a great deal of fire and blood to come.


RATING: 6/10 (++)

body.title: Harrassment should be abolished
body.body:
Greetings!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeaDgBNFMr8ydoZs8RouhEvDdj8bvSnHdSUEFbL9JsVnX/img_20260421_wa0024.jpg)

One thing that has plunged society into uncertainty in life is harassment. People on so many occasions have been harrassed just because they are doing what they feel it's right to do.

Bullying is a one form of harassment which is now prevalent amongst both the young and the old in the society and it's really cost so many people's life as some people who can not withstand the gravity of being harrassed have taken their own lives.

Having said this, I would like to delve into the topic of today's prompt which is all about, “Online vs Physical.”

Well, one thing that is sacrosanct in this is that bullying is bullying either online or physical, there's no other nomenclature to it than harassment. 

However, even as they are, both still have a slight difference and the difference here is that, one can go viral while the other can be limited within the locality where it happens.

Physical bullying or harassment is the kind that happens physically and might be tougher atimes. I have seen people being harassed physically in the public space without them being allowed to tell their own story. Sometimes,  they are being injured and molested. It's somehow pathetic and like I said earlier, it's taken away lives, I mean this harrassment of a thing.

Also, the online harassment of a thing has brought about shame and stigma to the lives of people. Whenever I see people on social media attacking others, I used to feel for such souls.

People are being dragged or called out on social media for what they know nothing about. Although, there are some people that are guilty of the offenses they were being called out for, but notwithstanding, it's not in the hand of any individual to judge or harrass anyone even, if guilty.

So, since no one is permitted to judge or take a precise action on the activities of others except the law enforcement agency, then anyone found guilty of harassing others both off and online should be properly punished under the law.

Furthermore, another thing is that, majority of those who judge others just because of their deeds are also to be judged if searched or investigated vividly. So, who now appoints them to be a judge in others matter when they are not even innocent of what they are harassing others for.

So, since the law is in place, I think the wrath of the law should be adequately metted out on those who harrass others both physically or onlineand moreso, I would advise those who are always harassing others to take caution as they are not assigned to be a judge in other people's matter through which they mow harrass others when they claim to be innocent of what they are harassing others for.

In conclusion, both the physical and the online harrassment are not good and people should desist from harassing others while the law takes its full course.

Si no esta en tus manos lograr un cambio, entonces y solo entonces te darás cuenta que solo te traerá preocupación y no ocupación del problema. Se que no es fácil mantenerse atento a los problemas y a veces hasta los chismes nos entretiene. Los días siguen pasando, las madrugadas se siguen viendo hermosas y se acercan los cambios, lo sé, lo estoy mirando. Adaptarse a esos cambios seguramente me costara tiempo, pero sigo repitiéndome día con día; todo va a salir bien. No es fácil improvisar todos los días, no es fácil levantarse cada día con una sonrisa y de buen humor, pero el día esta allí esperando por ti. No lo haces por los demás lo haces simplemente para ti y luego eso te permite cambiar en algo tu entorno. Son esos pequeños pasos de logros, de metas por lograr. Tengo licencia para vivir y siempre me la da cada día la fuerza suprema del universo y yo se la agradezco.
***
Este texto corresponde a mi participación en el reto diario del amigo @latino.romano y @mariannewest [post](https://hive.blog/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/21-april-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3080-licence-to-do-something) **ENGLISH VERSION** If you can do something to change your environment, you simply have to do it and not look around for someone who can help you. You do it, and little by little, those who feel they can do something to change their environment will join you. If making a change isn't in your hands, then and only then will you realize that it will only bring you worry and not address the problem. I know it's not easy to stay focused on problems, and sometimes even gossip distracts us. The days keep passing, the early mornings continue to be beautiful, and changes are coming. I know it; I can see it. Adapting to these changes will surely take time, but I keep telling myself every day: everything will be alright. It's not easy to improvise every day, it's not easy to get up every day with a smile and in a good mood, but the day is there waiting for you. You don't do it for others; you do it simply for yourself, and then that allows you to change your environment in some way. These are the small steps of achievement, of goals to reach. I have a license to live, and the supreme force of the universe grants it to me every day, and I am grateful for it.
***
This text corresponds to my participation in the daily challenge of my friend @improv, @felt.buzz, @latino.romano and @mariannewest [post](https://hive.blog/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/21-april-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3080-licence-to-do-something)

body.title: Teeth Straightening Options for Adults in Troy
body.body:
[Adult Orthodontist Troy](https://www.myamazingsmile.com/) services are becoming popular as more and more adults decide to enhance their smile at various stages of their lives. In 2026, orthodontic treatment is no longer restricted to teens. Research shows that almost one-third of orthodontic patients are now adults and reflects a significant shift towards treatment for later in life. This trend is due to advancements in technology, more the flexibility of treatment options, as well as more awareness of the oral health benefits.

Adults who seek to straighten their teeth have aesthetic as well as functional reasons. Incorrectly aligned teeth can result in problems like irregular wear, difficulty in cleaning and jaw discomfort. Orthodontic treatment can help solve these issues by enhancing the alignment of the teeth and overall function. Many people also seek treatment to boost confidence in social and professional situations, particularly with the increase in video communication and personal interactions.

A very sought-after options available today are clear aligners. They are clear removable trays made of digital scans that gradually shift teeth to a desired position. Aligners are worn for the majority of the day, and are changed every two to three weeks. They can be effective for moderate to mild alignment problems and provide an option for adults who prefer to have minimal privacy when they undergo treatment. Clear aligners require less appointments in the clinic, usually scheduled every 8-10 weeks, which can be a good fit for people with busy schedules.

Traditional braces are still an excellent option, especially in more complicated cases. Modern braces utilize high-end materials and smaller brackets, which makes the braces more comforting than older models. They give exact control of tooth movement and are typically suggested for cases of extreme teeth crowding or teeth correction. The duration of treatment with braces usually can vary from 18 to 24 months based on the nature of the situation.

Ceramic braces provide an alternative that is less obvious than braces made of metal. They use tooth-colored brackets that match natural teeth, which makes them ideal for those who wish to strike an equilibrium between efficiency and aesthetics. Lingual braces are a different alternative, which are placed behind teeth so that they are completely concealed. They are designed specifically and give you a firm control while still maintaining discretion.

When it comes to treatment planning Adult Orthodontist Troy solutions usually provide a customized treatment plan depending on the individual's needs. Orthodontists today use the latest technology in digital image, 3-D modeling and AI driven planning to track tooth movements with high precision. This technology lets patients get the desired results prior to when treatment begins. It also helps to reduce the duration of treatment by increasing accuracy.

A new trend that is gaining momentum is the hybrid treatment. It is a method that combines various orthodontic techniques, like beginning with braces for major adjustments and then finishing with aligners to make fine adjustments. Hybrid strategies increase effectiveness and allows orthodontists modify treatment in accordance with changes in the condition. This results in better outcomes while reducing total treatment time.

Lifestyle compatibility plays a significant factor in deciding on the best choice. Adults favor treatments that are able to be integrated into their routines without causing major interruption. Clear aligners, less appointments, and electronic monitors make modern orthodontics more adaptable. Clinics have developed treatment plans that cut down on appointments while ensuring consistent improvement, which is essential for professionals working full-time and busy people.

Health benefits are another important aspect. Straight teeth are simpler to keep clean, which lowers the chance of developing gum disease and cavities. A properly aligned bite also increases chewing efficiency and eases strain on the jaw joint. A lot of adults view the treatment of orthodontics as a health preventive measure rather than an improvement in appearance.

Retention is an integral component of the process. When teeth are aligned retainers are employed to keep the results and avoid shifting. Regular use of retainers will ensure the stability of teeth over time and protects the final results of the treatment.

In the end, [Adult Orthodontist Troy ](https://www.myamazingsmile.com/)options for 2026 offer numerous effective options for straightening teeth of any stage of life. From clear aligners, to advanced braces and hybrid treatment Adults now have the option of an array of flexible and precise options that are suited to their needs. With the right planning and regular treatment, orthodontics can bring long-term improvements in dental wellbeing and confidence.

title.title: Adult Smile Solutions That Last in Rochester Hills
title.body:
[Adult Orthodontics Rochester Hills](https://www.myamazingsmile.com/) is being a primary area of interest for those who seek to see long-lasting improvements in dental appearance and health. In 2026, the need for orthodontic treatment for adults will no longer be dependent on the age. Teeth can be repositioned at any age provided that the health of the gums and bones are steady. This has resulted in an increasing number of the number of adult orthodontic patients. research suggesting that almost one-third of orthodontic patients is now an adult.

The best long-term solutions to your smile start by identifying the root cause of the alignment issue. The most frequent causes of problems are overbite, spacing, crowding as well as jaw alignment issues. These issues impact more than just appearance. Incorrect alignment of teeth can result in irregular wear, problems with cleaning, and a higher chance of developing gum disease. An alignment that is correct improves the way teeth work together and can help to distribute pressure equally across the bite and reduces the risk of long-term damage.

Modern orthodontic procedures offer a variety of efficient choices for adult patients. Traditional braces are among the most effective methods, particularly in complicated cases. They employ controlled pressure to slowly move teeth into the right place. Clear aligners are a commonly employed option, particularly for moderate to mild issues. The removable trays are developed by using digital scans. They are then replace every few weeks to control tooth movement. The typical time for wearing aligners is around 20 to 22 hours per day. They allow for a variety of eating options and dental hygiene.

Another significant development is the development of custom treatment plans. Orthodontists are now relying on 3D models and digital imaging to determine the movement of teeth before treatment starts. This increases accuracy and decreases the chance of delays. Each plan is customized to the patient's specific dental structure and lifestyle as well as long-term goals, which means more predictability in the results.

In the process of planning treatment, Adult Orthodontics Rochester Hills insists on the durability and stability. The objective isn't just to straighten teeth, but also to ensure that results are durable throughout the course of time. Bite correction plays an essential part during this procedure. A properly aligned bite can reduce pressure on the jaw joints. This can help avoid issues like headaches, jaw pain and wear on enamel.

Retention is the most crucial step that will ensure long-term achievement. Following therapy, retainers can be utilized to ensure the position of the teeth. Teeth are naturally inclined to shift back when retention isn't taken care of. Orthodontists generally recommend regular retainer usage, particularly in the first year following treatment. This protects the outcomes and ensures that the smile stays in good shape for many years.

Adults usually opt for orthodontic treatment, not just for aesthetics, but also for health advantages. Straight teeth are simpler to keep clean, which decreases plaque buildup and decreases the chance of developing cavities and gum disease. A better alignment can also aid in eating and speech, which enhances the overall function of your mouth. The benefits of orthodontics make it more of a long-term investment than a quick cosmetic choice.

Lifestyle compatibility is an additional aspect. Modern orthodontic treatments are specifically designed to integrate into your daily routine. Clear aligners, less appointments to the clinic, and electronic monitoring tools enable adults to handle treatment in conjunction with the demands of work and personal commitments. This flexibility has eliminated many of the obstacles that stopped adults from seeking orthodontic treatment.

The demand for orthodontics for adults is growing as the public's awareness grows. Many people who did not receive treatment in the past or who had a relapse from prior treatment are now opting to improve their smile. Orthodontic treatment is also a complement to various dental treatments by aligning the teeth prior to restoration work, thereby improving overall results.

In the end, [Adult Orthodontics Rochester Hills](https://www.myamazingsmile.com/) offers effective and lasting solutions to improve the appearance and function of your teeth. With the latest technology, customized treatment plans and a concentration on retention, patients can enjoy results that are constant throughout time. The orthodontic treatment of 2026 has been intended to provide long-term benefits, which makes it an ideal step to improved dental wellbeing and self-confidence.

title.title: STREET ART #248 – Beautiful portrait in Aarhus, Denmark
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQvLYjmmwf3gkGNDjZEEHYgPpZ7z4gda19xV3DtS9Uz1P/01.jpg)
This beautiful portrait is found in the city center of Aarhus, one of the larger cities in Denmark. The title « Beautiful Age» is painted by artist Hendrik Beikirch. As I don't know the artist from before, I had to look for information and found out that he is a based in Germany. I did quess he might be German because of the name... I found out that he paints beautiful black and white portraits. Seems he has done lots of work around the world, but I haven't come across work done by him before this work in Aarhus.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmf3nZddKpTVANPKaHNus9J2QFUp8KmvKgzhbNYbMa6zXD/02.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmZmtjeeZLKUXocfXceHVAVu4MLWDuAmjCmgqgXY7E3Wo5/03.jpg https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ3WCiZ8vXB4uW2zsE6ohrDKUSa3peBgVGE3tEi5KTgTb/04.jpg
His black and white work does make a powerful inpression. His portraits certainly have personalities and expression of emotions. His portraits are just as eye-catching as those in colors. His portraits are not just subjects. They have character that I think comes out much more strongly when he uses nothing but black and white and not the full color palette. Impressive work. Check the link for more portraits and an article about Beikirch. Henrick Beikirch : https://magazine-art-mag.fr/en/henrick-beikirch-masters-of-monumental-frescoes/

title.title: Delhi to Dehradun Road Trip- A Perfect Weekend Escape to the Hills
title.body:
![Delhi to Dehradun Trip on New EXPRESSWAY.jpg.jpeg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/58f886de7dbbe0c2c9b561f99393f535c562f451ea70a3136eab40e307671115)



Planning a quick getaway from Delhi? A road trip to Dehradun is one of the best options for a refreshing weekend escape. Nestled in the foothills of the Himalayas, Dehradun offers scenic beauty, pleasant weather, and a peaceful environment away from city life.

The journey from Delhi to Dehradun covers around 240 to 250 kilometers and usually takes about 5 to 6 hours by road, making it ideal for a short trip. As you leave behind the busy streets of Delhi, the drive becomes more enjoyable with green fields, roadside cafes, and beautiful views along the route.

This road trip is not just about reaching the destination- it’s about enjoying every moment of the journey. You can take short breaks, enjoy local food, and feel the refreshing change in weather as you move closer to the hills.

Whether you are traveling with family, friends, or colleagues, this trip offers the perfect mix of comfort and relaxation. A [Delhi to Dehradun road trip](https://www.tempotravellerrentindelhi.com/blog/delhi-to-dehradun-trip/) is a simple yet memorable way to enjoy nature and spend a peaceful weekend in the mountains.

title.title: Is religion needed for salvation// The old path bible review
title.body:
Salvation is a free gift which we get from God for being good and obeying his Commandments. Salvation come to us because of the grace of God and the faith which we have in him. This means that no amount of external religious activity can replace a genuine relationship with God.
https://youtu.be/7U91Nn7ahqI?si=DgN_rCuRqUvbuBLf
Religion is not the major foundation of salvation from God, but religion helps us to seek the face of God which we can easily gain salvation. The Bible often warns against relying only on outward religion while the heart remains unchanged. Jesus criticized religious leaders who followed rules but lacked true faith and love, showing that religion without sincerity is empty.

However, true faith often expresses itself through actions that may look religious, such as prayer, worship, and fellowship. These practices are not the means of salvation but are evidence of a transformed life. They help believers grow spiritually and stay connected to God and others who share the same faith.

title.title: Roasted Sweet Potatoes with Palm Sugar Glaze
title.body:
> ![20260417_123544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/Eoc9uk4q9cUnv6NnTBY28rZncDHpfcFS3XQMqNRdePyr5mPei2HTr43b3W7bsEXDNPN.jpg)
Hello, vegan lovers! hidangannblvegan always brings a fresh twist to every unique flavor. The deliciousness of a simple dish gives me an unusual new sensation. It might sound simple, but when you taste it, this is truly a heavenly snack.
![20260417_123538.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23uFbyCUzsTvwrAt7DKh3VYEXz3PE3LgAbiovG4v7zxMGHw7VqR2KfNUKAvpQ1G1EFgcC.jpg) Roasted sweet potatoes topped with a generous sprinkle of coconut sugar—a simple combination that results in a luxurious dish. The idea for this dish came to me when I was craving something roasted. So I decided to try roasting sweet potatoes; usually, when I enjoy roasted sweet potatoes, I use a special variety called \

But this time, I turned regular sweet potatoes into a delicious treat with melted palm sugar. The generous topping makes this dish look absolutely amazing.
Ingredients
![20260417_091424.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EpQyH7BZ7VMMmufFZCqRqo1XLmyzLA7xYUZ96Fxbei7vUEMW5QXbhVh9YvcGQhT9cKN.jpg)
4 sweet potatoes 1 tablespoon palm sugar 1 tablespoon sesame seeds 1 tablespoon peanuts
Instructions
Wash the sweet potatoes thoroughly and scrub them first, since we’ll be baking them with the skin on, then slice them thinly—about half a centimeter thick.

> ![20260417_092142.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23z7QCwKd7KcpWvjFzshSftNSjmqLi3AQvPrL163Re3Dq3w1XGu2qAoyZPhUnQ4qzuGs2.jpg)
Next, arrange them on a baking sheet and bake in an oven at 180 degrees Celsius using top and bottom heat for about 2 hours. If you want them to cook faster, you can parboil them until half-done first, though the texture will be slightly different.

> ![20260417_092729.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqpjCaanwMwyDFv8YGwaQpMb4bWdB7KS4WXNux8meRbinkgKa4cYwJMkJwTseT1urMk.jpg) ![20260417_100447.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tmYTZLa59UoXmq9pVjHQVCDzABdiMRS1L2mmrapQ3ZBZggYxfuGnvxb23gaCiNCB727.jpg)
Once they’re partially baked, sprinkle them with powdered palm sugar, then top with roasted peanuts and sesame seeds, and bake again until fully cooked.

> ![20260417_111012.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23x1FAawsGGbrMhyVGdvHsgm6ixPMvLNM5teW9yDvU8YtrenSzqmQjDrPxe2JY7bfbT4Z.jpg)
Result
![20260417_123628.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EoErxM3JCGwctxbVBwTgGjs9GF5FpNqWhh9SPv22MTuMCwXQVSGL7USGkD5MsG9MKF6.jpg) These ready-to-serve roasted sweet potatoes make a perfect healthy family snack to enjoy during the rainy season—best served warm. They’re incredibly tender and cooked evenly, even though they take quite a while to prepare, but I’m very satisfied with the result.
|![20260417_123613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23zbae1YEbYf7gwtjNxj9sLFH7ickSZMQ7f5nwMHunFBszDQaPUMHkm48zheXoLhQzV6C.jpg)|![20260417_123609.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xAnWivXuuxmBcyWEngRSZscqMZ64o57hNjGFM1yyUjhd3xjFGctVRXkf11CfSfMd8V1.jpg)|![20260417_123657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xyk2aLzaqShYSMzW58k2uaVQpi6Q6DzsHnbDz7RP7GAAx11hK9GMir5tF5fDzF2WdjA.jpg)| |-|-|-|
The flavor is savory-sweet with a rich aroma of sesame and palm sugar. The combination of ingredients is just right—I’m sure anyone who tries this will want to make it again because it’s truly delicious, especially for those of you trying to cut back on oily foods; these sweet potatoes will be the perfect solution, in my opinion. ![20260417_123602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23viCmaNtpMGrfK84UtSXMUS9fNi45vfoQ5XG8hKuJgyL5XBEQWDJPWyWQfr7wT3pc1ca.jpg)
![20230813_094117_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23ynhM4HY26LsJBc56VnzHwHASWwNh2k6eRFsTW3ZB37BNXHsDPbYNJn7HniS1Ky4w7Ki.png)

> ![20240420_153413.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xybJaDM9iJEac2d34ghVhwHTLJQ2LkMrCFUTk1gbXyPNb8JzZk9mvDrrsvBt1wnEFYU.jpg)

Welcome to this blog, I have a real name \

, who comes from Indonesia. I have several hobbies, reading, writing, gardening, I also love food and cooking, even art related.  And the most interesting one is spending the whole day traveling. title.title: Something Off
title.body:
I saw the message before anyone else reacted.
It was dropped in the group casually.
Short. Direct.
A decision had been made.

I read it once.
Then again.
Something didn’t add up.

The numbers looked fine at first glance. Clean. Well arranged.
But one part didn’t sit right.
I checked it again.
Still the same.

I scrolled up, trying to connect it with what had been discussed earlier.
That’s when it became clearer.

It wasn’t wrong enough to be obvious.
Just off enough to matter later.
Replies started coming in.

“Looks good.”
“Let’s move.”
“Approved.”

I watched the confirmations stack up.
For a moment, I almost typed the same.
Just to keep things moving.

But I didn’t.
I pointed out the part that didn’t align.
There was a pause.

Then a reply.
Not to the issue.
Just a repeat of the original message.

I read it again.
Same numbers. Same confidence.
I left it there.

Didn’t argue. Didn’t push.
Just stepped back.
Later, the correction came.
Quietly.

No announcement. No explanation.
Just an updated version.
The same part I noticed had changed.

Everything moved on like nothing happened.
But I knew exactly when it shifted. 

This story is fictional and written to share a life lesson

title.title: Cien años de soledad. El libro que marcó mi vida/One Hundred Years of Solitude. The book that changed my life
title.body: Buen día comunidad de @hiveargentina. Cuando leí la propuesta, aparecieron en mi mente muchos libros de mi adolescencia. Sin embargo, decidí quedarme con Cien años de soledad de Gabriel García Márquez. Aunque ya pasó mucho tiempo y no recuerdo todos los detalles (lo que me hace pensar que debería volver a leerlo), hay una escena que quedó grabada a fuego en mí. En ese momento de mi vida estaba muy involucrada con la música: tocaba en dos orquestas y cantaba en un coro. Tenía ensayos casi todos los días y conciertos todos los fines de semana. Era algo que amaba profundamente, pero también aprendí que duele cuando el trabajo no es valorado. Recuerdo especialmente un concierto en un acto político. Venía el intendente —quien pagaba nuestro sueldo— a hacer su típica campaña, y nosotros debíamos tocar antes de su discurso. Todo parecía normal al principio. El director dio la señal y comenzamos. A lo lejos ya se escuchaba la muchedumbre acercándose con sus cantos y bombos. Cada vez sonaban más fuerte, completamente fuera de tiempo con nuestra música. Empezamos a mirarnos entre nosotros, sin saber si reír o llorar. Se abrieron las puertas del hall. El intendente nos escuchó, literalmente, unos veinte segundos… y siguió avanzando. En ese instante, los bombos —que habían parado— volvieron a sonar por encima de nosotros. Cruzó la siguiente puerta rumbo a su discurso. El director bajó la batuta y dijo simplemente: “Nos vamos”. Y todos estuvimos de acuerdo. Indignada, llegué a casa y le conté a mi mamá lo sucedido. Ella solo dijo: “Cien años de soledad”. —¿Qué? —le respondí. Conseguí el libro y lo leí. Y ahí, en medio de tragedias, absurdos y situaciones increíbles, encontré algo muy familiar: lo mismo que nos había pasado a nosotros. Otro país, otro contexto… pero la misma sensación.Ahí entendí lo que mi mamá quiso decirme: el mundo está lleno de esas repeticiones. Cambian los escenarios, pero las historias —y las personas— muchas veces no tanto. Hay de todo, para todos los estilos. Respondiendo a las demás preguntas mi genero favorito es de suspenso o policiales, aunque Garcia Marquez siempre me gustó mucho aunque no tuviera nada de eso. Siempre lei mucho de Agatha Christie y Mary Higgins Clark, ahora me modernice un poco y estoy leyendo a Anne Perry. Los día en que se festeja el día del libro, me gustaba o mejor dicho solia ir a las ferias del libro desde chica y luego cuando fui mama lleve siempre a mis hijas, una de mis hijas es muy lectora pero no de suspenso sino de ciencia ficcion. Nunca conocí personalmente a un escritor, al menos no he hablado cara a cara con él. Invito a participar de la iniciativa a @borjan y a @marcosalomao95 . Bueno espero que hayan disfrutado de mis palabras tanto como yo al recordarlas😂, nos estamos viendo.

/> * * * * * * Good morning, @hiveargentina community. When I read the prompt, many books from my teenage years came to mind. However, I decided to go with _One Hundred Years of Solitude_ by Gabriel García Márquez. Although it’s been a long time and I don’t remember all the details (which makes me think I should reread it), there’s one scene that’s burned itself into my memory. At that point in my life, I was deeply involved in music: I played in two orchestras and sang in a choir. I had rehearsals almost every day and concerts every weekend. It was something I loved deeply, but I also learned that it hurts when your work isn’t appreciated. I especially remember a concert at a political event. The mayor—who paid our salaries—was coming to do his usual campaign routine, and we were supposed to play before his speech. Everything seemed normal at first. The conductor gave the signal, and we began. In the distance, we could already hear the crowd approaching with their chants and drums. They grew louder and louder, completely out of sync with our music. We started looking at each other, not knowing whether to laugh or cry. The doors to the hall opened. The mayor listened to us—literally—for about twenty seconds… and kept walking. At that moment, the drums—which had stopped—began to sound again, drowning us out. He walked through the next door on his way to his speech. The conductor lowered his baton and simply said, “Let’s go.” And we all agreed. Outraged, I went home and told my mom what had happened. She just said, “One Hundred Years of Solitude.” “What?” I replied. I got the book and read it. And there, amid tragedies, absurdities, and unbelievable situations, I found something very familiar: the same thing that had happened to us. Another country, another context… but the same feeling. That’s when I understood what my mom meant: the world is full of those repetitions. The settings change, but the stories—and the people—often don’t change that much. There’s something for everyone, for every taste. To answer your questions, my favorite genres are thrillers and mysteries, although I’ve always really liked García Márquez even though his work isn’t like that at all. I used to read a lot of Agatha Christie and Mary Higgins Clark, but now I’ve branched out a bit and am reading Anne Perry. On Book Day, I used to love—or rather, I used to go to book fairs ever since I was a girl, and then when I became a mom, I always took my daughters. One of my daughters is a voracious reader, but not of thrillers—she prefers science fiction. Well, I hope you’ve enjoyed my words as much as I’ve enjoyed remembering them. See you soon.

title.title: Cats, cats and cats part 1 [Eng/Esp]
title.body:
Hello Hivers! How have you been? I'll start today with more cat photos jjj. Right now my life revolves around cats. Be it my two cats and other stray cats that seek shelter in my house. I have given them all names: Rabbit Cat, One-Eyed Cat, Cow, Blonde and many more. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbouCz4wemYBovvwVqwLqxLB5TZTDRL7d9JTKNtoZw9Ff/1776591588092.jpg) In addition to cats I also carry bones and cooked rice with me for stray dogs that I may find along the way. As long as my cats don't find out because they are very jealous. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVpyWL466un8UzbFYgTyWtY7AepuQJPRNuEGvAB1HEWyk/1776591769834.jpg) I would like Maneki and Mikan not to fight with other cats but I find it difficult for them not to fight. The other night Mikan came home around 11 Pm covered in dirt and with a lack of hair on his head, apparently he came from a cat fight 😱. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX72F2c3pnX35Lc2qV1o9a6sVLyfoAZJw3bS6mxNW7Hg3/1776591859608.jpg) The funniest thing is that they always fight with cats much bigger than them, although I never really know who won the fight hahaha. I still feed every stray cat I can. Poor animals are not to blame for the irresponsibility of their former owners. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPFyRsXUDsScFc7VAyqfShqHZCidkMX12gAweSwoiy47E/1776591913825.jpg) Since I was little, some of my neighbors dedicated themselves to hunting cats for food, something that I have always hated. A few years ago I lost a cat to people like that 😐. Nowadays they have stopped eating cats and dogs luckily 🙏. Now they are dedicated to hunting vultures to eat, poor birds have had a difficult time this year. 🌙 🐝 ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmScnTutgHv23h2ofzbM81eGW9XpKKWsMAGHKEPUCPcDw3/1776591992423.jpg)

Hola Hivers! Como han estado? Empezaré el dia de hoy con más fotos de gatos jjj. Ahora mismo mi vida gira alrededor de los gatos. Ya sea mis dos gatos y otros gatos callejeros que buscan refugio en mi casa. A todos les he dado nombre: Gato conejo, Gato tuerto, Vaquita, Rubio y muchos más. Además de gatos también llevo conmigo huesos y arroz cocido para perritos callejeros que pueda encontrar en el camino. Siempre que mis gatos no se enteren porque son muy celosos. Mw gustaria que Maneki y Mikan no se fajaran con otros gatos pero me resulta dificil que no se peleen. La otra noche Mikan llegó a casa sobre las 11 Pm cubierto de tierra y con falta de pelo en su cabeza, al parecer llegó de una pelea gatuna 😱. Lo mas chistoso es que siempre se pelean con gatos mucho mas grande que ellos, aunque realmente nunca sé quien ganó la pelea jajaja. Yo igual le doy alimento a cada gato callejero que pueda. Pobres animales no tienen la culpa de las inresponsabilidades de sus antiguos dueños. Desde que era pequeña unos vecinos mio se dedicaban a cazar gatos para comer, algo que siempre he detestado. Hace unos años atrás perdi un gato por personas como esa 😐. Hoy en dia han dejado de comer gatos y perros por suerte 🙏. Ahora se dedican a cazar Aura tiñozas para comer, pobres aves les ha tocado dificil este año. 🌙 🐝
